records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that Umar, ؓ, passed a man who was performing prostrations one after another. Umar disapproved of this or forbade him. Abu Hanifah said: “This has reached me from the Prophet, ﷺ.”
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ «عُمَرَ رضي الله عنه مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ يُتَابِعُ بَيْنَ السُّجُودِ، فَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ أَوْ نَهَاهُ» . وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي ذَلِكَ ⦗ص: 35⦘ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that Umar, ؓ, passed by a man who was hurrying between prostrations, so he disliked that or forbade him. Abu Hanifah said It has reached me from the Prophet, ﷺ, the same.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that a man passed by Abu Dharr (ؓ) while he was praying a brief, light prayer, frequently bowing and prostrating. When he finished, the man said to him, "You are a companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), yet you pray this prayer?" Abu Dharr replied, "Did I not complete the bowing and prostration?" The man said, "Yes." Abu Dharr said, "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever prostrates to God in a prostration, God raises him a degree in Paradise by it.' So I loved to be raised in degrees or to have degrees written for me."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا مَرَّ بِأَبِي ذَرٍّ رضي الله عنه وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي صَلَاةً وَجِيزَةً خَفِيفَةً يُكْثِرُ الرُّكُوعَ وَالسُّجُودَ، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ قَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ: أَنْتَ صَاحِبُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَتُصَلِّي هَذِهِ الصَّلَاةَ؟ فَقَالَ: أَلَمْ أُتِمَّ الرُّكُوعَ وَالسُّجُودَ؟ قَالَ: بَلَى. قَالَ: فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: «مَنْ سَجَدَ لِلَّهِ سَجْدَةً رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ بِهَا دَرَجَةً فِي الْجَنَّةِ، فَأَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ أُرْفَعَ دَرَجَاتٍ، أَوْ تُكْتَبَ لِي دَرَجَاتٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said regarding the woman experiencing istihadah: She leaves off prayer during the days of her menstrual cycle, then bathes when those days have passed. She bathes at the end of the time for Dhuhr and prays it, then prays Asr at the beginning of its time. Then she bathes at the end of the time for Maghrib and prays it, then prays Isha at the beginning of its time, and bathes for Fajr and prays it.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said who said: “The first time I sat with Ibn Abbas, ؓ, a letter came to him from a Qurashi woman: ‘I am experiencing irregular bleeding, and the blood does not stop.’ Sa‘id said: ‘I read it to him.’ He asked me, ‘Had you read it before?’ I said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘I was impressed by your reading of it, and that distracted me from understanding it. Read it to me again.’ I read it to him again. He then wrote to her: ‘Do not pray during the days of your usual menstrual period. When they have passed, perform ghusl, then perform ghusl for each prayer.’ Abu Hanifah said: ‘Hammad followed this view. I, however, hold that she should perform wudu for each prayer and not perform ghusl.’”
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ أَوَّلَ مَا جَالَسْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما، إِذْ جَاءَهُ كِتَابٌ مِنَ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ: إِنِّي قَدِ اسْتُحِضْتُ فَلَا يَنْقَطِعُ عَنِّي الدَّمُ. قَالَ سَعِيدٌ: فَقَرَأْتُهُ، فَقَالَ لِي: هَلْ قَرَأْتَهُ قَبْلَهَا؟ فَقُلْتُ: لَا. فَقَالَ: لَقَدْ أَعْجَبَتْنِي قِرَاءَتُكَ لَهُ، فَشَغَلَنِي ذَلِكَ عَنْ فَهْمِهِ. قَالَ: أَعِدْ عَلَيَّ. فَأَعَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ. قَالَ: فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهَا: «تَدَعُ الصَّلَاةَ فِي أَيَّامِ أَقْرَائِهَا، فَإِذَا مَضَتِ اغْتَسَلَتْ، ثُمَّ تَغْتَسِلُ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ» . قَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بِذَلِكَ كَانَ حَمَّادٌ يَأْخُذُ، وَأَمَّا أَنَا فَأَرَى أَنْ تَتَوَضَّأَ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ وَلَا تَغْتَسِلُ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said The first time I sat with Ibn Abbas, ؓ, a letter came to him from a woman of Quraysh saying: "I have begun menstruating and the blood does not cease from me." Sa'id said: I read it to him, so he asked me: "Had you read it before?" I said: "No." He said: "Your reading of it pleased me, and that distracted me from understanding it." He said: "Repeat it to me." So I repeated it to him. He then wrote to her: "Leave prayer during the days of your usual cycle, then when they pass, perform ghusl, and then perform ghusl for every prayer." Abu Hanifah said: Hammad used to adopt this position, but as for me, I hold that she should perform wudu for every prayer and not perform ghusl.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding the woman who becomes pure before the sun sets: "She makes up only the prayer whose time she became pure in."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Abu Wa’il, from Ibn Mas’ud, ؓ, who said When one of you is praying and does not know whether he has prayed three or four rak’ahs, let him seek what is most likely correct. If he is more certain that it was three, let him pray a fourth. If he is more certain that it was four, let him finish, prostrate twice for forgetfulness, recite the tashahhud, and give the salutation.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ يُصَلِّي، فَلَمْ يَدْرِ أَثَلَاثًا صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعًا، فَلْيَتَحَرَّ الصَّوَابَ، فَإِنْ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ رَأْيِهِ أَنَّهُ ثَلَاثٌ، فَلْيُصَلِّ إِلَيْهَا رَابِعَةً، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ رَأْيِهِ أَنَّهُ أَرْبَعٌ، فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ وَيَسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ وَيَتَشَهَّدْ وَيُسَلِّمْ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he would perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness in every voluntary or obligatory prayer. He said , "They rectify what has been corrupted in the prayer." And he would say, "Performing them when they are not obligatory upon me is more beloved to me than leaving them when they are obligatory upon me."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man doubts his ablution or his prayer, and this is the first time he has encountered such doubt, he should repeat the ablution and the prayer. But if he frequently encounters such doubt, he should proceed without repeating.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said regarding forgetfulness: "If you encounter that repeatedly, you should strive to determine what is correct, then act upon what you believe to be correct, and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ فِي السَّهْوِ: «إِذَا لَقِيتَ ذَلِكَ مِرَارًا تَحَرَّيْتَ الصَّوَابَ، ثُمَّ بَنَيْتَ عَلَى مَا تَرَى أَنَّهُ صَوَابٌ، وَسَجَدْتَ سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said who said: “If you forget something while praying behind the imam and the imam remembers correctly, there is no prostration of forgetfulness for you. If the imam forgets while you remember, then the prostration of forgetfulness is due from you. If the imam does not perform the prostration, do not perform it. The same applies if everyone praying with the imam forgets, or if the imam forgets.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا سَهَوْتَ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ، وَحَفِظَ الْإِمَامُ، فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ سَهْوٌ، وَإِنْ سَهَا وَحَفِظْتَ فَعَلَيْكَ السَّهْوُ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْجُدِ الْإِمَامُ فَلَا تَسْجُدْ، وَكَذَلِكَ إِذَا سَهَا جَمِيعُ مَنْ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ أَوْ سَهَا الْإِمَامُ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said If you make a mistake behind the imam while the imam remains correct, you bear no mistake. But if the imam makes a mistake while you remain correct, then you must perform the prostration of forgetfulness. If the imam does not prostrate, do not prostrate. Likewise, if all those with the imam make a mistake or if the imam alone makes a mistake.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said If the imam precedes you in something and then makes a mistake, prostrate with him. Then stand and complete what he preceded you in. If this occurs during the days of *Tashriq*, do not say the *takbir* until the prayer is completed, then say the *takbir* after you give the *salam*.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا سَبَقَكَ الْإِمَامُ بِشَيْءٍ وَقَدْ سَهَا فَاسْجُدْ مَعَهُ، ثُمَّ قُمْ فَاقْضِ مَا سَبَقَكَ بِهِ، وَإِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِي أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ فَلَا تُكَبِّرْ حَتَّى تُقْضَى الصَّلَاةُ، ثُمَّ تُكَبِّرُ بَعْدَ مَا تُسَلِّمُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said "There are three practices that people have introduced: giving salutations in the two prostrations of forgetfulness, giving salutations during the funeral prayer, and saying the takbir in the qunut of the Witr prayer."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding a man whose ablution is broken during prayer: “He should leave the prayer and perform ablution. If he speaks, he must start the prayer over; if he does not speak, he may count what he has already prayed and complete what remains.” Ibrahim added: “I prefer that he speak and start the prayer over.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرَّجُلِ يَسْبِقُهُ الْحَدَثُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ: إِنَّهُ «يَنْصَرِفُ فَيَتَوَضَّأُ، فَإِنْ تَكَلَّمَ اسْتَقْبَلَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمِ اعْتَدَّ بِمَا مَضَى، وَصَلَّى مَا بَقِيَ» . وَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: يَتَكَلَّمُ وَيَسْتَقْبِلُ ⦗ص: 38⦘ الصَّلَاةَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ

If he spoke, he must restart the prayer, but if he did not speak, he may count what has passed and pray what remains." Ibrahim also said: "Speaking and restarting the prayer is more beloved to me."

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf narrated to us from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr from Ma'bad ibn Subayh that a man from the Companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, broke his ablution while praying behind Uthman ibn Affan, ؓ. He left, performed ablution, and returned with his forearm uncovered, reciting: “And they did not persist in what they had done, knowingly” [Qur’an 3:135]. He then counted what he had already prayed and completed what remained.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ مَعْبَدِ بْنِ صُبَيْحٍ، " أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَحْدَثَ خَلْفَ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ رضي الله عنه فِي الصَّلَاةِ، فَانْفَتَلَ فَتَوَضَّأَ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ وَهُوَ حَاسِرٌ عَنْ ذِرَاعِهِ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: {وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ} [آل عمران: 135] ، فَاعْتَدَّ بِمَا مَضَى، وَصَلَّى مَا بَقِيَ "

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf narrated to us from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr from Ma'bad ibn Subayh that a man from the Companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, passed wind behind Uthman ibn Affan, ؓ, during prayer. He turned away, performed ablution, then returned with his forearm uncovered, saying: *"And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except God?—and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know."* He then resumed his prayer from where he had left off and completed what remained.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man sits for the duration of the tashahhud and then breaks wind, his prayer is complete.

records.isnad_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ
records.matn_ar: «إِذَا جَلَسَ الرَّجُلُ قَدْرَ التَّشَهُّدِ ثُمَّ أَحْدَثَ، فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُهُ»
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s ruling on sitting through the tashahhud before passing wind.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said to Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh, ؓ: When menstruation begins, leave the prayer, and when it ends, wash the blood from yourself and pray. This was when she complained to him, saying: "I experience irregular bleeding and do not become pure."
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِفَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ أَبِي حُبَيْشٍ رضي الله عنها: «إِذَا أَقْبَلَتِ الْحَيْضَةُ فَدَعِي الصَّلَاةَ، فَإِذَا أَدْبَرَتِ الْحَيْضَةُ فَاغْسِلِي عَنْكِ الدَّمَ وَصَلِّي» حِينَ شَكَتْ إِلَيْهِ: إِنِّي أُسْتَحَاضُ فَلَا أَطْهُرُ

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated: Abu Yusuf said Abu Hanifah narrated to me from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, ؓ, “When your menstrual days have passed, perform ghusl and perform wudu for every prayer.” Yusuf followed this view. Through his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, it is reported that Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, said: “Satan moves through a person as blood moves through the veins. When one of you prostrates, Satan comes and blows at his backside to make him think he has broken his ablution. If one of you senses something of that, let him not leave until he hears a sound or detects an odor.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو يُوسُفَ: وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها مِثْلَهُ، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا ذَهَبَ أَيَّامُ حَيْضِكِ، فَاغْتَسِلِي وَتَوَضَّئِي لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ» . وَبِهِ كَانَ يَأْخُذُ يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَجْرِي فِي الْإِنْسَانِ مَجْرَى الدَّمِ فِي الْعُرُوقِ، فَإِذَا سَجَدَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَتَاهُ فَنَفَخَ فِي دُبُرِهِ لِيُرِيَهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَحْدَثَ، فَإِذَا أَحَسَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يَنْصَرِفْ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ صَوْتًا أَوْ يَجِدَ رِيحًا»
records.raw_text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو يُوسُفَ: وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها مِثْلَهُ، غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا ذَهَبَ أَيَّامُ حَيْضِكِ، فَاغْتَسِلِي وَتَوَضَّئِي لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ» . وَبِهِ كَانَ يَأْخُذُ يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَجْرِي فِي الْإِنْسَانِ مَجْرَى الدَّمِ فِي الْعُرُوقِ، فَإِذَا سَجَدَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَتَاهُ فَنَفَخَ فِي دُبُرِهِ لِيُرِيَهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَحْدَثَ، فَإِذَا أَحَسَّ أَحَدُكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يَنْصَرِفْ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ صَوْتًا أَوْ يَجِدَ رِيحًا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated: Abu Yusuf said Abu Hanifah narrated to me from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, ؓ, similarly, except that he said: "When the days of your menstruation have passed, perform ghusl and perform wudu for every prayer." And this was his practice. Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, said Satan flows through man like blood flows in the veins. When one of you prostrates, he comes and blows into his backside to make him think he has passed wind. If one of you feels something of that, let him not turn away until he hears a sound or smells an odor.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man sits for the duration of the tashahhud, his prayer is complete.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding a man who speaks before the salutation or laughs aloud: if he has sat for the duration of the tashahhud, his prayer is invalid.

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah narrated from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said who said: “If I were to say, ‘I saw Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, prostrating during Idha al-Sama’ Unshaqqat (Surah al-Inshiqaq),’ I would be telling the truth. What I know for certain is that one of them did.”

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he "would not prostrate in *Sad* nor would he prostrate in Surah al-Hajj except in the first one."

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Abd al-Karim, who raised the hadith to the Prophet, ﷺ, that he prostrated in *Sad*.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he was with Alqamah in a litter. He recited the Quran, and when he reached the prostration, he wanted to jump down. So he said , "O nephew, a gesture is sufficient for you."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ مَعَ عَلْقَمَةَ فِي مَحْمَلٍ، فَقَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ، فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ السَّجْدَةَ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَثِبَ، فَقَالَ «ابْنَ أَخِي، الْإِيمَاءُ يُجْزِئُكَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf, from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the man who prays on an upper level of the mosque with the imam below, or who prays alone in the row: regarding the man who prays above the mosque with the imam while the imam is below, or prays alone in the row: "That suffices for him."
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَوْقَ الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ، وَالْإِمَامُ فِي أَسْفَلَ، أَوْ يُصَلِّي فِي الصَّفِّ وَحْدَهُ: إِنَّهُ «يُجْزِئُهُ ذَلِكَ»
records.raw_text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَوْقَ الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ، وَالْإِمَامُ فِي أَسْفَلَ، أَوْ يُصَلِّي فِي الصَّفِّ وَحْدَهُ: إِنَّهُ «يُجْزِئُهُ ذَلِكَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud from Abu Razin from Ibn Masud, ؓ, that he caught a louse while in the mosque, buried it in the gravel, and recited: *"Have We not made the earth a container for the living and the dead?"*
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النَّجُودِ، عَنْ ⦗ص: 41⦘ أَبِي رَزِينٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه " أَنَّهُ أَخَذَ قَمْلَةً وَهُوَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، فَدَفَنَهَا فِي الْحَصَى، وَقَرَأَ: {أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا} [المرسلات: 26]

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: “People used to perform five tarwīḥāt (rest periods) in Ramadan.”

records.matn_en: that she used to lead women in voluntary prayers during Ramadan, standing in the middle of the row.
records.isnad_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها
records.matn_ar: «أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَؤُمُّ النِّسَاءَ فِي رَمَضَانَ تَطَوُّعًا، وَتَقُومُ فِي وَسَطِ الصَّفِّ»
records.boundary_review_note: Aisha leading women in voluntary prayer.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from someone who narrated to him from the Prophet, ﷺ, that when Ramadan began, he would pray and fast. When the last ten days came, he would gird himself for worship and spend the night in worship.
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ «كَانَ إِذَا دَخَلَ رَمَضَانَ صَلَّى وَصَامَ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ الْعَشْرُ الْأَوَاخِرُ شَدَّ الْمِئْزَرَ، وَأَحْيَا اللَّيْلَ»
records.raw_text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ «كَانَ إِذَا دَخَلَ رَمَضَانَ صَلَّى وَصَامَ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ الْعَشْرُ الْأَوَاخِرُ شَدَّ الْمِئْزَرَ، وَأَحْيَا اللَّيْلَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from someone who narrated to him from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he would pray and fast when Ramadan entered. Then, when the last ten days came, he would tighten his waist-wrapper, and stay awake at night.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ «كَانَ إِذَا دَخَلَ رَمَضَانَ صَلَّى وَصَامَ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ الْعَشْرُ الْأَوَاخِرُ شَدَّ الْمِئْزَرَ، وَأَحْيَا اللَّيْلَ»
records.boundary_review_note: Unnamed transmitter between al-Haytham and Prophet.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from Dhakwan—who said , "As I recall, from Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, and I do not doubt that he said: 'Whoever says, *I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He has created*, three times in the morning, no scorpion will harm him until the evening. And if he says it in the evening, no scorpion will harm him until the morning.'"
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ ذَكْوَانَ، قَالَ فِيمَا أَحْسِبُ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَا أَشُكُّ فِيهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " مَنْ قَالَ: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ، حِينَ يُصْبِحُ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، لَمْ تَضُرَّهُ عَقْرَبٌ حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ، أَوْ حِينَ يُمْسِي لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ عَقْرَبٌ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ "

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah reported from Abd al-Karim, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said Whoever, upon finishing the Fajr prayer before moving from his place, says: "There is no god but God, alone without partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, He gives life and causes death, and He is ever-living and never dies, in His hand is all good, and He has power over all things," ten times—ten good deeds will be recorded for him, ten sins will be erased from him, and ten degrees will be raised for him. He will be under God’s protection until evening. Whoever says it upon finishing the Maghrib prayer before moving from his place will receive the same.
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 42⦘ أَنَّهُ قَالَ " مَنْ قَالَ حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ مِنْ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَأَخَّرَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ، بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ؛ كُتِبَتْ لَهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ حَسَنَاتٍ، وَمُحِيَ عَنْهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ سَيِّئَاتٍ، وَرُفِعَ لَهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ دَرَجَاتٍ، وَكَانَ فِي جِوَارِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ، وَمَنْ قَالَهَا حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَحَرَّكَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ؛ كَانَ لَهُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ "
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 42⦘ أَنَّهُ قَالَ " مَنْ قَالَ حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ مِنْ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَأَخَّرَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ، بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ؛ كُتِبَتْ لَهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ حَسَنَاتٍ، وَمُحِيَ عَنْهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ سَيِّئَاتٍ، وَرُفِعَ لَهُ بِهَا عَشْرُ دَرَجَاتٍ، وَكَانَ فِي جِوَارِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ، وَمَنْ قَالَهَا حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَحَرَّكَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ؛ كَانَ لَهُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ "

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from an elder who said Whoever says, *"So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning"* [Ar-Rum: 17] to the end of the verse three times in the morning, nothing that happens in his day will overtake him. And whoever says it in the evening, nothing that happens in his night will overtake him.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, who said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, passed by Umm Salamah while she was glorifying God with her date stones. He stood beside her briefly, then said: “I have said words that outweigh what you have said.” He then told her that he had said: “Glory be to God as many times as His creatures; glory be to God, as heavy as His Throne; glory be to God, as much as the ink of His words.”

records.raw_text_en: It reached Abu Hanifah from his father that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, passed by Umm Salamah while she was glorifying God with her date-stone beads. records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that Abu Bakr and Umar sat with the Prophet, ﷺ, one night. They left, and he went out with them. They passed by Ibn Mas'ud while he was reciting, so the Prophet, ﷺ, said "Whoever wishes to recite the Quran as fresh as it was revealed, let him recite according to the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd." And he kept saying to him: "Ask, and you shall be given." Then Abu Bakr and Umar, ؓ, came to him to give him the good news. records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, A man was reciting to Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, and he was non-Arab. He began saying, *"Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinner,"* but the man kept saying, *"the food of the orphan."* Ibn Mas‘ud corrected him, yet every time he still said , *"the food of the orphan."* So Ibn Mas‘ud said, "Say, *'the food of the wicked.'"* Then Ibn Mas‘ud said, "The mistake in the Quran is not saying, *'the Forgiving, the Merciful, the Mighty, the Wise.'* Rather, the mistake is reciting a verse of mercy as a verse of punishment, or a verse of punishment as a verse of mercy, and adding to the Book of God what is not in it."

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he recited the entire Quran in the Ka'bah in one unit of prayer, and in the second unit with "Say: He is God, the One."
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، «أَنَّهُ قَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ فِي الْكَعْبَةِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، وَفِي الثَّانِيَةِ بِقُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»
records.raw_text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، «أَنَّهُ قَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ فِي الْكَعْبَةِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، وَفِي الثَّانِيَةِ بِقُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, used to say: "Beautify the Quran with your voices."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ⦗ص: 45⦘ رضي الله عنه كَانَ يَقُولُ: «حَسِّنُوا الْقُرْآنَ بِأَصْوَاتِكُمْ»

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he said "Recite, O so-and-so, recite *al-Hijr*." The man said: "Is it not with you?" He replied: "Not with a voice like yours."

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the wives of the Prophet, ﷺ, gathered one night to Abu Musa, ؓ, while he was praying. When morning came, they said to him: "O Abu Musa, how beautiful your voice was last night!" He said: "Had I known, I would have embellished it even more."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ أَزْوَاجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اجْتَمَعْنَ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى رضي الله عنه ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ قُلْنَ لَهُ: يَا أَبَا مُوسَى، مَا كَانَ أَحْسَنَ صَوْتَكَ الْبَارِحَةَ فَقَالَ «لَوْ عَلِمْتُ لَحَبَّرْتُهُ تَحْبِيرًا»

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab led them in the dawn prayer at Mina and recited to them: "By the fig and the olive" and "Say, O disbelievers."

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham—as we suppose—from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, ؓ, that he led the people in prayer the day Umar, ؓ, was stabbed, and he recited: *When the victory of God has come and the conquest, and say: He is God, the One.*
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، فِيمَا نَحْسَبُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ رضي الله عنه " أَنَّهُ أَمَّ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ طُعِنَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه، فَقَرَأَ: إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ وَقُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ "

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said When you place the east to your left and the west to your right, then what lies between them is the direction of prayer.
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا جَعَلْتَ الْمَشْرِقَ عَنْ يَسَارِكَ، وَالْمَغْرِبَ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ، فَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا قِبْلَةٌ»

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Aisha, ؓ, who said "O people of Iraq, you have compared us to donkeys, dogs, and cats. Nothing interrupts the prayer, but ward off from yourself what you can."

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding a man who prays while a woman prays to his right, to his left, or directly beside him: “He must repeat the prayer. If the distance between them is at least the length of the rear of a saddle, that suffices him.”

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, and Hudhayfah, ؓ, and some of the Prophet's companions, ﷺ, were all together when the prayer was established. They began saying, "Go forward, so-and-so, go forward, so-and-so." So Ibn Mas'ud led them in prayer, praying a light and brief prayer, completing the prostrations and bowings. When he finished, the people said , "Abu Abd al-Rahman has preserved the prayer of the Messenger of God, ﷺ."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، وَأَبَا مُوسَى، وَحُذَيْفَةَ رضي الله عنهم، وَأُنَاسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا جَمِيعًا، فَأُقِيمَتِ الصَّلَاةُ، فَجَعَلُوا يَقُولُونَ: «تَقَدَّمْ يَا فُلَانُ، تَقَدَّمْ يَا فُلَانُ» ، فَأَمَّهُمُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ صَلَاةً خَفِيفَةً وَجِيزَةً، وَتَمَّمَ السُّجُودَ وَالرُّكُوعَ، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ قَالَ الْقَوْمُ: «قَدْ حَفِظَ أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ صَلَاةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، وَأَبَا مُوسَى، وَحُذَيْفَةَ رضي الله عنهم، وَأُنَاسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا جَمِيعًا، فَأُقِيمَتِ الصَّلَاةُ، فَجَعَلُوا يَقُولُونَ: «تَقَدَّمْ يَا فُلَانُ، تَقَدَّمْ يَا فُلَانُ» ، فَأَمَّهُمُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ صَلَاةً خَفِيفَةً وَجِيزَةً، وَتَمَّمَ السُّجُودَ وَالرُّكُوعَ، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ قَالَ الْقَوْمُ: «قَدْ حَفِظَ أَبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ صَلَاةَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم»
records.boundary_review_note: Matn reports the group choosing Ibn Masʿud to lead and praising his prayer.

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding those who recite no more than a verse or so of the Qur’an: “A man is in a state of major ritual impurity; a man is having intercourse; and a man is in the bathhouse.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad... When they turned away from the prayer, they turned to the right side. He said What is the matter with one of you that he turns around like the turning of a donkey? When he gives the salutation to his right and left, let him turn away however he faces. When he gives the salutation to his right and left, he has finished.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he was informed that some people, when they prayed the two rak'ahs of Fajr, would lie down. He said "Why does one of you roll around like a donkey rolls?"

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who reported: A group of the Prophet’s Companions were praying when a man arrived on his camel. He tethered it and joined the prayer, but the camel broke loose and went off. When the man saw what had happened, he prayed in a corner of the mosque, then went after his camel. This was reported to the Prophet, ﷺ, and he said: “Do not drive people away; be welcoming and bring people together, and do not repel them.”
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ قَوْمًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم صَلَّوْا، فَانْتَهَى إِلَيْهِمْ رَجُلٌ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ لَهُ، فَعَقَلَهُ وَدَخَلَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، فَانْبَعَثَ الْبَعِيرُ فَذَهَبَ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ صَلَّى فِي نَاحِيَةِ الْمَسْجِدِ، ثُمَّ لَحِقَ بَعِيرَهُ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ «لَا تُنَفِّرُوا، وَكُونُوا مُؤَلِّفِينَ، وَلَا تَكُونُوا مُنَفِّرِينَ» .

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he was asked, and he said "We were not commanded with..." (the rest is incomplete).

records.display_text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who reported: A group of the Prophet’s Companions were praying when a man arrived on his camel. He tethered it and joined the prayer, but the camel broke loose and went off. When the man saw what had happened, he prayed in a corner of the mosque, then went after his camel. This was reported to the Prophet, ﷺ, and he said: “Do not drive people away; be welcoming and bring people together, and do not repel them.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim that Ibn Mas'udthat Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, led Alqamah and al-Aswad in prayer at his house without an adhan or iqama, standing between them, and used to clasp his hands in bowing. Hammad said: Ibrahim said, “I prefer placing the hands on the knees; he considered the practice of Ibn Mas‘ud to have been abandoned.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ أَنَّ «ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه صَلَّى بِعَلْقَمَةَ وَالْأَسْوَدِ فِي بَيْتِهِ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ وَلَا إِقَامَةٍ، وَقَامَ وَسْطَهُمَا ⦗ص: 50⦘ ، وَكَانَ يُطَبِّقُ فِي الرُّكُوعِ» . وَقَالَ حَمَّادٌ: قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: يَضَعُ الْيَدَيْنِ عَلَى الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ، وَكَانَ يَرَى أَنَّ مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ قَدْ تُرِكَ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, led Alqamah and Al-Aswad in prayer in his house without a call to prayer or an establishment, and he stood between them. He would join his hands in bowing. Hammad said Ibrahim said: Placing the hands on the knees is more beloved to me, and he was of the opinion that what Ibn Mas'ud used to do had been abandoned.

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Maymun ibn Siyah, that a man came to Al-Hasan al-Basrithat a man came to al-Hasan al-Basri and asked, “Would it be more beloved to you for me to pray one rak‘ah reciting five hundred verses?” Al-Hasan was astonished, then said: “The prayer most beloved to God is the one with the longest standing.”
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ سِيَاهٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى الْحَسَنَ الْبَصْرِيَّ، فَقَالَ أُصَلِّي بِخَمْسِمِائَةِ آيَةٍ فِي رَكْعَةٍ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ؟ فَتَعَجَّبَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: «أَحَبُّ الصَّلَاةِ إِلَى اللَّهِ طُولُ الْقُنُوتِ»

records.text_en: It has reached me from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, that he said "Be solemn in prayer."

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah narrated from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, saidthat Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: “Delay the noon prayer until the heat subsides, for the scorching heat is from the blast of Hell.”
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «أَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلَاةِ، يَعْنِي الظُّهْرَ، فِي الْحَرِّ عَنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ»
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «أَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلَاةِ، يَعْنِي الظُّهْرَ، فِي الْحَرِّ عَنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ»

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn Abi Rabah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would pray standing, sitting, barefoot, and wearing sandals, and he would turn away to his right and to his left.
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، «أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يُصَلِّي قَائِمًا، وَقَاعِدًا، وَحَافِيًا، وَمُنْتَعِلًا، وَيَنْصَرِفُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ، وَعَنْ شِمَالِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، «أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يُصَلِّي قَائِمًا، وَقَاعِدًا، وَحَافِيًا، وَمُنْتَعِلًا، وَيَنْصَرِفُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ، وَعَنْ شِمَالِهِ»

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he smelled the odor of garlic and said "Whoever eats anything from this herb, let him stay in his house and not harm us with it."

Masruq sat in both, while Jundub stood in the first of them. They came to Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, and he said "Both have done well, but what Masruq did is more beloved to me."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he dislikedthat he disliked a man spreading his forearms on the ground and sitting briefly after the final prostration of the first and third rak‘ahs; rather, he would stand directly.

records.raw_text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَفْرِشَ الرَّجُلُ ذِرَاعَيْهِ، وَأَنْ يَقْعُدَ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ وَالْأُولَى بَعْدَ السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ، يَعْنِي يَقُومُ كَمَا هُوَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he disliked a man spreading his forearms (on the ground) and sitting in the third (rak'ah) and the first (rak'ah) after the final prostration, meaning he would stand as he was.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he would lean on his arms upon his thighs when the prostration was prolonged.
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَعْتَمِدُ بِذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ إِذَا طَالَ السُّجُودَ»
records.raw_text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَعْتَمِدُ بِذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ إِذَا طَالَ السُّجُودَ»

records.boundary_review_note: Arabic and English agree on the route through Ibn Umar.

records.text_en: Narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Adam ibn Ali: I prayed beside Ibn Umar, ؓ, and I laid my forearms flat. When I finished, he said , "Are you from the people of Iraq?" I said, "Yes." He said, "When you prostrate, rely on your palms and keep your upper arms away from your sides, for every part of you prostrates in this way. Do not lay your forearms flat like a beast does."
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ آدَمَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ إِلَى جَنْبِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، فَأَفْرَشْتُ ذِرَاعِي، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفْتُ قَالَ: «أَنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ؟» قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: «إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَاعْتَمِدْ عَلَى رَاحَتَيْكَ وَأَبِدَّ ضَبْعَيْكَ، فَإِنَّهُ يَسْجُدُ كُلُّ عُضْوٍ مِنْكَ، وَلَا تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ افْتِرَاشَ السَّبْعِ»
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ آدَمَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ إِلَى جَنْبِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، فَأَفْرَشْتُ ذِرَاعِي، فَلَمَّا انْصَرَفْتُ قَالَ: «أَنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ؟» قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: «إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَاعْتَمِدْ عَلَى رَاحَتَيْكَ وَأَبِدَّ ضَبْعَيْكَ، فَإِنَّهُ يَسْجُدُ كُلُّ عُضْوٍ مِنْكَ، وَلَا تَفْتَرِشْ ذِرَاعَيْكَ افْتِرَاشَ السَّبْعِ»

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Amr ibn Atiyyah, from Salman, ؓ, who said  scratching something from his body and then moistening it with saliva.
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَحُكَّ الشَّيْءَ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ، ثُمَّ يَبُلَّهُ بِبُزَاقٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَحُكَّ الشَّيْءَ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ، ثُمَّ يَبُلَّهُ بِبُزَاقٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Yahya ibn Bakir narrated to us from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Amr ibn Atiyyah, from Salman, ؓ, that he used to dislike scratching something from his body and then moistening it with saliva.
records.display_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَحُكَّ الشَّيْءَ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ، ثُمَّ يَبُلَّهُ بِبُزَاقٍ»
records.display_text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Amr ibn Atiyyah, from Salman, ؓ, who said  scratching something from his body and then moistening it with saliva.
records.isnad_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يَكْرَهُ
records.matn_ar: أَنْ يَحُكَّ الشَّيْءَ مِنْ جَسَدِهِ، ثُمَّ يَبُلَّهُ بِبُزَاقٍ»
records.isnad_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Amr ibn Atiyyah, from Salman, ؓ, who said
records.matn_en: scratching something from his body and then moistening it with saliva.
records.boundary_review_note: English names Yahya ibn Bakir, but Arabic starts “from his father” without naming Yahya. The transmitted forms are kept separately.

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said The night prayer is two by two; you give the salutation after every two rak'ahs if you wish, or if you wish you may pray fifty rak'ahs without giving the salutation between them and give the salutation only at the end of them. As for the day prayer, if you wish you may pray two rak'ahs, or if you wish four, without separating between them except for the four before Zuhr, in which you do not give the salutation except at the end of them.
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ مَثْنَى مَثْنَى، تُسَلِّمُ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ إِنْ شِئْتَ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ صَلَّيْتَ خَمْسِينَ رَكْعَةً لَمْ تُسَلِّمْ بَيْنَهُنَّ وَسَلَّمْتَ فِي آخِرِهِنَّ وَصَلَاةُ النَّهَارِ إِنْ شِئْتَ صَلَّيْتَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ أَرْبَعًا لَا تَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُنَّ إِلَّا أَرْبَعًا قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ لَا تُسَلِّمُ إِلَّا فِي آخِرِهِنَّ»

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he went out to the mosque one night and found the people gathered there, filling it. He asked, "What is the matter with the people?" They said , "A man saw in his dream that whoever prays tonight in the mosque will be forgiven." He then began to call out and shout, "Woe to you! Go out! Do not be punished twice!"
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ، وَقَدِ اجْتَمَعَ فِيهِ النَّاسُ، وَقَدِ امْتَلَأَ، فَقَالَ «مَا شَأْنُ النَّاسِ؟» قَالُوا: إِنَّ رَجُلًا رَأَى فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ صَلَّى اللَّيْلَةَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ غُفِرَ لَهُ. قَالَ: " فَجَعَلَ يُنَادِي وَيَهْتِفُ: وَيْلَكُمُ اخْرُجُوا، لَا تُعَذَّبُوا مَرَّتَيْنِ "

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said Do not crack your fingers in prayer, do not fiddle with your beard, do not bury large pebbles, do not touch them, do not place your hand on your hip, do not cover your mouth, do not drape your cloak over your shoulder, and do not squat.

records.text_en: On the authority of his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Abu Wa’il, from Ibn Mas’ud, ؓ, that they used to say: "Peace be upon God, peace be upon Jibril, peace be upon the Messenger of God." So the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said "Do not say, 'Peace be upon God,' for God is the source of peace, and peace comes from Him. Rather, say: 'All greetings, prayers, and good things are for God. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.'"
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ: السَّلَامُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَى جَبْرَائِيلَ، السَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لَا تَقُولُوا السَّلَامُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْهُ السَّلَامُ، وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا: التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ "

records.text_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who taught a man the tashahhud: The man began saying, “In the name of God and by God,” while Alqamah said, “All greetings are for God.” At the end, the man said, “I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner,” while Alqamah said, “I bear witness that there is no god but God.”

records.raw_text_en: Alqamah taught a man the tashahhud. The man began saying, "In the name of God and by God," while Alqamah was saying, "All compliments are for God." The man then said at its end, "I bear witness that there is no god but God, alone with no partner," while Alqamah was saying, "I bear witness that there is no god but God."

records.isnad_en: From his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who taught a man the tashahhud:
records.matn_en: The man began saying, “In the name of God and by God,” while Alqamah said, “All greetings are for God.” At the end, the man said, “I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner,” while Alqamah said, “I bear witness that there is no god but God.”
records.boundary_review_note: Arabic gives a chain through Alqamah, but the supplied English contains only the report wording; English isnad is absent.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said The imam gives salutation to his right: "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God," and he intends by it the men, women, and the recording angels on his right. He gives salutation to his left likewise, and he intends likewise. The one behind the imam also gives salutation and intends likewise. The imam intends if he is on the right side, and he gives salutation on the left side likewise, and the imam intends if there are people there.
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ " يُسَلِّمُ الْإِمَامُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، وَيَنْوِي مَنْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْحَفَظَةِ، وَيُسَلِّمُ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ كَذَلِكَ، وَيَنْوِي كَذَلِكَ، وَيُسَلِّمُ الَّذِي خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ وَيَنْوِي كَذَلِكَ، وَيَنْوِي الْإِمَامُ إِنْ كَانَ فِي الْجَانِبِ الْأَيْمَنِ، وَيُسَلِّمُ فِي الْجَانِبِ الْأَيْسَرِ كَذَلِكَ، وَيَنْوِي الْإِمَامُ إِذَا كَانَ فِيهِمْ "

records.text_en: His father narrated from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that a vagabond came to them. Ibn Mas‘ud said: “Drive him away with the Qur’an.” He then ordered a boy to recite a surah from the mushaf. When the boy reached the prostration verse, Ibn Mas‘ud said: “Stay where you are, boy.” He then said: “This is your imam in it, my son. When you prostrate, say the takbir.” When the vagabond heard the Qur’an, he left.
records.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّ بَطَّالًا أَقْبَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: «اطْرُدُوهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ» ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ غُلَامًا أَنْ يَقْرَأَ سُورَةً فِي الْمُصْحَفِ، فَلَمَّا انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّجْدَةِ، فَقَالَ: كَمَا أَنْتَ يَا غُلَامُ. فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ هَذَا ⦗ص: 54⦘ إِمَامُكُمْ فِيهَا يَا بُنَيَّ، إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَكَبِّرَ. فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْبَطَّالُ الْقُرْآنَ ذَهَبَ»
records.raw_text_ar: عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّ بَطَّالًا أَقْبَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: «اطْرُدُوهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ» ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ غُلَامًا أَنْ يَقْرَأَ سُورَةً فِي الْمُصْحَفِ، فَلَمَّا انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّجْدَةِ، فَقَالَ: كَمَا أَنْتَ يَا غُلَامُ. فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ هَذَا ⦗ص: 54⦘ إِمَامُكُمْ فِيهَا يَا بُنَيَّ، إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَكَبِّرَ. فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْبَطَّالُ الْقُرْآنَ ذَهَبَ»
records.raw_text_en: His father narrated from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that a vagabond came to them. Ibn Mas'ud said "Drive him away with the Quran." records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said The sun eclipsedThe sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, died. The people hurried to the Prophet in the mosque. He stood and led them in prayer, prolonging the standing until they thought he would not bow. Then he bowed for as long as he had stood. He raised his head and stood for as long as he had bowed. Then he prostrated for as long as he had stood, sat for as long as he had prostrated, and prostrated again for as long as he had sat. He did the same in the second rak‘ah. During its final prostration, he wept intensely. We heard him say three times: “O God, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them?” He then sat, recited the tashahhud, and concluded the prayer. Turning to the people, he said: “The sun and moon are two of God’s signs; they do not eclipse for anyone’s death or life. When that happens, pray. I saw myself brought near to Paradise so that, had I wished, I could have taken one of its branches. I also saw myself brought near to the Fire, and I began shielding myself and you from its flames. I saw there the man who stole the Prophet’s sandals, ﷺ. I also saw the slave of Banu al-Da‘da‘, who stole from pilgrims with his hooked staff: whenever he could take something unseen, he took it; if he was noticed, he said, ‘It only caught on my staff.’ I saw there a tall, dark-complexioned Himyari woman being punished for a cat she had tied up, not allowing it to eat the small creatures of the earth.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رضي الله عنهما، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ يَوْمَ مَاتَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ابْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم. قَالَ: فَفَزِعَ النَّاسُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. قَالَ: فَقَامَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ، فَأَطَالَ الْقِيَامَ حَتَّى ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ لَنْ يَرْكَعَ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ فَكَانَ رُكُوعُهُ قَدْرَ قِيَامِهِ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَكَانَ قِيَامُهُ كَقَدْرِ رُكُوعِهِ، ثُمَّ سَجَدَ فَكَانَ سُجُودُهُ كَقَدْرِ قِيَامِهِ، ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فَكَانَ جُلُوسُهُ كَقَدْرِ سُجُودِهِ، ثُمَّ سَجَدَ فَكَانَ سُجُودُهُ كَقَدْرِ جُلُوسِهِ، وَصَنَعَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ فِي السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ مِنَ الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ بَكَى وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ حَتَّى اشْتَدَّ بُكَاؤُهُ، قَالَ: فَسَمِعْنَاهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: «اللَّهُمَّ أَلَمْ تَعِدْنِي أَلَّا تُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنَا فِيهِمْ، اللَّهُمَّ أَلَمْ تَعِدْنِي أَلَّا تُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنَا فِيهِمْ» ، يَقُولُهَا ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، ثُمَّ قَعَدَ فَتَشَهَّدَ وَانْصَرَفَ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَجْهِهِ فَقَالَ: " إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ آيَتَانِ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ، لَا يَنْكَسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلَا لِحَيَاتِهِ، فَإِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالصَّلَاةِ، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُنِي أُدْنِيتُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى لَوْ شِئْتُ أَنْ أَتَّنَاوَلَ غُصْنًا مِنْ أَغْصَانِهَا لَفَعَلْتُ، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُنِي أُدْنِيتُ مِنَ النَّارِ حَتَّى جَعَلْتُ أَتَّقِي لَهَبَهَا عَلَيَّ وَعَلَيْكُمْ، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهَا سَارِقَ سِبْتِيَّتَيْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهَا عَبْدَ بَنِي الدَّعْدعِ سَارِقَ الْحَاجِّ ⦗ص: 55⦘ بِمِحْجَنِهِ، كَانَ إِذَا records.raw_text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رضي الله عنهما، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ يَوْمَ مَاتَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ابْنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم. قَالَ: فَفَزِعَ النَّاسُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. قَالَ: فَقَامَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ، فَأَطَالَ الْقِيَامَ حَتَّى ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ لَنْ يَرْكَعَ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ فَكَانَ رُكُوعُهُ قَدْرَ قِيَامِهِ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَكَانَ قِيَامُهُ كَقَدْرِ رُكُوعِهِ، أَلَّا تُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنَا فِيهِمْ، اللَّهُمَّ أَلَمْ تَعِدْنِي أَلَّا تُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنَا فِيهِمْ» ، يَقُولُهَا ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، ثُمَّ قَعَدَ فَتَشَهَّدَ وَانْصَرَفَ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَعَلَيْكُمْ، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهَا سَارِقَ سِبْتِيَّتَيْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهَا عَبْدَ بَنِي الدَّعْدعِ سَارِقَ الْحَاجِّ ⦗ص: 55⦘ بِمِحْجَنِهِ، كَانَ إِذَا خَفِيَ لَهُ شَيْءٌ ذَهَبَ بِهِ، فَإِنْ ظَهَرَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ: إِنَّمَا تَعَلَّقَ بِمِحْجَنِي، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِيهَا امْرَأَةً حِمْيَرِيَّةً، أَدْمَاءَ طُوَالةً تُعَذَّبُ فِي هِرَّةٍ كَانَتْ تَرْبِطُهَا، فَلَا تَدَعُهَا تَأْكُلُ مِنْ خَشَاشِ الْأَرْضِ "
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said The sun eclipsed on the day Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, died. The people rushed to the Prophet, ﷺ, in the mosque. He stood and prayed with them, prolonging his standing until they thought he would not bow. Then he bowed, and his bowing was as long as his standing. Then he raised his head from bowing, and his standing was as long as his bowing. Then he prostrated, and his prostration was as long as his standing. Then he sat, and his sitting was as long as his prostration. Then he prostrated again, and his prostration was as long as his sitting. He did the same in the second rak‘ah. When he was in the final prostration of the second rak‘ah, he wept while prostrating until his weeping intensified. We heard him saying: "O God, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them? O God, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them?" He said this three times. Then he sat, testified, and departed. He then turned to them and said: "The sun and the moon are two of God’s signs. They do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone. When that happens, you must pray. I saw myself brought near Paradise until, if I had wished, I could have taken a branch from its branches. I saw myself brought near the Fire until I began shielding myself from its flames. I saw in it the thief of the Prophet’s sandals, ﷺ. I saw in it the slave of Banu al-Da‘da‘, the thief of the pilgrims, with his staff—when something was hidden from him, he would take it, and if he was caught, he would say, 'It only clung to my staff.' I saw in it a Himyari woman, dark-skinned and tall, being punished for a cat she had tied up, not letting it eat from the creatures of the earth."

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said The sun eclipsedThe sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, died. The people hurried to the Prophet in the mosque. He stood and led them in prayer, prolonging the standing until they thought he would not bow. Then he bowed for as long as he had stood. He raised his head and stood for as long as he had bowed. Then he prostrated for as long as he had stood, sat for as long as he had prostrated, and prostrated again for as long as he had sat. He did the same in the second rak‘ah. During its final prostration, he wept intensely. We heard him say three times: “O God, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them?” He then sat, recited the tashahhud, and concluded the prayer. I saw myself brought near to Paradise so that, had I wished, I could have taken one of its branches. I also saw myself brought near to the Fire, and I began shielding myself and you from its flames. I saw there the man who stole the Prophet’s sandals, ﷺ. I also saw the slave of Banu al-Da‘da‘, who stole from pilgrims with his hooked staff: whenever he could take something unseen, he took it; if he was noticed, he said, ‘It only caught on my staff.’ I saw there a tall, dark-complexioned Himyari woman being punished for a cat she had tied up, not allowing it to eat the small creatures of the earth.”

records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said The sun eclipsed
records.matn_en: The sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim, son of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, died. The people hurried to the Prophet in the mosque. He stood and led them in prayer, prolonging the standing until they thought he would not bow. Then he bowed for as long as he had stood. He raised his head and stood for as long as he had bowed. Then he prostrated for as long as he had stood, sat for as long as he had prostrated, and prostrated again for as long as he had sat. He did the same in the second rak‘ah. During its final prostration, he wept intensely. We heard him say three times: “O God, did You not promise me that You would not punish them while I am among them?” He then sat, recited the tashahhud, and concluded the prayer. Turning to the people, he said: “The sun and moon are two of God’s signs; they do not eclipse for anyone’s death or life. When that happens, pray. I saw myself brought near to Paradise so that, had I wished, I could have taken one of its branches. I also saw myself brought near to the Fire, and I began shielding myself and you from its flames. I saw there the man who stole the Prophet’s sandals, ﷺ. I also saw the slave of Banu al-Da‘da‘, who stole from pilgrims with his hooked staff: whenever he could take something unseen, he took it; if he was noticed, he said, ‘It only caught on my staff.’ I saw there a tall, dark-complexioned Himyari woman being punished for a cat she had tied up, not allowing it to eat the small creatures of the earth.”
records.boundary_review_note: The source has the Prophet in the route followed by his statement; the sun-eclipse narrative starts the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he prayed two rak'ahs when the sun was eclipsed, then he supplicated until it cleared.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، «أَنَّهُ صَلَّى حِينَ انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ كَانَ الدُّعَاءُ حَتَّى تَجَلَّتْ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، «أَنَّهُ صَلَّى حِينَ انْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ كَانَ الدُّعَاءُ حَتَّى تَجَلَّتْ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated to us from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that the Prophet, ﷺ, passedby a refuse heap belonging to some Ansar. The people moved away from him, and he stood with his legs apart until they felt compassion for him, fearing that urine might hit him; then he urinated standing.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَرَّ عَلَى سُبَاطَةِ قَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ فَنَحَا الْقَوْمُ عَنْهُ، وَقَامَ فَتَفَاجَّ حَتَّى رَقَّ لَهُ الْقَوْمُ، خَوْفًا أَنْ يُصِيبَهُ الْبَوْلُ، ثُمَّ بَالَ قَائِمًا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, permitted women to go out for the dawn and night prayers. A man then said to Ibn Umar, "In that case, they will use it as a pretext." Ibn Umar replied, "I narrate to you from the Prophet, ﷺ, and you say this?"
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَخَّصَ لِلنِّسَاءِ فِي الْخُرُوجِ إِلَى صَلَاةِ الْغَدَاةِ وَالْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ» فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ: إِذًا يَتَّخِذْنَهُ دَغَلًا، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: أُحَدِّثُكَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَتَقُولُ هَذَا؟

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The Companionsthat he said: “The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, agreed on no prayer matter as they agreed on delaying Fajr until it grew light and hastening Maghrib. They were not persistent in any voluntary prayer as they were in the four rak‘ahs before Zuhr and the two before Fajr.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَمْ يَجْتَمِعْ أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى شَيْءٍ كَمَا اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى التَّنْوِيرِ بِالْفَجْرِ، وَالتَّبْكِيرِ بِالْمَغْرِبِ، وَلَمْ يُثَابِرُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ التَّطَوُّعِ، كَمَا ثَابَرُوا عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ، وَرَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَمْ يَجْتَمِعْ أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى شَيْءٍ كَمَا اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى التَّنْوِيرِ بِالْفَجْرِ، وَالتَّبْكِيرِ بِالْمَغْرِبِ، وَلَمْ يُثَابِرُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ التَّطَوُّعِ، كَمَا ثَابَرُوا عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ، وَرَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, did not agree upon anything as they agreed upon brightening the dawn prayer and hastening the Maghrib prayer. They did not persist in any voluntary act as they persisted in the four rak'ahs before Zuhr and the two rak'ahs of Fajr.
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَمْ يَجْتَمِعْ أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى شَيْءٍ كَمَا اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى التَّنْوِيرِ بِالْفَجْرِ، وَالتَّبْكِيرِ بِالْمَغْرِبِ، وَلَمْ يُثَابِرُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ التَّطَوُّعِ، كَمَا ثَابَرُوا عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ، وَرَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The Companionsthat he said: “The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, agreed on no prayer matter as they agreed on delaying Fajr until it grew light and hastening Maghrib. They were not persistent in any voluntary prayer as they were in the four rak‘ahs before Zuhr and the two before Fajr.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَمْ يَجْتَمِعْ
records.matn_ar: أَصْحَابُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى شَيْءٍ كَمَا اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى التَّنْوِيرِ بِالْفَجْرِ، وَالتَّبْكِيرِ بِالْمَغْرِبِ، وَلَمْ يُثَابِرُوا عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنَ التَّطَوُّعِ، كَمَا ثَابَرُوا عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ، وَرَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The Companions
records.matn_en: that he said: “The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, agreed on no prayer matter as they agreed on delaying Fajr until it grew light and hastening Maghrib. They were not persistent in any voluntary prayer as they were in the four rak‘ahs before Zuhr and the two before Fajr.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from ‘Ata ibn Abi Rabah that he was asked: "Can a child born of adultery lead the prayer?" He replied: "Yes. Are there not among them those who pray and fast more than us?"
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ: أَيَؤُمُّ وَلَدُ الزِّنَا؟ قَالَ: «نَعَمْ، أَوَلَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ هُوَ أَكْثَرُ مِنَّا صَلَاةً وَصَوْمًا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, used to say the salutation, "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God," to his right until the whiteness of his left cheek could be seen, and to his left until the whiteness of his right cheek could be seen.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يُسَلِّمُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، عَنْ يَمِينِهِ حَتَّى يُرَى بَيَاضُ خَدِّهِ الْأَيْسَرِ، وَعَنْ يَسَارِهِ حَتَّى يُرَى بَيَاضُ خَدِّهِ الْأَيْمَنِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf who said Abu Sufyan narrated to me from al-Hasan that the Prophet, ﷺ, used to pray while sitting with his arms wrapped around his legs.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who fell unconscious for a day and a night. He said Ibn Umar, ؓ, used to say: "He makes up for that, but if he was unconscious for more than that, he does not make it up."
records.text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فِي رَجُلٍ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمًا وَلَيْلَةً، فَقَالَ: ابْنُ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما كَانَ يَقُولُ: «يَقْضِي ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَقْضِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said to Aisha, ؓ: "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer." So she sent word to him, and he said: "Tell her: My father is an old, frail man. How can I stand in the place of the Messenger of God, ﷺ? It will be difficult for me. Tell him to order Umar instead." She mentioned this to the Prophet, ﷺ, and he said: "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer." So she sent word to him again, and he sent back to her: "Let you and Hafsah spare me. Tell him: Abu Bakr is frail." Then Umar passed by and said: "You are like the companions of Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead." The prayer was established, and the Prophet, ﷺ, felt some relief, so he came out for prayer supported by two men. Aisha said to him: "You cannot do this, or it will be difficult for you." He said: "The coolness of my eyes is in prayer." He entered the mosque, and Abu Bakr heard the sound of the Prophet, ﷺ, so he began to step back. The Prophet, ﷺ, gestured to him to stay in his place. The Prophet, ﷺ, sat down, and Abu Bakr stood to his right. The Prophet, ﷺ, pronounced the takbir, and Abu Bakr pronounced the takbir, and the people pronounced the takbir following Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr prayed following the prayer of the Prophet, ﷺ, and the people prayed following the prayer of Abu Bakr.

He said: "The coolness of my eyes is in prayer." He entered the mosque, and Abu Bakr heard the sound of the Prophet, ﷺ, so he began to step back. The Prophet, ﷺ, gestured to him to stay in his place. Abu Bakr prayed following the prayer of the Prophet, ﷺ, and the people prayed following the prayer of Abu Bakr.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said "I dislike that a man should spread his forearms in prayer."

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf narrated to us from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad, who said I saw Mujahid, Ata, and Tawus squatting in prayer, so I asked them about that. They said: We saw Ibn Umar squatting in prayer. I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and he said: They spoke the truth; he did that after he grew old. He said: Someone who saw him when he was young informed me that he used to dislike it and forbid it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ مُجَاهِدًا وَعَطَاءً وَطَاوُسًا يُقْعُونَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ، فَسَأَلْتُهُمْ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالُوا: «رَأَيْنَا ابْنَ عُمَرَ يُقْعِي فِي الصَّلَاةِ» فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ فَقَالَ: صَدَقُوا، قَدْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ بَعْدَ مَا كَبِرَ، قَالَ: فَأَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ رَآهُ وَهُوَ شَابٌّ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُهُ وَيَنْهَى عَنْهُ

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf related to me from his father from Abu Hanifah, who said Isma'il related to me from 'Amir from Qumayr, the wife of Masruq, that she mentioned to 'Aishah, ؓ, that she was experiencing istihadah (non-menstrual bleeding). She instructed her to refrain from prayer during the days of her menstruation, perform ghusl when she becomes pure, perform wudu for each prayer, and use a pad.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ قُمَيْرَ امْرَأَةِ مَسْرُوقٍ، أَنَّهَا ذَكَرَتْ لِعَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها أَنَّهَا مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ، «فَأَمَرَتْهَا أَنْ تَدَعَ الصَّلَاةَ أَيَّامَ حَيْضِهَا، وَتَغْتَسِلَ لِطُهْرِهَا، وَتَوَضَّأَ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ وَتَحْتَشِيَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Al-Walid ibn Uqbah wentthat Al-Walid ibn Uqbah went to Ibn Mas‘ud, Hudhayfah, and Abu Musa, ؓ, and asked, “Your Eid is tomorrow; how should I pray?” Ibn Mas‘ud said: “O Abu Abd al-Rahman, tell him.” He replied: “Begin the prayer without an adhan or iqama. Say five takbirs in the first rak‘ah: four before recitation; then recite, say the fifth takbir, and bow with it. Then stand, recite, and continue directly between the two recitations. Then say four takbirs and bow with the last of them.” He instructed him to deliver the sermon after the prayer while mounted.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ خَرَجَ الْوَلِيدُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ إِلَى ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَحُذَيْفَةَ، وَأَبِي مُوسَى رضي الله عنهم، فَقَالَ: إِنَّ عِيدَكُمْ غَدًا، فَكَيْفَ أُصَلِّي؟ فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ أَخْبِرْهُ، فَقَالَ: «ابْدَأْ بِالصَّلَاةِ بِلَا أَذَانٍ وَلَا إِقَامَةٍ، وَكَبِّرْ فِي الْأُولَى خَمْسًا، أَرْبَعَةً قَبْلَ الْقِرَاءَةِ، ثُمَّ اقْرَأْ وَكَبِّرِ الْخَامِسَةَ، فَارْكَعْ بِهَا، ثُمَّ قُمْ فَاقْرَأْ وَوَالِ مَا بَيْنَ الْقِرَاءَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ أَرْبَعًا، وَارْكَعْ بِآخِرِهِنَّ، وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَخْطُبَ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf narrated to us from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad, who said I asked Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the prayer before the Eid prayer, and they said: "There is no prayer before it." Ibrahim said: "Pray four rak'ahs after it," and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Pray after it as you wish."

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Mu'awiyah, ؓ, was a stout man. When he ascended the pulpit, he would sit. He was the first to deliver the Friday sermon while seated, the first to begin the sermon before the prayer on Eid, and the first to give the call to prayer on the two Eids.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said I asked himI asked him, “If I do not go out with the imam for the Eid prayer, should I pray at home as the imam does?” He said, “No.” I asked, “If I come to the Eid prayer ground and have missed it, how much should I pray?” He said, “If you wish, pray two rak‘ahs; if you wish, four; and if you wish, do nothing.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ إِذَا لَمْ أَخْرُجْ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ فِي الْعِيدِ، أُصَلِّي فِي بَيْتِي كَمَا يُصَلِّي الْإِمَامُ؟ قَالَ: «لَا» ، قُلْتُ: فَإِذَا أَتَيْتُ الْجَبَّانَةَ، وَقَدْ فَاتَنِي، كَمْ أُصَلِّي؟ قَالَ: «إِنْ شِئْتَ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ شِئْتَ أَرْبَعًا، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَلَا شَيْءَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he would go to the prayer ground on the day of Fitr having eaten, and on the day of Adha before eating.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abd al-Karim from Umm Atiyyah, ؓ, who said Women were permitted to go out for the two Eids, to the extent that even young virgins would go out wearing a single garment, and menstruating women would also go out, sitting among the other women, making supplications but not praying.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنْ أُمِّ عَطِيَّةَ رضي الله عنها قَالَتْ «كَانَ يُرَخَّصُ لِلنِّسَاءِ فِي الْخُرُوجِ فِي الْعِيدَيْنِ ⦗ص: 60⦘ ، حَتَّى لَقَدْ كَانَتِ الْبِكْرَانِ لَتَخْرُجَانِ فِي الثَّوْبِ الْوَاحِدِ، وَحَتَّى تَخْرُجَ الْحَائِضُ فَتَجْلِسُ فِي عَرْضِ النِّسَاءِ، فَتَدْعُو وَلَا تُصَلِّي»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, who said I saw al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, ؓ, delivering a sermon on the day of Eid after the prayer while mounted on his riding animal.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he would say the takbir in the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah until after the Asr prayer on the last of the Days of Tashriq.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said regarding the takbir during the days of Tashriq: "From after the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah until after the Asr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice." And he would say the takbir as follows: "God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest, God is the Greatest, and to God belongs all praise."

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah claimed that it reached him from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said "There is no Friday prayer nor *Tashriq* except in a major city with a central mosque."
records.text_ar: وَزَعَمَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا جُمُعَةَ وَلَا تَشْرِيقَ إِلَّا فِي مِصْرٍ جَامِعٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: وَزَعَمَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا جُمُعَةَ وَلَا تَشْرِيقَ إِلَّا فِي مِصْرٍ جَامِعٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Abu Hanifah claimed that it reached him from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said "There is no Friday prayer nor *Tashriq* except in a major city with a central mosque."

records.matn_en: "There is no Friday prayer nor *Tashriq* except in a major city with a central mosque."
records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hanifah’s statement is a balagh; the intervening route is not supplied.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "The 'known days' are the first ten days [of Dhu al-Hijjah], and the 'counted days' are the days of Tashriq."
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ ⦗ص: 61⦘ ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ: «أَيَّامٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ أَيَّامُ الْعَشْرِ، وَأَيَّامٌ مَعْدُودَاتٌ أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ أَبِي يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ ⦗ص: 61⦘ ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ: «أَيَّامٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ أَيَّامُ الْعَشْرِ، وَأَيَّامٌ مَعْدُودَاتٌ أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s explanation begins the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he would come on Friday while the Imam was delivering the sermon and would recite a portion when he sat down, and in those conquests.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَجِيءُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ وَالْإِمَامُ يَخْطُبُ، وَيَقْرَأُ جُزْءًا إِذَا أَخَذَ ، وَفِي تِلْكَ الْفُتُوحِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “The imam begins with the sermon on the Day of Arafah, before the prayer.”

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: "He used to say the takbir on the afternoon of Arafah while sitting with his companions."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said One should remain silent during the two Eids just as one remains silent during Friday prayer.

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “The sacrifice is slaughtered when either of the two groups has departed: the people at the mosque or the people at the Eid prayer ground.”

records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "The days of sacrifice (al-Adha) are three: the Day of Sacrifice and the two days following it, and the days of Tashriq are three days after the Day of Sacrifice."
