records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah who said It reached me that when the Prophet, ﷺ, conquered
records.matn_en: Mecca, he did not enter any house until he brought down Khubayb, embraced him, prayed over him, and buried him.
records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hanifah explicitly introduces the Prophetic attribution as بلغني; unnamed intermediaries are not reconstructed.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding men and women for whom the funeral prayer is offered: The men are placed on the side nearest the imam, and the women on the side nearest the qiblah, because in life the men are closest to the imam, and so it is in death.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِمْ: «يُوضَعُ الرِّجَالُ مِمَّا يَلِي الْإِمَامَ، وَالنِّسَاءُ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، لِأَنَّ الرِّجَالَ هُمْ يَلُونَ الْإِمَامَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ، فَكَذَلِكَ هُمْ فِي الْمَوْتِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِمْ: «يُوضَعُ الرِّجَالُ مِمَّا يَلِي الْإِمَامَ، وَالنِّسَاءُ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، لِأَنَّ الرِّجَالَ هُمْ يَلُونَ الْإِمَامَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ، فَكَذَلِكَ هُمْ فِي الْمَوْتِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: "The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, used to lower the deceased into the grave from the qiblah side or from the feet end; they would place the body by either approach.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، وَمِنْ قِبَلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ، وَكُلَّ ذَلِكَ كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، وَمِنْ قِبَلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ، وَكُلَّ ذَلِكَ كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: "The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, used to enter [the lavatory] from the direction facing the qiblah, from the direction of the feet, and from all directions—they used to enter from all of them."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، وَمِنْ قِبَلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ، وَكُلَّ ذَلِكَ كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: "The Companions of Muhammad, ﷺ, used to lower the deceased into the grave from the qiblah side or from the feet end; they would place the body by either approach.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ مُحَمَّدٍ
records.matn_ar: صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ، وَمِنْ قِبَلِ الرِّجْلَيْنِ، وَكُلَّ ذَلِكَ كَانُوا يَدْخُلُونَ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: "The Companions of Muhammad
records.matn_en: , ﷺ, used to lower the deceased into the grave from the qiblah side or from the feet end; they would place the body by either approach.”
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s report about the Companions begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Ishaq from Amir from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he prayed over Zayd ibn Umar and Umm Kulthum, placing Zayd on the side nearest the imam and Umm Kulthum on the side nearest the qiblah.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما «أَنَّهُ صَلَّى عَلَى زَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، وَأُمِّ كُلْثُومٍ، فَجَعَلَ زَيْدًا مِمَّا يَلِي الْإِمَامَ، وَأُمَّ كُلْثُومٍ مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he used to disapprove of placing a marker on the grave, putting bricks on the *lahd* (grave niche), and plastering the grave.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said The people of Medina used to lower the deceased into the grave from the qiblah side in earlier times. Because their soil was weak, they later adopted the sliding method of placing the body into the grave.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Sufyan ibn al-Ala from al-Hakam who said Ali, ؓ, went out for the funeral of a man from Banu Badda’. When he reached the grave, he reproached the man’s sons until they brought the bier.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ بْنِ الْعَلَاءِ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ، قَالَ «خَرَجَ عَلِيٌّ رضي الله عنه فِي جَنَازَةِ رَجُلٍ مِنْ بَنِي بَدَّاءٍ، فَأَتَى الْقَبْرَ، فَأَنْكَرَ عَلَى بَنِيهِ حَتَّى جَاءُوا بِالْجَنَازَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said There is no zakat on fewer than five camels. When they reach five, there is one sheep due on them up to nine. When they are ten, there are two sheep due up to fourteen. When they are fifteen, there are three sheep due up to nineteen. When they are twenty, there are four sheep due up to twenty-four. When they reach twenty-five, there is a *bint makhad* (a one-year-old she-camel) due up to thirty-five. If they increase by one, there is a *bint labun* (a two-year-old she-camel) due up to forty-five. If they increase by one, there is a *hiqqah* (a three-year-old she-camel) due up to sixty. If they increase by one, there is a *jatha'ah* (a four-year-old she-camel) due up to seventy-five. If they increase by one, there are two *bint labun* due up to ninety. If they increase by one, there are two *hiqqah* due up to one hundred and twenty. Then the obligation restarts—if the camels are many, there is one *hiqqah* for every fifty.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَيْسَ فِي أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسٍ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ صَدَقَةٌ، فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ خَمْسًا فَفِيهَا شَاةٌ إِلَى تِسْعٍ، وَإِذَا كَانَتْ عَشْرًا فَفِيهَا شَاتَانِ إِلَى أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ، فَإِذَا كَانَتْ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ فَفِيهَا ثَلَاثُ شِيَاهٍ إِلَى تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ، فَإِذَا كَانَتْ عِشْرِينَ فَفِيهَا أَرْبَعُ شِيَاهٍ إِلَى أَرْبَعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ، فَإِذَا بَلَغَتْ خَمْسًا وَعِشْرِينَ فَفِيهَا ابْنَةُ مَخَاضٍ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا ابْنَةُ لَبُونٍ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا حِقَّةٌ إِلَى سِتِّينَ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا جَذَعَةٌ إِلَى خَمْسٍ وَسَبْعِينَ ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا ابْنَتَا لَبُونٍ إِلَى تِسْعِينَ ، فَإِذَا زَادَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَفِيهَا حِقَّتَانِ إِلَى عِشْرِينَ وَمِائَةٍ، ثُمَّ تُسْتَأْنَفُ الْفَرِيضَةُ، فَإِنْ كَثُرَتِ الْإِبِلُ فَفِي كُلِّ خَمْسِينَ حِقَّةٌ»

records.matn_ar: بْنَ مَالِكٍ سَاعِيًا إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ فَمَكَثَ حِينًا، ثُمَّ اسْتَأْذَنَهُ فِي الْجِهَادِ، فَقَالَ «أَوَلَسْتَ فِي الْجَهْدِ» قَالَ: وَمِنْ أَيْنَ وَالنَّاسُ يَقُولُونَ: هُوَ يَظْلِمُنَا، قَالَ: «فَبِمَاذَا؟ قَالُوا» : قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: تَعُدُّ عَلَيْنَا السَّخْلَةَ، وَلَا تَأْخُذُهَا مِنَّا، قَالَ: «فَاعْدُدْهَا عَلَيْهِمْ، وَإِنْ جَاءَ بِهَا الرَّاعِي يَحْمِلُهَا عَلَى كَتِفِهِ، أَوَلَسْتَ تَدَعُ لَهُمُ الرُّبَّى وَالْأَكِيلَةَ وَالْمَاخِضَ وَفَحْلَ الْغَنَمِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from ‘Ata ibn ‘Ajlan, from al-Hasan, that ‘Umar, ؓ, sent Sufyan
records.matn_en: ibn Malik as a zakat collector to Basra. He stayed there for a time, then asked Umar for leave to go on a military expedition. Umar said, “Are you not already engaged in strenuous work?” He replied, “How so, when people say, ‘He is treating us unjustly’?” Umar asked, “In what way?” He replied, “They say, ‘You count the young lamb against us but do not take it from us.’” Umar said, “Then count it against them—even if the shepherd brings it carried on his shoulder. Do you not leave them the ewe nursing her lamb, the animal kept for food, the pregnant ewe, and the breeding ram?”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said There is no alms due on less than twenty mithqals of gold. When it reaches twenty mithqals, half a mithqal is due, and for any increase beyond that, the calculation follows the same proportion.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said If you have wealth on which you must pay zakat and you acquire more wealth before a full year has passed, then pay zakat on it together with the original wealth when the year elapses. But if you had no wealth, then do not pay zakat on it until a full year has passed from the day you acquired it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ لَكَ مَالٌ تُزَكِّيهِ فَأَصَبْتَ مَالًا قَبْلَ أَنْ يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ، فَزَكِّهِ مَعَهُ إِذَا حَالَ الْحَوْلُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكَ مَالٌ، فَلَا تُزَكِّهِ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ مُذْ يَوْمِ أَصَبْتَهُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Sirin from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, regarding a man who has a debt owed to him and then collects it: "He pays its zakah for the past years."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ لَهُ الدَّيْنُ فَيَقْبِضُهُ، قَالَ: «يُزَكِّيهِ لِمَا كَانَ مَضَى»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding the man who has a debt: "Its zakat is upon him."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said "The injury caused by an animal is not compensable; damage caused by a fall into a well is not compensable; injury caused in a mine is not compensable; and one-fifth is due on buried treasure.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «فِي الْعَجْمَاءِ جُبَارٌ، وَالْقَلِيبِ جُبَارٌ، وَالْمَعْدِنِ جُبَارٌ، وَفِي الرِّكَازِ الْخُمُسُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «فِي الْعَجْمَاءِ جُبَارٌ، وَالْقَلِيبِ جُبَارٌ، وَالْمَعْدِنِ جُبَارٌ، وَفِي الرِّكَازِ الْخُمُسُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said "The injury caused by an animal is without liability, the injury in a well is without liability, the injury in a mine is without liability, and one-fifth is due on treasure trove."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "There is a fifth is due on what is extracted from a mine.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said There is no alms on less than two hundred dirhams. When it reaches two hundred dirhams, then five dirhams are due on it, and whatever exceeds that is calculated accordingly.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the wife of Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, said to him: "I have some jewelry. Is zakah due on it?" He said: "Yes." She said: "If I give it to my nephew who is an orphan, will that suffice for me?" He said: "Yes." And he said: "Half a mithqal for every twenty mithqals."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said There is no zakah on any pearls or jewels if they are worn, but if they are for trade, then zakah is due on them. If they are for trade, he should evaluate them and pay zakah at the rate of five dirhams for every two hundred dirhams.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَيْسَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ اللُّؤْلُؤِ وَالْجَوْهَرِ زَكَاةٌ إِذَا كَانَ يُلْبَسُ، وَإِذَا كَانَ لِلتِّجَارَةِ فَفِيهِ الزَّكَاةُ، فَإِنْ كَانَ لِلتِّجَارَةِ قَوَّمَهُ، فَزَكَّاهُ عَنْ كُلِّ مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from Anas ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that he wanted to appoint him, so he said, “No—not until you write for me the same agreement that Umar wrote for Anas: that I am to collect one-tenth from the people of war, one-half of one-tenth from the protected people, and one-quarter of one-tenth from the Muslims.” Yusuf narrated to me from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Sakhrah, from Ziyad ibn Hudayr, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that Umar appointed him over Ayn al-Tamr and instructed him to do the same.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said On everything produced by the earth, whether little or much, there is zakah. On what is watered by the sky or by flowing water, there is a tenth, and on what is watered by a bucket or a waterwheel, there is half a tenth.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding this verse: *"And give its right on the day of its harvest"* (6:141): "It is abrogated."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from someone who narrated to him, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he doubled the alms-tax upon the Christians of Banu Taghlib as compensation for the land tax.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Umar ibn Jubayr, from Ibrahim that a man wanted to give Ibrahim four hundred dirhams as zakat from his wealth, but Ibrahim refused to accept it. So Ibrahim went with him to guide him, and he was giving the people of each household ten dirhams each. Ibrahim then said "If it were me, I would prefer to enrich one household with it."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُعْطِيَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ زَكَاةَ مَالِهِ أَرْبَعَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ، فَأَبَى أَنْ يَقْبَلَهَا، فَذَهَبَ مَعَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَدُلُّهُ، وَكَانَ يُعْطِي أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ عَشَرَةً عَشَرَةً، فَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: «لَوْ كُنْتُ أَنَا كُنْتُ أُغْنِي بِهَا أَهْلَ بَيْتٍ وَاحِدٍ، كَانَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Masruq: Abu al-Awja’ used to prepare food, and Masruq would come to him. Abu al-Awja’ was in charge of the taxes, and he was ill.

records.text_en: Yusuf said Abu Yusuf said, and Abu Hanifah said: It has reached me from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said, "There is nothing due on what exceeds two hundred until it reaches forty dirhams." Abu Hanifah used to follow this. Abu Yusuf said, "Whatever exceeds two hundred, even if it does not reach forty dirhams, then there is something due on it according to its calculation."

records.isnad_ar: قَالَ يُوسُفُ قَالَ أَبُو يُوسُفَ وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " مَا زَادَ عَلَى الْمِائَتَيْنِ

records.isnad_en: Yusuf said Abu Yusuf said, and Abu Hanifah said: It has reached me from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said, "There is nothing due on what exceeds two hundred
records.matn_en: until it reaches forty dirhams." Abu Hanifah used to follow this. Abu Yusuf said, "Whatever exceeds two hundred, even if it does not reach forty dirhams, then there is something due on it according to its calculation."
records.boundary_review_note: Several speakers are named before and after the quotation. The report text starts with al-Hasan’s quoted view; subsequent Abu Hanifah and Abu Yusuf comments are retained in the same matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said There is no zakah on the wealth of an orphan until he reaches maturity and prayer becomes obligatory upon him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا زَكَاةَ فِي مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ حَتَّى يُدْرِكَ وَيَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said When a man intends to enter ihram for Hajj while combining Hajj and Umrah, he may bathe if he wishes or perform ablution; bathing is preferable. He enters ihram after his prayer, or after he has mounted and his camel has risen to its feet. On arriving in Mecca, he circumambulates the House for his Umrah: three circuits at a brisk pace from the Black Stone back to it, then four at an ordinary pace. Each time he passes the Stone, he touches it without harming a Muslim; if he cannot, he faces it and says the takbir. Then he prays two rak‘ahs at the Station of Ibrahim, or wherever convenient, returns to the Stone, and touches it. He then goes to Safa and Marwah. At Safa he stands facing the Kaaba where he can see it, praises God, and supplicates for himself. He descends toward Marwah at an ordinary pace, walks briskly through the bottom of the valley, and after passing it continues at an ordinary pace until he reaches Marwah. He does there as he did at Safa. He makes seven passages between the two, beginning at Safa and ending at Marwah, walking briskly through the valley. Then he circumambulates the House for Hajj and performs sa‘i between Safa and Marwah. He remains in ihram; none of the things forbidden by ihram becomes lawful to him. He circumambulates the House as he wishes and recites the talbiyah. At midday he sets out for Mina, where he prays Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and the Fajr prayer of the Day of Arafah. Then in the morning he proceeds to Arafat and prays Dhuhr and Asr there. If he prays with the Imam, he combines the two; if he prays at his camp, he prays each at its proper time. He does not depart until he has prayed Asr. Then he stands behind the Imam if he can. When the sun sets, he departs.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَرَادَ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يُحْرِمَ بِالْحَجِّ وَيَقْرِنَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اغْتَسَلَ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ تَوَضَّأَ، وَالْغُسْلُ أَفْضَلُ، ثُمَّ يُحْرِمُ فِي دُبُرِ صَلَاتِهِ، أَوْ بَعْدَ مَا يَسْتَوِي بِهِ بَعِيرُهُ، وَإِذَا قَدِمَ مَكَّةَ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ لِعُمْرَتِهِ ثَلَاثَةَ أَشْوَاطٍ، يَرْمُلُ فِيهَا مِنَ الْحَجَرِ إِلَى الْحَجَرِ، وَأَرْبَعَةَ ⦗ص: 93⦘ أَشْوَاطٍ عَلَى هِينَتِهِ، يَسْتَلِمُ الْحَجَرَ كُلَّمَا مَرَّ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يُؤْذَى بِهِ مُسْلِمٌ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعِ اسْتَقْبَلَهُ فَكَبَّرَ، ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ عِنْدَ الْمَقَامِ، أَوْ حَيْثُ تَيَسَّرَ عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ يَأْتِي الْحَجَرَ فَيَسْتَلِمُهُ، ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ إِلَى الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، فَيُقِيمُ عَلَى الصَّفَا مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْكَعْبَةِ حَيْثُ يَرَاهَا، فَيَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ، وَيَدْعُو لِنَفْسِهِ، ثُمَّ يَهْبِطُ إِلَى الْمَرْوَةِ عَلَى هِينَتِهِ، وَيَسْعَى فِي بَطْنِ الْوَادِي سَعْيًا، فَإِذَا جَاوَزَهُ مَشَى عَلَى هِينَتِهِ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ الْمَرْوَةَ، فَيَفْعَلُ كَمَا يَفْعَلُ عَلَى الصَّفَا، وَيَطُوفُ بَيْنَهُمَا سَبْعَةَ أَشْوَاطٍ، يَبْدَأُ بِالصَّفَا، وَيَخْتِمُ بِالْمَرْوَةِ، وَيَسْعَى فِي بَطْنِ الْوَادِي، ثُمَّ يَطُوفُ لِحَجِّهِ بِالْبَيْتِ، وَبَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، ثُمَّ يُقِيمُ حَرَامًا لَا يَحِلُّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، وَيَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ مَا بَدَا لَهُ، وَيُلَبِّي، ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ إِلَى مِنًى بِالْهَاجِرَةِ، فَيُصَلِّي بِهَا يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ وَالْمَغْرِبَ وَالْعِشَاءَ وَالْفَجْرَ، مِنْ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ، ثُمَّ يَغْدُو فَيَنْزِلُ بِعَرَفَاتٍ فَيُصَلِّي بِهَا الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ، فَإِنْ صَلَّى مَعَ الْإِمَامِ صَلَّاهُمَا جَمِيعًا، وَإِنْ صَلَّى فِي رَحْلِهِ صَلَّى كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ لِوَقْتِهَا، وَلَا يَرْحَلُ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ الْعَصْرَ، ثُمَّ يَقِفُ وَرَاءَ الْإمَامِ إِنِ اسْتَطَاعَ، فَإِذَا غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ دَفَعَ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said When a man intends to enter ihram for Hajj and combine it with Umrah, if he wishes he may perform ghusl, or if he wishes he may perform wudu, but ghusl is better. Then he enters ihram after his prayer or after his camel has settled. When he arrives in Mecca, he performs tawaf for his Umrah with three circuits, jogging between the two markers, and four circuits at a normal pace. He touches the Black Stone every time he passes it without harming any Muslim. If he cannot touch it, he faces it and says takbir. Then he prays two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim or wherever it is convenient for him. Then he comes to the Black Stone and touches it. Then he goes out to Safa and Marwah, standing on Safa facing the Kaaba where he can see it, praising God and supplicating for himself. Then he descends to Marwah at a normal pace, jogging in the valley, and when he passes it he walks at a normal pace until he reaches Marwah, doing as he did on Safa. He performs seven circuits between them, starting at Safa and ending at Marwah, jogging in the valley. Then he performs tawaf for his Hajj at the House and between Safa and Marwah. Then he remains in ihram, not coming out of anything. He performs tawaf of the House as he wishes and recites the talbiyah. Then he departs for Mina at midday, praying Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr there on the Day of Tarwiyah. On the Day of Arafah, he sets out early and stops at Arafat, praying Zuhr and Asr there. If he prays with the Imam, he prays them together, and if he prays in his camp, he prays each at its time. He does not leave until he has prayed Asr. Then he stands behind the Imam if he can. When the sun sets, he departs.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Al-Aswad and Alqamah, that they set out with Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he said "O people, maintain tranquility, for righteousness is not in making the camels run or spurring the horses." They said: "He did not urge his mount beyond its natural pace, even as it trotted along." Then he returned to Ibrahim’s narration: Then you descend at Al-Muzdalifah and pray Maghrib and Isha there with one call to prayer and one iqamah. When you pray the morning prayer, stand with the Imam. When he departs, you depart until you reach Mina, where you stone Jamrat al-Aqabah. Then you cease the talbiyah at the first pebble you throw. Then you slaughter, shave your head, and visit the House on the same day. You stay in Mina, stoning the jamarat the next day when the sun has passed its zenith, before praying. You begin with the one near the mosque, stoning it with seven pebbles. Then you stand where the people stand. Then you do the same with the middle one. Then you stand where the people stand and stone Jamrat al-Aqabah, without stopping there. You do all this the next day as well. If you leave, there is no harm. If the sun sets on you, stay until the next day, then stone the jamarat as you did the day before. Then depart and perform the farewell tawaf. Hammad said: I mentioned this to Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and he and Ibrahim did not differ on anything regarding Hajj.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Al-Aswad and Alqamah, that they set out with Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he said "O people, maintain tranquility, for righteousness is not in making the camels run or spurring the horses." They said: "He did not urge his mount beyond its natural pace, even as it trotted along." Then he returned to Ibrahim’s narration: Then you descend at Al-Muzdalifah and pray Maghrib and Isha there with one call to prayer and one iqamah. When you pray the morning prayer, stand with the Imam. When he departs, you depart until you reach Mina, where you stone Jamrat al-Aqabah. Then you cease the talbiyah at the first pebble you throw. Then you slaughter, shave your head, and visit the House on the same day. You stay in Mina, stoning the jamarat the next day when the sun has passed its zenith, before praying. You begin with the one near the mosque, stoning it with seven pebbles. Then you stand where the people stand. Then you do the same with the middle one. Then you stand where the people stand and stone Jamrat al-Aqabah, without stopping there. You do all this the next day as well. If you leave, there is no harm. If the sun sets on you, stay until the next day, then stone the jamarat as you did the day before. Then depart and perform the farewell tawaf. Hammad said: I mentioned this to Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and he and Ibrahim did not differ on anything regarding Hajj.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man intends to enter ihram for Hajj, he performs ablution or bathes; bathing is preferable. He then wears an izar and a rida’, applies whatever oil he wishes, and prays two rak‘ahs. He enters ihram after that prayer, after an obligatory prayer, or once he has mounted and his camel has risen to its feet. His izar and rida’ should be new or washed, provided they are not saturated with safflower, saffron, or wars. The talbiyah is to say: “Here I am, O God, here I am. Here I am; You have no partner; here I am. All praise and blessing are Yours, and sovereignty; You have no partner.” When he says this, he has entered ihram.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man intends to enter into the state of ihram for Hajj, he should perform ablution or take a bath, and taking a bath is better. records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from the one who narrated to him that Ibn Umar, ؓ, pronounced the talbiyah as in Ibrahim’s report, adding: “Here I am at Your service; here I am at Your service, ever obedient. My longing is toward You, and my deeds are for You.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ أَنَّ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما لَبَّى مِثْلَ حَدِيثِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَزَادَ فِيهِ: «لَبَّيْكَ لَبَّيْكَ، وَسَعْدَيْكَ لَبَّيْكَ، وَالرَّغْبَاءُ إِلَيْكَ وَالْعَمَلُ»

Here I am at Your service, and happiness is Yours. Longing and deeds are for You."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said "The best of Hajj is *al-‘ajj* and *al-thajj*. As for *al-‘ajj*, it is raising the voice with *talbiyah*, and as for *al-thajj*, it is the slaughter of camels."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «أَفْضَلُ الْحَجِّ الْعَجُّ وَالثَّجُّ، فَأَمَّا الْعَجُّ فَالْعَجِيجُ بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ، وَأَمَّا الثَّجُّ فَنَحْرُ الْبُدْنِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «أَفْضَلُ الْحَجِّ الْعَجُّ وَالثَّجُّ، فَأَمَّا الْعَجُّ فَالْعَجِيجُ بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ، وَأَمَّا الثَّجُّ فَنَحْرُ الْبُدْنِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the takbir: "People say the takbir in what they should not, and they abandon it in what they should."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said "The one in ihram should say the talbiyah after every prayer, whenever he has mounted and his camel has risen to its feet, whenever he ascends a hill, and in the last part of the night.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from ‘Ata’ that he used to wear a cap while in ihram, and he would say: “I suffer from my head, so I wear it, and I slaughter a sheep.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far say: "Ata' has more knowledge of Hajj than I do."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said Women are not required to perform *ramal* around the House, nor to run between al-Safa and al-Marwah in the bottom of the valley. Women may wear whatever they wish when in ihram, except the face-veil, and except what is dyed with wars or saffron, or saturated with safflower.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ‘Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from Kathir ibn Jumhan, who said While ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, ؓ, was in the area between the two hills (al-Mas‘a) wearing two garments dyed in the color of Harawi, a man approached him and said, “Do you wear these two dyed garments while in a state of ihram?” He replied, “They were only dyed with mud.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, who said I asked Ibn Umar, ؓ, “Does a man apply perfume before entering ihram?” He said, “No. I would rather wake up with tar on me than wake up with perfume on me while in ihram.” He continued: “Then I went to Aisha, ؓ, and told her what Ibn Umar had said. She replied, ‘I perfumed the Messenger of God, ﷺ; he then went to his wives and afterward entered ihram.’”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, was standing at Arafat when he saw a man whose head was dripping with perfume. Umar said to him, “Are you not in ihram, woe to you?” The man replied, “Yes, Commander of the Faithful.” Umar said, “Why do I see your head dripping with perfume when a pilgrim in ihram should be disheveled and dusty?” The man replied, “I entered ihram for Umrah alone and came to Mecca with my family. I completed my Umrah, then on the eve of the Day of Tarwiyah I entered ihram for Hajj.” Umar judged that the man had told the truth: his last contact with women and perfume had been only the day before. Umar then forbade tamattu‘ in Hajj and said, “By God, if I let you practice tamattu‘—completing Umrah and then entering ihram for Hajj—you would soon lie with your wives beneath the arak trees of ʿUranah, then set out as pilgrims.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ بَيْنَا هُوَ وَاقِفٌ بِعَرَفَاتٍ، إِذْ أَبْصَرَ رَجُلًا يَقْطُرُ رَأْسُهُ طِيبًا، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ: «أَلَسْتَ مُحْرِمًا؟ وَيْحَكَ» فَقَالَ: بَلَى يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. قَالَ: «مَا لِي أَرَاكَ يَقْطُرُ رَأْسُكَ طِيبًا، وَالْمُحْرِمُ أَشْعَثُ أَغْبَرُ» ؟ قَالَ: أَهْلَلْتُ بِالْعُمْرَةِ مُفْرَدَةً، وَقَدِمْتُ مَكَّةَ وَمَعِي أَهْلِي، فَفَرَغْتُ مِنْ عُمْرَتِي، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ عَشِيَّةُ التَّرْوِيَةِ أَهْلَلْتُ بِالْحَجِّ، قَالَ: فَرَأَى عُمَرُ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ قَدْ صَدَقَهُ، إِنَّمَا عَهْدُهُ بِالنِّسَاءِ وَالطِّيبِ بِالْأَمْسِ، فَنَهَى عُمَرُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ، وَقَالَ: «إِذًا وَاللَّهِ لَأَوْشَكْتُمْ لَوْ خَلَّيْتُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْمُتْعَةِ أَنْ تُضَاجِعُوهُنَّ ⦗ص: 98⦘ تَحْتَ أَرَاكِ عُرَنَةَ، ثُمَّ تَرُوحُونَ حُجَّاجًا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, was standing at Arafat when he saw a man whose head was dripping with perfume. Umar said to him, "Are you not in ihram? Woe to you!" The man replied, "Yes, O Commander of the Faithful." Umar said, "Why do I see your head dripping with perfume, when the one in ihram should be disheveled and dusty?" The man said, "I entered ihram for Umrah alone, then I came to Mecca with my family. After completing my Umrah, on the evening of Tarwiyah, I entered ihram for Hajj." Umar realized the man was truthful, as his last encounter with women and perfume was only the day before. So Umar forbade mut'ah (temporary marriage) at that point and said, "If I were to leave you to mut'ah, by God, you would soon be lying with them under the Arak trees of Uranah, then returning as pilgrims."
records.display_text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ بَيْنَا هُوَ وَاقِفٌ بِعَرَفَاتٍ، إِذْ أَبْصَرَ رَجُلًا يَقْطُرُ رَأْسُهُ طِيبًا، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ: «أَلَسْتَ مُحْرِمًا؟ وَيْحَكَ» فَقَالَ: بَلَى يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. قَالَ: «مَا لِي أَرَاكَ يَقْطُرُ رَأْسُكَ طِيبًا، وَالْمُحْرِمُ أَشْعَثُ أَغْبَرُ» ؟ قَالَ: أَهْلَلْتُ بِالْعُمْرَةِ مُفْرَدَةً، وَقَدِمْتُ مَكَّةَ وَمَعِي أَهْلِي، فَفَرَغْتُ مِنْ عُمْرَتِي، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ عَشِيَّةُ التَّرْوِيَةِ أَهْلَلْتُ بِالْحَجِّ، قَالَ: فَرَأَى عُمَرُ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ قَدْ صَدَقَهُ، إِنَّمَا عَهْدُهُ بِالنِّسَاءِ وَالطِّيبِ بِالْأَمْسِ، فَنَهَى عُمَرُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ، وَقَالَ: «إِذًا وَاللَّهِ لَأَوْشَكْتُمْ لَوْ خَلَّيْتُ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْمُتْعَةِ أَنْ تُضَاجِعُوهُنَّ تَحْتَ أَرَاكِ عُرَنَةَ، ثُمَّ تَرُوحُونَ حُجَّاجًا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, that he came out on the morning of the Day of Sacrifice from the Mosque of al-Khayf, pronouncing the talbiyah, intending to stone the Jamrat al-‘Aqabah. The people gathered around him, saying, "A man pronouncing the talbiyah for Hajj on the Day of Sacrifice!" He asked, "What is the matter with the people? Have they forgotten, or are they ignorant, or has it been too long since they knew?" Then he raised his voice, pronouncing the talbiyah, "Labbayk as many times as the number of dust particles, labbayk." When the people realized it was Ibn Mas‘ud, they dispersed from him, knowing that he was more knowledgeable about the matter than they.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ata ibn Abi Rabah from al-Fadl ibn Abbas, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he continued to recite the talbiyah until he threw the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The talbiyah for Umrah is not discontinued until one says the takbir upon touching the Black Stone at the beginning of his first circumambulation of the House. The talbiyah for Hajj is discontinued when casting the first pebble at Jamrat al-Aqabah on the Day of Sacrifice.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said Zayd ibn Suhan al-Abdi, Salman ibn Rabi‘ah al-Bahili, and al-Subayy ibn Ma‘bad al-Taghlibi set out to perform Hajj during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ. Zayd and Salman entered ihram for Hajj alone, while al-Subayy entered ihram for both Umrah and Hajj. They said to him, “Woe to you! You are combining Umrah and Hajj even though Umar has forbidden tamattu‘ in Hajj? By God, you are more misguided than your camel!” Al-Subayy replied, “We will go to Umar, and you will go to him too.” When al-Subayy reached Mecca, he circumambulated the House for his Umrah and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah. He then returned still in ihram, with nothing having become lawful to him. He circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for his Hajj, then remained in ihram until he reached Arafat and completed his Hajj. On the Day of Sacrifice he offered a sacrifice for his tamattu‘. When they departed, they passed Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ. Zayd ibn Suhan said, “Commander of the Faithful, you forbade tamattu‘, yet al-Subayy has performed it.” Umar asked, “What exactly did you do, al-Subayy?” He replied, “I entered ihram for Umrah and Hajj. When I reached Mecca, I circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for my Umrah. Then I returned and circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for my Hajj. I remained in ihram until the Day of Sacrifice, when I offered a sacrifice for my tamattu‘ and then exited ihram.” Umar patted him on the back and said, “You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ خَرَجَ زَيْدُ بْنُ صُوحَانَ الْعَبْدِيُّ وَسَلْمَانُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ الْبَاهِلِيُّ، وَالصُّبَيُّ بْنُ مَعْبَدٍ ⦗ص: 99⦘ التَّغْلِبِيُّ، يُرِيدُونَ الْحَجَّ فِي زَمَنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، فَأَهَلَّ زَيْدٌ وَسَلْمَانُ بِالْحَجِّ وَحْدَهُ، وَأَهَلَّ الصُّبَيُّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ وَالْحَجِّ، فَقَالَا لَهُ: وَيْحَكَ تَمَتَّعُ وَقَدْ نَهَى عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ؟ وَاللَّهِ لَأَنْتَ أَضَلُّ مِنْ بَعِيرَكِ، فَقَالَ الصُّبَيُّ: نَقْدُمُ عَلَى عُمَرَ وَتَقْدُمُونَ. فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ الصُّبَيُّ مَكَّةَ طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ لِعُمْرَتِهِ، وَبَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، ثُمَّ عَادَ وَهُوَ حَرَامٌ، لَمْ يَحِلَّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، فَطَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَسَعَى بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ لِحَجَّتِهِ، ثُمَّ أَقَامَ حَرَامًا لَمْ يَحِلَّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، حَتَّى أَتَى عَرَفَاتٍ فَفَرَغَ مِنْ حَجَّتِهِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ أَهْرَاقَ دَمًا لِتَمَتُّعِهِ، فَلَمَّا صَدَرُوا، مَرُّوا بِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، فَقَالَ زَيْدُ بْنُ صُوحَانَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، إِنَّكَ قَدْ نَهَيْتَ عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ، وَإِنَّ الصُّبَيَّ قَدْ تَمَتَّعَ. فَقَالَ: أَصَنَعْتَ يَا صُبَيُّ مَاذَا؟ قَالَ: أَهْلَلْتُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ وَالْحَجِّ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمْتُ مَكَّةَ طُفْتُ بِالْبَيْتِ، وَالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ لِعُمْرَتِي، ثُمَّ عُدْتُ فَطُفْتُ بِالْبَيْتِ وَبِالصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ لِحَجَّتِي، ثُمَّ أَقَمْتُ حَرَامًا حَتَّى كَانَ يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ، فَأَهْرَقْتُ دَمًا لِمُتْعَتِي، ثُمَّ أَحْلَلْتُ. قَالَ: فَضَرَبَ عُمَرُ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ، قَالَ: «هُدِيتَ لِسُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ»

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said Zayd ibn Suhan al-Abdi, Salman ibn Rabi‘ah al-Bahili, and al-Subayy ibn Ma‘bad al-Taghlibi set out to perform Hajj during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ. Zayd and Salman entered ihram for Hajj alone, while al-Subayy entered ihram for both Umrah and Hajj. They said to him, “Woe to you! You are combining Umrah and Hajj even though Umar has forbidden tamattu‘ in Hajj? By God, you are more misguided than your camel!” Al-Subayy replied, “We will go to Umar, and you will go to him too.” When al-Subayy reached Mecca, he circumambulated the House for his Umrah and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah. He then returned still in ihram, with nothing having become lawful to him. He circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for his Hajj, then remained in ihram until he reached Arafat and completed his Hajj. On the Day of Sacrifice he offered a sacrifice for his tamattu‘. When they departed, they passed Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ. Zayd ibn Suhan said, “Commander of the Faithful, you forbade tamattu‘, yet al-Subayy has performed it.” Umar asked, “What exactly did you do, al-Subayy?” He replied, “I entered ihram for Umrah and Hajj. When I reached Mecca, I circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for my Umrah. Then I returned and circumambulated the House and performed sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for my Hajj. I remained in ihram until the Day of Sacrifice, when I offered a sacrifice for my tamattu‘ and then exited ihram.” Umar patted him on the back and said, “You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said When you perform Hajj: “When you perform Hajj, do not omit qiran (combining Umrah and Hajj). If you perform Umrah separately, your Umrah is Kufan—your journey and expenses are for it—while your Hajj is Meccan. But if you enter ihram for both together, your Umrah is Kufan and your Hajj is Kufan, and your talbiyah is for both together. Perform a separate tawaf of the House for each and a separate sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for each.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Ibrahim, from Abu Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he said "When you enter ihram: “When you enter ihram for both together—Umrah and Hajj—perform a separate tawaf of the House for each and a separate sa‘i between Safa and Marwah for each.” Mansur said: “I met Mujahid while he was giving people the ruling that one tawaf sufficed for a person combining the rites. When I related Ali’s report to him, he said, ‘Had I heard this report, I would have ruled only for two tawafs. From today onward, I will issue rulings on that basis alone.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ الْمُعْتَمِرِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي نَصْرٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَهْلَلْتَ بِهِمَا جَمِيعًا - بِالْعُمْرَةِ وَالْحَجِّ - فَطُفْ لَهُمَا بِالْبَيْتِ طَوَافَيْنِ، وَاسْعَ لَهُمَا بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ سَعْيَيْنِ» ⦗ص: 101⦘ . قَالَ مَنْصُورٌ: فَلَقِيتُ مُجَاهِدًا وَهُوَ يُفْتِي النَّاسَ بِطَوَافٍ وَاحِدٍ إِذَا قَرَنَ، فَلَمَّا حَدَّثْتُهُ الْحَدِيثَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، قَالَ: لَوْ كُنْتُ سَمِعْتُ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ لَمْ أُفْتِ إِلَّا بِطَوَافَيْنِ، فَأَمَّا بَعْدَ الْيَوْمِ فَإِنِّي لَا أُفْتِي إِلَّا بِهِمَا

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man enters ihram for both Hajj and Umrah together, and he is harmed in his head or catches game, he must offer expiation for each of them.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَحْرَمَ الرَّجُلُ بِحَجَّةٍ وَعُمْرَةٍ جَمِيعًا، فَأَصَابَهُ أَذًى فِي رَأْسِهِ، أَوْ أَصَابَ صَيْدًا، فَعَلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا كَفَّارَةٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that the Prophet, ﷺ, performed four Umrahs and one Hajj, combining one of his four Umrahs with it.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the *qarin*: “He performs two tawafs and two sa‘i performances between Safa and Marwah, beginning with the Umrah tawaf. He said, ‘Consider: if he entered ihram for each rite separately, would he not perform a tawaf and sa‘i for each—two of each? Why, when he combines them, should he omit one tawaf and one sa‘i?’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ " قَالَ فِي الْقَارِنِ: يَطُوفُ طَوَافَيْنِ، وَيَسْعَى سَعْيَيْنِ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، يَبْدَأُ بِطَوَافِ الْعُمْرَةِ فِي ذَلِكَ، وَقَالَ: أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَهَلَّ بِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا، أَلَمْ يَكُنْ يَطُوفُ لَهُمَا طَوَافَيْنِ، وَيَسْعَى سَعْيَيْنِ؟ فَمَا شَأْنُهُ إِذَا جَمَعَهُمَا أَلْغَى طَوَافًا وَسَعْيًا "
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ " قَالَ فِي الْقَارِنِ: يَطُوفُ طَوَافَيْنِ، وَيَسْعَى سَعْيَيْنِ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، يَبْدَأُ بِطَوَافِ الْعُمْرَةِ فِي ذَلِكَ، وَقَالَ: أَرَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَهَلَّ بِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى وَجْهِهَا، أَلَمْ يَكُنْ يَطُوفُ لَهُمَا طَوَافَيْنِ، وَيَسْعَى سَعْيَيْنِ؟ فَمَا شَأْنُهُ إِذَا جَمَعَهُمَا أَلْغَى طَوَافًا وَسَعْيًا "
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the *qarin*: He performs two circuits of *tawaf* and two circuits of *sa‘y* between al-Safa and al-Marwah, beginning with the *tawaf* of *‘umrah* in that. He said: Do you not see that if he entered into ihram for each of them separately, would he not perform two circuits of *tawaf* and two circuits of *sa‘y* for them? So why, when he combines them, should one *tawaf* and one *sa‘y* be omitted?

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When you enter ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj and you are not from the people of Makkah, then remain until you perform Hajj, you are a mutamatti’, and you must offer what is feasible from the sacrificial animal. Whoever does not find one must fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family. The three days of fasting during Hajj should end on the Day of Arafah. If he enters ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj, then returns to his family, and then enters ihram for Hajj in that same year, he is not a mutamatti’ and no sacrificial animal is required of him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَحْرَمْتَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ فِي أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ، وَأَنْتَ لَسْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ، ثُمَّ أَقَمْتَ حَتَّى تَحُجَّ، فَأَنْتَ مُتَمَتِّعٌ، وَعَلَيْكَ مَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ، فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ، وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ، وَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ، آخِرُهَا يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ، وَإِنْ هُوَ أَهَلَّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ فِي أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ، ثُمَّ أَهَلَّ مِنْ عَامِهِ ذَلِكَ لِحَجٍّ، لَمْ يَكُنْ مُتَمَتِّعًا، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ هَدْيٌ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَحْرَمْتَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ فِي أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ، وَأَنْتَ لَسْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ، ثُمَّ أَقَمْتَ حَتَّى تَحُجَّ، فَأَنْتَ مُتَمَتِّعٌ، وَعَلَيْكَ مَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ، فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ، وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ، وَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ، آخِرُهَا يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ، وَإِنْ هُوَ أَهَلَّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ فِي أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ، ثُمَّ أَهَلَّ مِنْ عَامِهِ ذَلِكَ لِحَجٍّ، لَمْ يَكُنْ مُتَمَتِّعًا، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ هَدْيٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man enters into the state of ihram for Umrah outside the months of Hajj, then performs its tawaf during the months of Hajj, and then remains until he performs Hajj in that same year, he is a mutamatti’.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from Abu Yusuf from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the pilgrim performing Tamattu‘ who cannot find an offering: He should borrow money and buy an offering. If he cannot find one, he should sell his lower garment and buy an offering with it.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding a man who enters into the state of *ihram* for Umrah during the months of Hajj. He said: “When he reaches Mecca, he circumambulates the House and performs sa‘i between Safa and Marwah, then shortens his hair and exits ihram. He remains out of ihram, circumambulating the House as he wishes, until the Day of Tarwiyah. Then he enters ihram for Hajj, circumambulates the House for Hajj and performs sa‘i between Safa and Marwah, then goes to Arafat. An offering as he can afford is due from him.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Aisha, ؓ, that she entered Mecca while performing Tamattu‘ and she was menstruating. The Prophet, ﷺ, ordered her to abandon her Umrah and start Hajj instead. When she completed her Hajj, he ordered her to depart. She said "O Prophet of God, the people are returning with both Hajj and Umrah, while I return with only Hajj?" So the Prophet, ﷺ, ordered Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, ؓ, and said: "Take her to al-Tan‘im, let her enter into Ihram for Umrah, then let her complete it, then hurry back to me, for I will be waiting for you at Batn al-Aqabah."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the one prevented (from completing the pilgrimage) who enters ihram for Umrah, Hajj, or both together, then is struck by illness or another obstacle beyond his control that prevents him from reaching the House: “He may remain there in ihram or return to his family if he wishes, but he must not exit ihram. He then sends an offering, or its value, if he entered ihram for Hajj alone or Umrah alone. If he entered ihram for both together, he sends two offerings, or their value. He agrees with his companions on the day they will slaughter the offering. When that day comes, he exits ihram. If he entered ihram for Umrah alone, he must perform another Umrah in its place; if he entered ihram for Hajj alone, he must perform an Umrah and a Hajj; and if he entered ihram for both together, he must perform two Umrahs and a Hajj.” Hammad said: “I asked Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and he did not disagree with Ibrahim on any matter of Hajj.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْمُحْصِرِ الَّذِي يُهِلُّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ، أَوْ بِالْحَجِّ، أَوْ بِهِمَا جَمِيعًا، ثُمَّ يُصِيبُهُ مَرَضٌ، أَوْ أَمْرٌ يَحْبِسُهُ، مِمَّا لَا يَمْلِكُهُ عَنِ الْبَيْتِ: «فَلْيُقِمْ مَكَانَهُ ذَلِكَ حَرَامًا، أَوْ لِيَرْجِعْ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ إِنْ شَاءَ، وَلَكِنْ لَا يَحِلُّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ بِهَدْيٍ، أَوْ بِثَمَنِ هَدْيٍ، إِنْ كَانَ أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ وَحْدَهُ أَوِ الْعُمْرَةِ وَحْدَهَا، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَهَلَّ بِهِمَا جَمِيعًا، بَعَثَ بِهَدْيَيْنِ أَوْ بِثَمَنِ هَدْيَيْنِ، ثُمَّ وَاعَدَ أَصْحَابَهُ الْيَوْمَ الَّذِي يَنْحَرُ فِيهِ الْهَدْيَ، فَإِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ حَلَّ، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَهَلَّ بِالْعُمْرَةِ وَحْدَهَا، فَعَلَيْهِ عُمْرَةٌ مَكَانَ عُمْرَتِهِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ وَحْدَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ عُمْرَةٌ وَحَجَّةٌ، وَإِنْ كَانَ أَهَلَّ بِهِمَا جَمِيعًا فَعَلَيْهِ عُمْرَتَانِ وَحَجَّةٌ» . قَالَ حَمَّادٌ: وَسَأَلْتُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ جُبَيْرٍ، فَلَمْ يُخَالِفْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْحَجِّ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the one prevented (from completing Hajj or Umrah) who has entered ihram for Umrah, or for Hajj, or for both together, then is afflicted by illness or something that detains him, which he cannot control from reaching the House: "Let him remain in that state of ihram, or return to his family if he wishes, but he must not exit ihram in any way. Then he sends a sacrificial animal, or its value, if he entered ihram for Hajj alone or Umrah alone. If he entered ihram for both together, he sends two sacrificial animals or the value of two. Then he appoints a day with his companions for when the sacrificial animal will be slaughtered. On that day, he exits ihram. If he entered ihram for Umrah alone, he must perform Umrah in place of his Umrah. If he entered ihram for Hajj alone, he must perform Umrah and Hajj. If he entered ihram for both together, he must perform two Umrahs and one Hajj." Hammad said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he did not disagree with Ibrahim on any matter concerning Hajj.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad, who said I asked Ata ibn Abi Rabah about a man prevented from completing Umrah: “What should he do?” I was about to ask him, “What if he is prevented while in ihram for Hajj?” and then ask, “What if he is prevented while combining Hajj and Umrah?” Regarding the man prevented during Umrah, he said: “If he wishes, he may offer a sacrifice; if he wishes, he may exit ihram without an offering.” Hammad said: “When he gave that mistaken answer, I left the matter with him. I then asked Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and he gave the same answer as Ibrahim.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad, who said I asked Ata ibn Abi Rabah about a man who is prevented from completing his Umrah—what should he do? I intended to say: If he is prevented while in the state of Ihram for Hajj, then I would ask him. And if he is prevented while in the state of Qiran, he said: Regarding the one prevented from completing his Umrah, Ata said, "If he wishes, he may offer a sacrificial animal, and if he wishes, he may exit Ihram without offering one." Hammad said: When he gave this answer, I left him. I then asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he gave the same answer as Ibrahim.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abd al-Karim that he said The first matter in which Ali and Uthman, ؓ, differed concerned partridges that had been brought to them while they were both in ihram. Uthman ate, but Ali did not. Uthman said to him, “You only wanted to oppose me; if I had not eaten, you would have eaten.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ أَوَّلُ مَا اخْتَلَفَ عَلِيٌّ وَعُثْمَانُ رضي الله عنهما فِي يَعَاقِيبَ أُتِيَ بِهَا، وَهُمَا مُحْرِمَانِ، فَأَكَلَ عُثْمَانُ وَلَمْ يَأْكُلْ عَلِيٌّ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُثْمَانُ: «مَا أَرَدْتَ إِلَّا خِلَافِي، لَوْ لَمْ آكُلْ لَأَكَلْتَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from al-Salt ibn Jubayr from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that Ibn Amir gifted Ibn Umar—while he was in Mecca—ostrich eggs and two live gazelles. Ibn Umar did not accept any of it and said , "Why did you not slaughter them before bringing them into the Sacred Precinct?" He also said, "They were gifted to us as long as they were safe."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ الصَّلْتِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّ ابْنَ عَامِرٍ أَهْدَى لِابْنِ عُمَرَ وَهُوَ بِمَكَّةَ ⦗ص: 105⦘ بَيْضَ نَعَامٍ وَظَبْيَيْنِ حَيَّيْنِ، فَلَمْ يَقْبَلْ شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَقَالَ «هَلَّا ذَبَحْتَهُمَا قَبْلَ أَنْ تُدْخِلَهُمَا الْحَرَمَ؟» وَقَالَ: أَهْدَاهُمَا لَنَا آمَنَ مَا كَانَا "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he said If you send a dog in the Sacred Precinct and it catches game from the non-Sacred area, you must offer expiation. And if you send it in the non-Sacred area and it catches game in the Sacred Precinct, you must offer expiation.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said Ka'b set out with a group of his companions intending to perform Hajj. On the way, they were given game meat that had been hunted by someone not in ihram, while they themselves were in ihram. Ka‘b said to his wife in the Roman language, “Prepare it and make it well, then bring it.” When she brought it, he told his companions, “Eat.” They refused. At evening they sat warming themselves by their fire, and a locust fell among them. Forgetting that he was in ihram, Ka‘b picked it up and threw it into the fire. His companions said, “Game meat by day, and a locust by night!” He gave a dirham in charity as expiation for the locust. When they came before Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and told him what had happened, Umar asked Ka‘b, “What did you do?” He replied, “I ate, but they did not.” Umar said, “Had you not eaten, you would not have understood.” He asked, “And what did you do about the locust?” Ka‘b replied, “I gave a dirham in charity.” Umar exclaimed, “Well done, well done! You people of Hims have plenty of dirhams. A date is better than a locust.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ: خَرَجَ كَعْبٌ فِي رَهْطٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ يُرِيدُونَ الْحَجَّ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانُوا بِبَعْضِ الطَّرِيقِ أُهْدِيَ لَهُمْ لَحْمُ صَيْدٍ صَادَهُ حَلَالٌ وَقَدْ أَحْرَمُوا، فَقَالَ كَعْبٌ لِامْرَأَتِهِ بِالرُّومِيَّةِ: اصْنَعِيهِ فَاجْبِدِي صَنْعَتَهُ، ثُمَّ ائْتِ بِهِ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْ بِهِ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ: كُلُوا، فَأَبَوْا أَنْ يَأْكُلُوا، فَلَمَّا أَمْسَوْا قَعَدُوا يَصْطَلُونَ عَلَى نَارٍ لَهُمْ، فَوَقَعَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ جَرَادَةٌ، فَأَخَذَهَا وَهُوَ نَاسٍ لِإِحْرَامِهِ، فَأَلْقَاهَا فِي النَّارِ، فَقَالَ أَصْحَابُهُ: لَحْمُ صَيْدٍ بِالنَّهَارِ، وَجَرَادَةٌ بِاللَّيْلِ. فَتَصَدَّقَ بِدِرْهَمٍ لِكَفَّارَةِ ⦗ص: 106⦘ الْجَرَادَةِ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمُوا عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، فَقَصُّوا عَلَيْهِ الْقِصَّةَ، فَقَالَ: صَنَعْتَ مَاذَا؟ قَالَ: أَكَلْتُ وَلَمْ يَأْكُلُوا، قَالَ: لَوْ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ لَمْ تَفْقَهْ، قَالَ: وَصَنَعْتَ فِي الْجَرَادَةِ مَاذَا؟ قَالَ: صَنَعْتُ أَنْ تَصَدَّقْتُ بِدِرْهَمٍ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ: «بَخٍ بَخٍ، إِنَّكُمْ يَا أَهْلَ حِمْصَ كَثِيرٌ دَرَاهِمُكُمْ، تَمْرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ جَرَادَةٍ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said Ka'b set out with a group of his companions intending to perform Hajj. When they were on the way, some game meat was gifted to them, which had been hunted by someone who was in a state of non-consecration, while they were in a state of ihram. Ka'b said to his Roman wife, "Prepare it, and do it well, then bring it." When she brought it, he said to his companions, "Eat." But they refused to eat. When evening came, they sat warming themselves by their fire, and a locust fell upon them. Ka'b took it, forgetting his ihram, and threw it into the fire. His companions said, "Game meat by day, and a locust by night!" So he gave a dirham in charity as expiation for the locust. When they came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, they related the story to him. He asked, "What did you do?" Ka'b replied, "I ate, but they did not." Umar said, "Had you not eaten, you would not have understood." Then he asked, "And what did you do about the locust?" Ka'b replied, "I gave a dirham in charity." Umar said, "Well done! You people of Hims, your dirhams are plentiful. A date is better than a locust."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Salamah, from a man of the family of Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, from Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, who said I passed by the people of Bahrain and they asked me about game meat hunted by someone not in ihram: “May a pilgrim in ihram eat it?” I told them that it was permissible, though I still had some doubt about it. I then came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he asked me about the matter. I told him what I had ruled. He said, “Had you said anything else, I would not have allowed you to issue rulings between people while I remained alive.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ آلِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضي الله عنه قَالَ مَرَرْتُ بِأَهْلِ الْبَحْرَيْنِ فَسَأَلُونِي عَنْ لَحْمِ الصَّيْدِ يَصِيدُهُ الْحَلَالُ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لِلْمُحْرِمِ أَنْ يَأْكُلَهُ؟ ⦗ص: 108⦘ قَالَ: فَأَفْتَيْتُهُمْ بِأَكْلِهِ وَفِي نَفْسِي مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، فَقَدِمْتُ عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه فَسَأَلَنِي عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِالَّذِي قُلْتُ، فَقَالَ: «لَوْ قُلْتَ غَيْرَ هَذَا مَا أَفْتَيْتَ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ مَا بَقِيتُ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Salamah, from a man of the family of Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, from Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, who said I passed by the people of Bahrain and they asked me about the meat of game hunted by a non-pilgrim—is it lawful for one in ihram to eat it? I gave them a fatwa permitting it, though I had some doubt in my heart. Then I came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he asked me about that. I told him what I had said, and he replied: Had you said anything else, I would not have let you give fatwas between two people as long as I lived.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Nafi‘ from Ibn ‘Umar, ؓ, that he said The pilgrim in ihram may kill mice, scorpions, kites, vicious dogs, and snakes, except al-jann, a small, slender house snake.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the expiation for hunting: When a pilgrim in ihram kills game, the ruler should assess the game’s value in dirhams in the land where it was killed. Then he should consider: if the dirhams reach the price of a sacrificial animal, he orders him to buy one with them. If it does not reach the price of a sacrificial animal, he buys food with them and gives it in charity—half a sa‘ of wheat to each poor person. If he has no food, he is ruled to fast one day for each poor person’s share of food. This is according to the word of God the Exalted: “Let two just men among you judge it” until the end of the verse.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Qays, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, who said While I was sitting with Ibn Abbas, ؓ, a man came to him and said, "I hunted a gazelle while I was in the state of ihram." Ibn Abbas said, "I and Abu Bakr judge that you must offer a sheep as expiation." Then another man came to him and said, "I have completed my rites except for the tawaf." He said, "Go and perform the tawaf, then return to me." The man returned and said, "I have performed the tawaf around the House." He said, "Go and resume your actions."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Malik, from his father, who said We set out as pilgrims until we reached Rabadhah, where we saw a tent. We asked, “What is this?” They said, “It is the tent of Abu Dharr, ؓ.” We went to him, and he lifted one side of the tent and asked, “Where have you come from?” We said, “Iraq.” He asked, “Where are you headed?” We said, “We intend to go to the House.” He said, “By God, is that the only reason you have set out?” We swore that it was. He said, “When you have finished, resume your work.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ خَرَجْنَا حُجَّاجًا حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا رَبَذَةَ إِذْ رُفِعَ لَنَا خِبَاءٌ، فَقُلْنَا: مَا هَذَا؟ قَالَ: خِبَاءُ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رضي الله عنه، فَأَتَيْنَاهُ فَرَفَعَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ جَانِبَ الْخِبَاءِ فَقَالَ: «مِنْ أَيْنَ أَقْبَلَ الْقَوْمُ؟» قَالَ: فَقُلْنَا مِنَ الْعِرَاقِ. قَالَ: «وَأَيْنَ تُرِيدُونَ؟» قَالَ: قُلْنَا نُرِيدُ الْبَيْتَ. قَالَ: «فَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَخْرَجَكُمْ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ؟» قَالَ: فَحَلَفْنَا لَهُ، فَقَالَ: «إِذَا فَرَغْتُمْ فَاسْتَأْنِفُوا الْعَمَلَ»

We asked, "What is this?" It was said, "The tent of Abu Dharr, ؓ." So we went to him, and Abu Dharr lifted the side of the tent and asked, "Where have the people come from?" We said, "From Iraq." records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Mansur from Ibrahim from Aisha that her husband had offered that her husband had set out a voluntary sacrificial animal, but it became incapacitated. He slaughtered it, dipped his sandal in its blood, struck its side with the sandal, and left it. Her aunt asked Aisha, ؓ, about this. She replied, “I would prefer that it be eaten rather than left for wild beasts.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, regarding the saying of God the Exalted: *"But whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin on him"*—he is free from sin—*"and whoever stays on, there is no sin on him"*—he is free from sin.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Aisha, ؓ, that she was asked about a pilgrim who died: what should be done with him? She said Do with him what you do with your dead, for when he died, his state of ihram ended.

records.text_en: In the saying of God the Exalted: *"Whoever undertakes the duty of Hajj therein, let there be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor wrangling in the Hajj."* [Al-Baqarah: 197], he said "Obscenity" refers to sexual intercourse, "wickedness" refers to sins, and "wrangling" refers to saying, "No, by God," and "Yes, by God."
records.text_ar: وَفِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: {فَمَنْ فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ} [البقرة: 197] قَالَ الرَّفَثُ ⦗ص: 113⦘ : الْجِمَاعُ، وَالْفُسُوقُ: الْمَعَاصِي وَالْجِدَالُ قَوْلُكَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ، بَلَى وَاللَّهِ "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Jahm, who said I saw Ibn Umar, ؓ, circumambulate the House after the morning prayer seven times, then he departed and did not pray until the sun had risen and brightened, then he prayed two rak'ahs.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Yazid Abu Khalid, from an old woman of the Atik tribe, from Aisha, ؓ, that she said "There is no harm in performing Umrah in any of the months of the year you wish, except for five or four days of the year: the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashriq."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ يَزِيدَ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، عَنْ عَجُوزٍ مِنَ الْعَتِيكِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ " لَا بَأْسَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ فِي أَيِّ أَشْهُرِ السَّنَةِ شِئْتَ، مَا خَلَا خَمْسَةَ أَيَّامٍ أَوْ أَرْبَعَةً مِنَ السَّنَةِ: يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ، وَيَوْمَ النَّحْرِ، وَأَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ "

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, , ؓ, who said: “A man said to me, ‘Abu Abd al-Rahman, I have seen you do four things.’ I asked, ‘What are they?’ He said, ‘When you intended to enter ihram, I saw you mount your camel and face the qiblah; you entered ihram when your camel set off carrying you. When you circumambulate the House, you do not pass the Yemeni Corner without touching it. I saw you dye your beard yellow, and perform ablution while wearing tanned-leather sandals with the hair removed.’ Ibn Umar replied, ‘I saw the Messenger of God, ﷺ, do all of these things.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما قَالَ قَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، رَأَيْتُكَ تَصْنَعُ أَرْبَعَ خِصَالٍ، قَالَ: «مَا هُنَّ؟» قَالَ: رَأَيْتُكَ حِينَ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُحْرِمَ رَكِبْتَ رَاحِلَتَكَ ثُمَّ اسْتَقْبَلْتَ الْقِبْلَةَ فَأَحْرَمَتْ حِينَ انْبَعَثَ بِكَ بَعِيرُكَ، وَرَأَيْتُكَ إِذَا طُفْتَ بِالْبَيْتِ لَمْ تَجُزِ الرُّكْنَ الْيَمَانِيَّ حَتَّى تَسْتَلِمَهُ، وَرَأَيْتُكَ تُلَوِّنُ لِحْيَتَكَ بِالصُّفْرَةِ، وَرَأَيْتُكَ تَوَضَّأُ فِي النِّعَالِ السِّبْتِيَّةِ. فَقَالَ: «إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ كُلَّهُ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, who said A man said, "O Abu Abdurrahman, I have seen you do four things." He said, "What are they?" The man said, "I saw you when you intended to enter ihram, you mounted your camel, then faced the qiblah and entered ihram when your camel set off. I saw you when you performed tawaf around the House, you did not pass the Yemeni Corner without touching it. I saw you dye your beard yellow. And I saw you perform ablution while wearing soft leather sandals." He said, "I saw the Messenger of God, ﷺ, do all of that."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said to the Black Stone: "I know that you are a stone, you can neither harm nor benefit. Had I not seen the Messenger of God, ﷺ, kiss you, I would not have kissed you."
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه قَالَ لِلْحَجَرِ: «إِنِّي لَأَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ حَجَرٌ، مِثْلُكَ لَا يَضُرُّ وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ⦗ص: 115⦘ ، وَلَوْلَا أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَبَّلَكَ لَمَا قَبَّلْتُكَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said "Whoever stipulates a condition and whoever does not stipulate are the same."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the one who has intercourse with his wife while both are in ihram: "They should continue on their way and each of them must offer a sacrificial animal until they complete their rites. They must also perform Hajj the following year, and they must separate when they enter ihram."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said If a pilgrim in ihram kisses out of desire or touches, he must offer a sacrificial animal.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said Whenever I came to the Yemeni Corner, I always found Jibril there.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Sawwar from Abu Hadir from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, was cupped while he was fasting and in a state of ihram at Al-Qahah.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَوَّارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَاضِرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم احْتَجَمَ وَهُوَ ⦗ص: 116⦘ صَائِمٌ مُحْرِمٌ بِالْقَاحَةِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَوَّارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَاضِرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم احْتَجَمَ وَهُوَ ⦗ص: 116⦘ صَائِمٌ مُحْرِمٌ بِالْقَاحَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham that the Prophet, ﷺ, married Maymunah, ؓ, while he was in the state of ihram at Usfan.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَزَوَّجَ مَيْمُونَةَ رضي الله عنها وَهُوَ مُحْرِمٌ بِعُسْفَانَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “For men, shaving the head is better than shortening the hair; for women, shortening is better than shaving. The less hair a woman trims, the better.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الْحَلْقُ أَفْضَلُ لِلرِّجَالِ مِنَ التَّقْصِيرِ، وَالتَّقْصِيرُ أَفْضَلُ لِلنِّسَاءِ مِنَ الْحَلْقِ، وَمَا أَقَلَّتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مِنَ الْأَخْذِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الْحَلْقُ أَفْضَلُ لِلرِّجَالِ مِنَ التَّقْصِيرِ، وَالتَّقْصِيرُ أَفْضَلُ لِلنِّسَاءِ مِنَ الْحَلْقِ، وَمَا أَقَلَّتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مِنَ الْأَخْذِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said Shaving the head is better for men than trimming, and trimming is better for women than shaving, and whatever little the woman trims is better.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “Women do not perform ramal (brisk walking) during tawaf, nor walk briskly during sa‘i between Safa and Marwah.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ رَمَلٌ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَلَا سَعْيٌ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ رَمَلٌ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَلَا سَعْيٌ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Najih, from Abdullah ibn Amr, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said "God has made Mecca sacred, and He has forbidden the sale of its real estate and the taking of rent for its houses."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رضي الله عنهما، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 117⦘ أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ مَكَّةَ وَبَيْعَ رِبَاعِهَا وَأَخْذَ أُجُورِ بُيُوتِهَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رضي الله عنهما، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 117⦘ أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ مَكَّةَ وَبَيْعَ رِبَاعِهَا وَأَخْذَ أُجُورِ بُيُوتِهَا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Salim that it reached him: "Around the Ka'bah are the graves of three hundred prophets, and no prophet fled from his people except that he took refuge near it, residing there until he died."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ «أَنَّ حَوْلَ الْكَعْبَةِ قُبُورَ ثَلَاثِمِائَةِ نَبِيٍّ، وَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَهْرُبْ نَبِيٌّ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا لَاذَ بِهَا مُجَاوِرًا حَتَّى يَمُوتَ بِهَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ «أَنَّ حَوْلَ الْكَعْبَةِ قُبُورَ ثَلَاثِمِائَةِ نَبِيٍّ، وَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَهْرُبْ نَبِيٌّ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا لَاذَ بِهَا مُجَاوِرًا حَتَّى يَمُوتَ بِهَا»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “The Prophet, ﷺ, prayed four rak‘ahs inside the Ka‘bah.” I [Sa‘id ibn Jubayr] said to Ibn Umar, “Show me the place where he prayed.” Ibn Umar sent his son with me. It seemed I had looked down on the son, so he said, “Do not underestimate me; I am a valuable asset.” He then led me and showed me the place by the middle pillar, beneath the crossbeam.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْكَعْبَةِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ» ، قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: أَرِنِي الْمَكَانَ الَّذِي صَلَّى فِيهِ. قَالَ: فَبَعَثَ مَعِيَ ابْنَهُ، قَالَ: فَكَأَنِّي غَمَصْتُهُ، فَقَالَ: «لَا تَزْدَرِ بِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ صَالِحِ الْمَتَاعِ» ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ بِي فَأَرَانِي عِنْدَ الْأُسْطُوَانَةِ الْوُسْطَى تَحْتَ الْجِذْعَةِ

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who narrated to him from al-Hasan that the Prophet, ﷺ, circumambulated the House while ill, riding his mount and touching the corners with his hooked staff. He then prayed two rak‘ahs and called for al-Abbas, asking him for a drink. Al-Abbas asked, “Would you like the drink of the elite or the drink of the common people?” He replied, “No, the drink of the common people.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَهُوَ وَجِعٌ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ يَسْتَلِمُ الْأَرْكَانَ بِمِحْجَنِهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ دَعَا عَبَّاسًا فَسَأَلَهُ شَرَابًا، فَقَالَ أَمِنْ شَرَابِ الْخَاصَّةِ أَوْ مِنْ شَرَابِ الْعَامَّةِ؟ قَالَ: «لَا، بَلْ مِنْ شَرَابِ الْعَامَّةِ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who narrated to him from al-Hasan that the Prophet, ﷺ, performed Tawaf around the House while he was ill, riding his mount, touching the corners with his staff. Then he prayed two rak'ahs, then called for al-'Abbas and asked him for a drink. Al-'Abbas said "Is it from the drink of the elite or from the drink of the common people?" He said: "No, rather from the drink of the common people."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad that he said I was performing the circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah with Ikrimah. He said: I would ascend al-Safa and al-Marwah, but he would not ascend. He said: So I asked him, "Why do you not ascend?" He said, "This is how the Prophet, ﷺ, performed the circuits." Then I met Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him about that, and he said, "The wicked one lied. The Prophet, ﷺ, performed the circuits while ill around the House on his mount, touching the corners with his staff."

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ كُنْتُ أَطُوفُ أَنَا وَعِكْرِمَةُ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ. قَالَ: وَكُنْتُ أصْعَدُ عَلَى الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ، وَلَا يَصْعَدُ. قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: مَا لَكَ لَا تَصْعَدُ؟ قَالَ: هَكَذَا طَافَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم. فَلَقِيتُ سَعِيدَ بْنَ جُبَيْرٍ فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ: «كَذَبَ الْخَبِيثُ، طَافَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ شَاكٍ بِالْبَيْتِ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ يَسْتَلِمُ الْأَرْكَانَ بِمِحْجَنِهِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad
records.matn_en: that he said I was performing the circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah with Ikrimah. He said: I would ascend al-Safa and al-Marwah, but he would not ascend. He said: So I asked him, "Why do you not ascend?" He said, "This is how the Prophet, ﷺ, performed the circuits." Then I met Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him about that, and he said, "The wicked one lied. The Prophet, ﷺ, performed the circuits while ill around the House on his mount, touching the corners with his staff."
records.boundary_review_note: Hammad’s first-person account and the subsequent dialogue with Ikrimah and Sa’id ibn Jubayr form the transmitted content.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim : “If someone does not reach Jam‘ (Muzdalifah), he has missed Hajj.”

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا لَمْ يُدْرِكْ جَمْعًا فَقَدْ فَاتَهُ الْحَجُّ»

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s statement begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ,  who said: “While Umar was at Jam‘ (Muzdalifah), a man came and said, ‘Commander of the Faithful, I have just arrived, having entered ihram for Hajj.’ Umar asked him, ‘Have you gone to Arafat?’ He said, ‘No.’ Umar sent a man with him and said, ‘Take him to Arafat and have him stand there, then hurry back to me; I am holding the people here for you.’ In the morning Umar stood with the people and kept asking, ‘Has the man arrived?’ They said, ‘No.’ He continued holding the people until the man arrived. Then Umar departed from Muzdalifah, and the people departed with him.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه قَالَ بَيْنَمَا عُمَرُ بِجَمْعٍ إِذْ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، إِنِّي قَدِمْتُ السَّاعَةَ وَأَنَا مُهِلٌّ بِالْحَجِّ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: «أَتُهْدَى إِلَى عَرَفَاتٍ؟» قَالَ: لَا. فَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ رَجُلًا فَقَالَ: «انْطَلِقْ بِهِ إِلَى عَرَفَاتٍ وَلْيَقِفْ بِهَا، ثُمَّ الْعَجَلَ عَلَيَّ، فَإِنِّي حَابِسٌ النَّاسَ عَلَيْكَ» . فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه وَقَفَ بِالنَّاسِ، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَقُولُ: «هَلْ جَاءَ الرَّجُلُ؟» فَقَالُوا: لَا. فَلَمْ يَزَلْ حَابِسًا النَّاسَ حَتَّى جَاءَ، فَأَفَاضَ وَأَفَاضَ النَّاسُ مَعَهُ
