records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, who narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba, from 'Amir al-Ahwal, from 'Ata, from Ibn 'Abbas, ؓ, that he said: “Whoever swears to abstain from his wife for one, two, or three months—any period under four months—is not subject to the legal rule of īlāʾ.” Abu Hanifah also related something similar from him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: ثنا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَرُوبَةَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ الْأَحْوَلِ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ آلَى مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ شَهْرًا أَوْ شَهْرَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثًا مَا دُونَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِيلَاءٌ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ هَذَا
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: ثنا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَرُوبَةَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ الْأَحْوَلِ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ آلَى مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ شَهْرًا أَوْ شَهْرَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثًا مَا دُونَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِيلَاءٌ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ هَذَا
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, who narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba, from 'Amir al-Ahwal, from 'Ata, from Ibn 'Abbas, ؓ, that he said "Whoever swears to abstain from his wife for a month, two months, or three—less than four—then it is not considered a valid oath of abstention." Abu Hanifa also mentioned something similar from him.

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, who narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba, from 'Amir al-Ahwal, from 'Ata, from Ibn 'Abbas, ؓ, that he said: “Whoever swears to abstain from his wife for one, two, or three months—any period under four months—is not subject to the legal rule of īlāʾ.” Abu Hanifah also related something similar from him.
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: ثنا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَرُوبَةَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ الْأَحْوَلِ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما
records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ آلَى مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ شَهْرًا أَوْ شَهْرَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثًا مَا دُونَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِيلَاءٌ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ هَذَا
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, who narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aruba, from 'Amir al-Ahwal, from 'Ata, from Ibn 'Abbas, ؓ,

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who declared *zihar* against his wife, then divorced her, then married her again after her waiting period had ended. He said "The *zihar* remains as it is."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “A female slave who has borne her master a child (umm walad) cannot be used to fulfill the emancipation required for zihār expiation. Whoever pronounces zihār concerning his female slave has no expiation for it except to emancipate her.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تُجْزِئُ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ فِي الظِّهَارِ، وَالَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ لَا يُجْزِئُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا التَّحْرِيرُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تُجْزِئُ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ فِي الظِّهَارِ، وَالَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ لَا يُجْزِئُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا التَّحْرِيرُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "A mother of a child (from her master) does not suffice for expiation in *zihar*, and whoever performs *zihar* with his slave woman, nothing suffices for her except manumission."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تُجْزِئُ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ فِي الظِّهَارِ، وَالَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ لَا يُجْزِئُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا التَّحْرِيرُ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “A female slave who has borne her master a child (umm walad) cannot be used to fulfill the emancipation required for zihār expiation. Whoever pronounces zihār concerning his female slave has no expiation for it except to emancipate her.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تُجْزِئُ أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ فِي الظِّهَارِ، وَالَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ لَا يُجْزِئُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا التَّحْرِيرُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a man who performs *zihar* from his wife and then performs *zihar* again two more times: If he intended to make it more severe, then he must offer expiation for each *zihar*. But if he only intended his first *zihar*, then he must offer only one expiation. The same applies to an oath.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding the man who performs *zihar* against his wife then has intercourse with her before expiating: "He should seek forgiveness from God and not repeat it until he has expiated."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said: “If a man declares zihār against his wife three times, then if he intended a single declaration of zihār, only one expiation is due; but if he intended each statement as a separate declaration, three expiations are due.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا ظَاهَرَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَإِنْ عَنَى الظِّهَارَ وَحْدَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ كَفَّارَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، وَإِنْ عَنَى بِكُلِّ قَوْلٍ ظِهَارًا فَعَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثُ كَفَّارَاتٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا ظَاهَرَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَإِنْ عَنَى الظِّهَارَ وَحْدَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ كَفَّارَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، وَإِنْ عَنَى بِكُلِّ قَوْلٍ ظِهَارًا فَعَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثُ كَفَّارَاتٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said When a man declares *zihar* against his wife three times, if he intended *zihar* alone, then only one expiation is required upon him. But if he intended each statement as a separate *zihar*, then three expiations are required upon him.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the slave who performs *dhihar* from his wife: "He must fast two months; freeing a slave or feeding the poor will not suffice for him."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْعَبْدِ يُظَاهِرُ مِنِ امْرَأَتِهِ: «فَعَلَيْهِ صَوْمُ شَهْرَيْنِ لَا يُجْزِئُهُ تَحْرِيرٌ وَلَا طَعَامٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf narrated to us from Abu Jaz’ Nasr ibn Tarif, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, that he said: “Whoever wishes, I will enter into a mutual imprecation with him: may God’s curse be upon whichever of us is lying about there being no expiation for one who pronounces zihār against his female slave.” Abu Hanifah also related something similar from him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ قَالَ: ثنا أَبُو يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي جَزْءٍ نَصْرِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ شَاءَ بَاهَلْتُهُ أَنَّهُ لَا كَفَّارَةَ عَلَى الَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ قَالَ: ثنا أَبُو يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي جَزْءٍ نَصْرِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ شَاءَ ⦗ص: 152⦘ بَاهَلْتُهُ أَنَّهُ لَا كَفَّارَةَ عَلَى الَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf narrated to us from Abu Jaz’ Nasr ibn Tarif, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, that he said "Whoever wishes, I will invoke the curse of God upon them that there is no expiation for the one who performs *zihar* with his female slave." Abu Hanifah also mentioned something similar from him.
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ قَالَ: ثنا أَبُو يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي جَزْءٍ نَصْرِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ شَاءَ بَاهَلْتُهُ أَنَّهُ لَا كَفَّارَةَ عَلَى الَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ
records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf narrated to us from Abu Jaz’ Nasr ibn Tarif, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, that he said: “Whoever wishes, I will enter into a mutual imprecation with him: may God’s curse be upon whichever of us is lying about there being no expiation for one who pronounces zihār against his female slave.” Abu Hanifah also related something similar from him.
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ قَالَ: ثنا أَبُو يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِي جَزْءٍ نَصْرِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضي الله عنهما
records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ شَاءَ بَاهَلْتُهُ أَنَّهُ لَا كَفَّارَةَ عَلَى الَّذِي يُظَاهِرُ مِنْ أَمَتِهِ» وَذَكَرَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ عَنْهُ نَحْوَ ذَلِكَ
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abu Yusuf narrated to us from Abu Jaz’ Nasr ibn Tarif, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, ؓ,
records.matn_en: that he said: “Whoever wishes, I will enter into a mutual imprecation with him: may God’s curse be upon whichever of us is lying about there being no expiation for one who pronounces zihār against his female slave.” Abu Hanifah also related something similar from him.
records.boundary_review_note: This report has an outer route through Abu Yusuf rather than the usual father–Abu Hanifah chain; a separate similar report from Abu Hanifah is noted in the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said We complained about celibacy, so temporary marriage was made lawful for us three times, then the verse of marriage, waiting period, and inheritance abrogated it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «شَكَوْنَا الْعُزُوبَةَ، فَأُحِلَّتْ لَنَا الْمُتْعَةُ ثَلَاثًا قَطُّ، ثُمَّ نَسَخَتْهَا آيَةُ النِّكَاحِ وَالْعِدَّةِ وَالْمِيرَاثِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «شَكَوْنَا الْعُزُوبَةَ، فَأُحِلَّتْ لَنَا الْمُتْعَةُ ثَلَاثًا قَطُّ، ثُمَّ نَسَخَتْهَا آيَةُ النِّكَاحِ وَالْعِدَّةِ وَالْمِيرَاثِ»

records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ,
records.matn_en: that he said We complained about celibacy, so temporary marriage was made lawful for us three times, then the verse of marriage, waiting period, and inheritance abrogated it.
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Masud’s statement begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, who said The Prophet, ﷺ, forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and temporary marriage—temporary marriage with women—saying, "We were not fornicators."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما قَالَ «نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ لُحُومِ الْحُمُرِ الْأَهْلِيَّةِ أَوِ الْإِنْسِيَّةِ وَعَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ» : مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُسَافِحِينَ
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما قَالَ «نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ لُحُومِ الْحُمُرِ الْأَهْلِيَّةِ أَوِ الْإِنْسِيَّةِ وَعَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ» : مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُسَافِحِينَ

records.matn_en: who said The Prophet, ﷺ, forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and temporary marriage—temporary marriage with women—saying, "We were not fornicators."
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Umar’s report of the Prophetic prohibition and his explanatory phrase begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Yunus ibn Abdullah from Rabi' that the Prophet, ﷺ, forbade temporary marriage on the day of the conquest of Mecca.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ رَبِيعٍ: «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ رَبِيعٍ: «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Yunus ibn Abdullah from Rabi'
records.matn_en: that the Prophet, ﷺ, forbade temporary marriage on the day of the conquest of Mecca.
records.boundary_review_note: The Prophetic report begins matn after Rabi.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who reported to him from al-Zuhri, that he said The Prophet, ﷺ, forbade temporary marriage on the day of the Conquest of Mecca.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who reported to him from al-Zuhri, that he said The Prophet, ﷺ, forbade temporary marriage on the day of the Conquest of Mecca.

records.matn_ar: نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who reported to him from al-Zuhri, that he said
records.matn_en: The Prophet, ﷺ, forbade temporary marriage on the day of the Conquest of Mecca.
records.boundary_review_note: The route contains an unnamed intermediary before al-Zuhri; the Prophetic report begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who accuses his wife of adultery and then divorces her three times: “There is no liʿān between them, and he is not subject to the prescribed punishment.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَجُلٍ قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثُمَّ طَلَّقَهَا ثَلَاثًا قَالَ «لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمَا لِعَانٌ، وَلَا حَدَّ عَلَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَجُلٍ قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثُمَّ طَلَّقَهَا ثَلَاثًا قَالَ «لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمَا لِعَانٌ، وَلَا حَدَّ عَلَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who slanders his wife and then divorces her thrice: "There is no *li'an* between them, nor is there any *hadd* punishment upon him."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَجُلٍ قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثُمَّ طَلَّقَهَا ثَلَاثًا قَالَ «لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمَا لِعَانٌ، وَلَا حَدَّ عَلَيْهِ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who accuses his wife of adultery and then divorces her three times: “There is no liʿān between them, and he is not subject to the prescribed punishment.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ
records.matn_ar: فِي رَجُلٍ قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثُمَّ طَلَّقَهَا ثَلَاثًا قَالَ «لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُمَا لِعَانٌ، وَلَا حَدَّ عَلَيْهِ»

records.matn_en: regarding a man who accuses his wife of adultery and then divorces her three times: “There is no liʿān between them, and he is not subject to the prescribed punishment.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “If a man accuses his wife of adultery, they remain married unless they bring the matter before a judge. If they do, he performs liʿān (mutual imprecation) with her, and the child is attributed to its mother. Liʿān is one irrevocable divorce, and she is entitled to housing and maintenance for as long as she remains in her waiting period.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said If a man marries a woman during her waiting period and consummates the marriage, then accuses her of adultery, and they engage in the imprecation (liʿan), but he later learns of her waiting period, the imprecation is invalid, and no hadd punishment applies to him. He may propose to her once her waiting period from the first husband has ended. If he learns before the imprecation that she is in her waiting period, then no hadd punishment applies to him, nor is there any imprecation, and they must be separated. He remains a suitor for her once the waiting period from the first husband has ended.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said "If God had taken a covenant from a soul in the loins of a man, then poured it onto a smooth rock, God would certainly bring forth from it that very soul from which He took the covenant."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Kathir al-Asamm from Abu Dhira‘ from Ibn Umar, ؓ, regarding the words of the Exalted, “Come to your tillage however you will,” that he said , “If you wish, withdraw, and if you wish, do not withdraw.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said "There is no harm in coitus interruptus with a slave woman. As for a free woman, if she permits you, then practice coitus interruptus, but if she does not permit you, then do not."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، قَالَ «لَا بَأْسَ بِالْعَزْلِ عَنِ الْأَمَةِ، فَأَمَّا الْحُرَّةُ، فَإِنْ أَذِنَتْ لَكَ فَاعْزِلْ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْذَنْ لَكَ فَلَا تَعْزِلْ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said A judge among the Children of Israel perished, leaving behind a young man from among their scholars. They approached a man and asked him to sit as a judge, but he refused. Then, he was visited in his dream and asked, "What prevents you from sitting as a judge?" He replied, "I fear that I may be unjust." It was said to him, "Shall We place between you and injustice a sign—so-and-so—so that if you stand with him and he is taller than you, then you have been unjust?" He said, "In the morning, he sat as a judge and would send for that man, standing with him several times a day whenever something was unclear or he had doubt about it." One day, he stood with him, and the man was taller than him. So, he stepped down from the judiciary, grieved and distressed. He was then visited in his dream and asked, "You stepped down from the judiciary?" He replied, "I sent for the sign you placed between me and injustice, and when I stood with him, he was taller than me." It was said to him, "That was not from the injustice you feared. Rather, two disputing parties came before you, and you wished the right to be for one of them, so you ruled in his favor." He said, "Do you not see that I am unjust within myself before I even speak? I will never sit as a judge after this, ever."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَابِطٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ " هَلَكَ قَاضٍ لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَى فَتًى مِنْ عُلَمَائِهِمْ، فَأَتَوْا رَجُلًا فَسَأَلُوهُ أَنْ يَقْعُدَ عَلَى الْقَضَاءِ فَأَبَى عَلَيْهِمْ، فَأُتِيَ فِي مَنَامِهِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ: مَا يَمْنَعُكَ أَنْ تَقْعُدَ عَلَى الْقَضَاءِ؟ قَالَ: خِفْتُ أَنْ أَجُورَ، قَالَ: فَقِيلَ لَهُ: أَمَا نَجْعَلُ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ الْجَوْرِ عَلَمًا فُلَانًا، إِذَا قُمْتَ مَعَهُ فَكَانَ أَطْوَلَ مِنْكَ فَقَدْ جُرْتَ، قَالَ: فَأَصْبَحَ فَقَعَدَ عَلَى الْقَضَاءِ، وَكَانَ يُرْسِلُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلِ فَيَقُومُ مَعَهُ فِي الْيَوْمِ مِرَارًا إِذَا أَشْكَلَ عَلَيْهِ الشَّيْءُ أَوْ شَكَّ فِيهِ، قَالَ: فَقَامَ مَعَهُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ فَكَانَ أَطْوَلَ مِنْهُ، قَالَ: فَقَامَ عَنِ الْقَضَاءِ حَزِينًا خَبِيثَ النَّفْسِ، فَأُتِيَ فِي مَنَامِهِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ: قُمْتَ عَنِ الْقَضَاءِ، قَالَ: الْعَلَمُ الَّذِي جَعَلْتُمُوهُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقُمْتُ مَعَهُ، فَكَانَ أَطْوَلَ مِنِّي، قَالَ: فَقِيلَ لَهُ: أَمَا إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيْسَ مِنْ جُورٍ جُرْتَهُ، وَلَكِنَّهُ انْتَهَى إِلَيْكَ خَصْمَانِ فَأَحْبَبْتَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْحَقُّ لِأَحَدِهِمَا فَتَقْضِي لَهُ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ: أَلَا تَرَانِي أَجُورُ فِي نَفْسِي قَبْلَ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ، لَا أَقْعُدُ عَلَى الْقَضَاءِ بَعْدَهَا أَبَدًا "

One day, he stood with him, and the man was taller than him. So, he stepped down from the judiciary, grieved and distressed. He was then visited in his dream and asked, "You stepped down from the judiciary?" He replied, "I sent for the sign you placed between me and injustice, and when I stood with him, he was taller than me." It was said to him, "That was not from the injustice you feared. Rather, two disputing parties came before you, and you wished the right to be for one of them, so you ruled in his favor." He said, "Do you not see that I am unjust within myself before I even speak? I will never sit as a judge after this, ever."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar: Two men came to Shurayh disputing before him. One of them had lent his wall to the other, who placed a beam on it. The owner of the wall wanted to move his beam, so Shurayh said , "Move your beam away from your brother’s mount."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْأَقْمَرِ: أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ أَتَيَا شُرَيْحًا يَخْتَصِمَانِ إِلَيْهِ، وَقَدْ أَعَارَ أَحَدُهُمَا حَائِطَهُ فَوَضَعَ عَلَيْهِ جِذْعًا، فَأَرَادَ أَنْ يُحَوِّلَ جِذْعَهُ، فَقَالَ شُرَيْحٌ: «حَوِّلْ جِذْعَكَ عَنْ مَطِيَّةِ أَخِيكَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar, ؓ, ruled that a man from Banu Dhubyan who had killed a man from the people of al-Hirah should be handed over to the victim’s heir. Someone said to the heir, “Kill Hunayn.” He replied, “Not until anger comes; then I will kill him.” Later, when Umar learned that Hunayn was one of the people’s horsemen, he wrote that he wanted to ransom him.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said When witnesses testify against a woman for adultery, and one of them is her husband, she is stoned.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding a man who spends the night in another man’s house armed at night and is killed: If it is known that he is a wicked, corrupt man, his blood is forfeit. But if he is not of that sort, the killer must pay compensation.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet, ﷺ, was approached by Maʿiz ibn Malik, ؓ, who said, “This wretched man has committed adultery.” The Prophet turned him away. Maʿiz came again, and the Prophet turned him away; he came a third time, and the Prophet turned him away; then he came a fourth time. The Prophet asked Maʿiz’s people, “Do you notice anything wrong with his reason?” They said, “No.” So he ordered that Maʿiz be stoned. He was taken to a place with few stones. When death was slow to come, he ran toward a place with many stones, and the people followed him until they killed him. When the Prophet was told what had happened, he said, “Why did you not let him go?” Some people of Medina said, “Maʿiz is ruined and has ruined others,” while others said, “We hope his repentance will be accepted.” When this reached the Prophet, he said, “He made such a repentance that, if a multitude of people made it, it would be accepted from them.” His people then sought his body and spoke to the Prophet about it. He said, “Do for him what you do for your dead: shroud him and pray over him.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet, ﷺ, was approached by Ma'iz ibn Malik, ؓ, who said "The other has committed adultery." The Prophet turned him away. Then he came again, and he turned him away. Then he came a third time, and he turned him away. Then he came a fourth time, so the Prophet asked his people about him: "Do you find any defect in his reason?" They said: "No." So he ordered that he be stoned. He was brought to a land with few stones, and when death was slow in coming to him, he ran toward a land with many stones, and the people followed him until they killed him. When the Prophet, ﷺ, was informed of this, he said: "Why did you not leave his path?" Some of the people of Medina said: "Ma'iz is ruined and has ruined others." Others said: "We hope his repentance is accepted." This reached the Prophet, ﷺ, and he said: "He has repented a repentance that, if a whole nation repented with it, it would be accepted from them." Then his people desired his body, so they spoke to the Prophet, ﷺ, about it, and he said: "Do with him as you do with your dead—shroud him and pray over him."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a man when he dies: "Whatever is in the house of men's belongings belongs to the men, and whatever is of women's belongings belongs to the woman. As for what belongs to both men and women, it goes to the one who remains afterward, unless the other produces evidence. If he divorces, it is the same, except that what belongs to both women and men goes to the man because he is the owner of the house, and everything in the house belongs to him except what is of women's belongings. If they dispute and he does not divorce, it is the same."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, Bashir reported to us from Muhammad ibn Ali from his father from Ali, ؓ, that he would not hold the fuller, the goldsmith, or the weaver liable for compensation.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr that a tall, beautiful woman, dressed in fine clothes, came before Ibn Ziyad to complain about her husband’s maintenance and the harm he caused her. Ibn Ziyad summoned her husband, who arrived as a short, unattractive man. He said, “Ask her about this person: is he from the food I provide?” She said, “Yes. Are you holding a morsel over me?” He said, “Ask her about these clothes: are they from the clothing I provide?” She said, “Yes. Are you holding a rag over me?” He said, “Ask her about the child in her womb: is it mine?” She said, “Yes, and I wish it were in a dog’s womb.” He said, “Is a husband required to do anything beyond feeding, clothing, and impregnating her?” Ibn Ziyad said, “You have spoken the truth; that is what is required of him. Take her by the hand.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ: أَنَّ امْرَأَةً طَوِيلَةً جَمِيلَةً، عَلَيْهَا ثِيَابٌ جِيَادٌ، تَقَدَّمَتْ إِلَى ابْنِ زِيَادٍ تَشْكُو زَوْجَهَا فِي النَّفَقَةِ وَإِضْرَارِهِ بِهَا، فَدَعَا زَوْجَهَا، فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ قَصِيرٌ قَلِيلٌ دَمِيمٌ، فَقَالَ سَلْهَا عَنْ هَذَا الشَّخْصِ أَمِنْ طَعَامِي هُوَ؟ قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، أَفَتَمُنُّ عَلَيَّ بِكِسْرَةٍ قَالَ: فَسَلْهَا عَنْ هَذِهِ الثِّيَابِ أَمِنْ كُسْوَتِي؟ قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، أَتَمُنُّ عَلَيَّ بِخِرْقَةٍ قَالَ: فَسَلْهَا عَمَّا فِي بَطْنِهَا أَمِنِّي هُوَ؟ قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، وَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّهُ فِي بَطْنِ كَلْبٍ، قَالَ: فَمَا يُطْلَبُ مِنَ الزَّوْجِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُطْعِمَ وَيَكْسُوَ وَيُحْبِلَ؟ فَقَالَ ابْنُ زِيَادٍ: «صَدَقْتَ ذَلِكَ يُطْلَبُ مِنْهُ خُذْ بِيَدِهَا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr that a tall, beautiful woman wearing fine clothes came forward to Ibn Ziyad to complain about her husband regarding maintenance and his harm to her. He summoned her husband, and a short, scant, and unattractive man came. He said , "Ask her about this person—is he from my food?" She said, "Yes. Do you boast to me over a morsel?" He said, "Ask her about these clothes—are they from my clothing?" She said, "Yes. Do you boast to me over a rag?" He said, "Ask her about what is in her belly—is it from me?" She said, "Yes, and I wish it were in a dog’s belly." He said, "Is anything required from the husband except that he feeds, clothes, and impregnates?" Ibn Ziyad said, "You have spoken the truth. That is all that is required of him. Take her by the hand."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said regarding a woman in labor: “When labor pains strike her, she is like a sick person in the legal dispositions she makes.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «قَالَ فِي الْمَرْأَةِ إِذَا ضَرَبَهَا الطَّلْقُ فَهِيَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْمَرِيضِ فِيمَا صَنَعَتْ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Harithah, ؓ, that Zayd ibn Harithah arrived with enslaved people from Yemen. Needing funds for expenses, he sold one young male slave. When he came to the Prophet, ﷺ, the boy’s mother was distraught. records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Harithah, ؓ, that he arrived with slaves from Yemen and needed expenses, so he sold one of the young male slaves. When he came to the Prophet, ﷺ, he saw the mother of the young slave distressed and said "Why do I see her distressed?" Zayd said: We needed expenses, so we sold her son. He said: "Go back and return him." So he went back and returned him. Zayd said: We and the family of Abbas dispute over his allegiance, they say: The Prophet, ﷺ, freed him, so his allegiance is ours. And we say: He gifted him to Ali, who freed him, so his allegiance is ours.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding a man who asked another man to guarantee him but he refused until he was given a fee: "It is not permissible."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding the *mudarabah*, deposit, and debt: they are equal in the wealth of the deceased, and they all share proportionally.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from a man from Jabir, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ: “Two men disputed before him over a she-camel. Each claimed it and presented evidence that it was his and that he had bred her. The Messenger of God ruled in favor of the one who possessed her.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم «أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ اخْتَصَمَا إِلَيْهِ فِي نَاقَةٍ ادَّعَاهَا كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا، وَأَقَامَ الْبَيِّنَةَ أَنَّهَا نَاقَتُهُ أَنْتَجَهَا، فَقَضَى بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِلَّذِي هِيَ فِي يَدَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم «أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ اخْتَصَمَا إِلَيْهِ فِي نَاقَةٍ ادَّعَاهَا كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا، وَأَقَامَ الْبَيِّنَةَ أَنَّهَا نَاقَتُهُ أَنْتَجَهَا، فَقَضَى بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِلَّذِي هِيَ فِي يَدَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from a man from Jabir, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ: Two men disputed before him regarding a she-camel, each claiming it as his own and both presenting evidence that it was his she-camel and that it had given birth under his care. records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding a woman who apostatizes from Islam: “She is invited to return to Islam. If she embraces Islam, she is left alone; if she refuses, she is killed.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that a killer does not inherit from the person he killed, either from that person’s blood money or from any other part of the estate.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is upon the defendant.” Ibrahim would not refer the oath back to the claimant.

records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الْبَيِّنَةُ عَلَى الْمُدَّعِي، وَالْيَمِينُ عَلَى الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ، وَكَانَ لَا يَرُدُّ الْيَمِينَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Shurayh that he would not accept the testimony of a man for his wife, nor of a woman for her husband, nor of a partner for his partner, nor of a master for his slave, nor of a man for his father, nor of a father for his son, nor of a blind man, nor of one who had been punished for slander.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ شَهَادَةَ الرَّجُلِ لِامْرَأَتِهِ، وَلَا الْمَرْأَةِ لِزَوْجِهَا، وَلَا الشَّرِيكِ لِشَرِيكِهِ وَلَا السَّيِّدِ لِعَبْدِهِ، وَلَا رَجُلٍ لِأَبِيهِ، وَلَا أَبٍ لِابْنِهِ، وَلَا الْأَعْمَى، وَلَا الْمَحْدُودِ فِي قَذْفٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ شَهَادَةَ الرَّجُلِ لِامْرَأَتِهِ، وَلَا الْمَرْأَةِ لِزَوْجِهَا، وَلَا الشَّرِيكِ لِشَرِيكِهِ وَلَا السَّيِّدِ لِعَبْدِهِ، وَلَا رَجُلٍ لِأَبِيهِ، وَلَا أَبٍ لِابْنِهِ، وَلَا الْأَعْمَى، وَلَا الْمَحْدُودِ فِي قَذْفٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Shurayh that he would not accept the testimony of a man for his wife, nor of a woman for her husband, nor of a partner for his partner, nor of a master for his slave, nor of a man for his father, nor of a father for his son, nor of a blind man, nor of one who had been punished for slander.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a child who later comes of age, an enslaved person who is later emancipated, and a Jew or Christian who later accepts Islam and then testifies regarding a prior testimony: “Their testimony is admissible.” He also said that Abu Hanifah did not require an oath when evidence had been presented and would not refer the oath back to the claimant; Hammad did none of these things.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي " الصَّبِيِّ ثُمَّ يَكْبُرُ وَالْعَبْدِ ثُمَّ يُعْتَقُ وَالْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ يُسْلِمَانِ، ثُمَّ يَشْهَدَانِ عَلَى شَهَادَةٍ: أَنَّهَا تَجُوزُ "، وَقَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ لَا يَسْتَحْلِفُ مَعَ الْبَيِّنَةِ، وَلَا يَرُدُّ الْيَمِينَ وَإِنَّ حَمَّادًا كَانَ لَا يَفْعَلُ شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ "
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي " الصَّبِيِّ ثُمَّ يَكْبُرُ وَالْعَبْدِ ثُمَّ يُعْتَقُ وَالْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ يُسْلِمَانِ، ثُمَّ يَشْهَدَانِ عَلَى شَهَادَةٍ: أَنَّهَا تَجُوزُ "، وَقَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ لَا يَسْتَحْلِفُ مَعَ الْبَيِّنَةِ، وَلَا يَرُدُّ الْيَمِينَ وَإِنَّ حَمَّادًا كَانَ لَا يَفْعَلُ شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ "
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding "the child who then grows up, the slave who is then freed, and the Jew and the Christian who then embrace Islam, and then they testify to a testimony: that it is valid." And he said: Abu Hanifah would not administer an oath along with the evidence, nor would he return the oath, and indeed Hammad would not do any of that.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding the disbeliever who is punished with a legal penalty while still a disbeliever, then later accepts Islam: "Islam erases what came before it during disbelief, and his testimony becomes valid."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a Muslim who was subjected to the prescribed punishment for slander, then apostatized from Islam, and then reverted to Islam: "His testimony is not permissible."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “A witness’s report of another person’s testimony is not admissible in cases involving fixed punishments (ḥudūd).”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَجُوزُ شَهَادَةٌ عَلَى شَهَادَةٍ فِي الْحُدُودِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَجُوزُ شَهَادَةٌ عَلَى شَهَادَةٍ فِي الْحُدُودِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim regarding a man who strikes another man and he dies, and witnesses testify that he struck him while he was healthy. He said If they testify that he remained bedridden until he died, the legal punishment is enforced upon him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يَضْرِبُ الرَّجُلَ فَيَمُوتُ، فَشَهِدَ الشُّهُودُ أَنَّهُ ضَرَبَهُ وَهُوَ صَحِيحٌ، قَالَ «إِذَا شَهِدُوا أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ صَاحِبُ فِرَاشٍ حَتَّى مَاتَ أُقِيمَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the one punished for slander: "If he repents, the label of wickedness is removed from him, but his testimony is never accepted. records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Shurayh that a man from Banu Asad had his hand amputated for theft, then repented sincerely. Later he gave testimony before Shurayh and asked, “Will you accept my testimony?” Shurayh replied, “Yes, and I consider you qualified to give it.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي أَسَدٍ قُطِعَ فِي سَرِقَةٍ، ثُمَّ تَابَ فَحَسُنَتْ تَوْبَتُهُ، ثُمَّ شَهِدَ عِنْدَ شُرَيْحٍ بِشَهَادَةٍ، فَقَالَ أَتُجِيزُ شَهَادَتِي؟ قَالَ: «نَعَمْ، وَأَرَاكَ لِذَلِكَ أَهْلًا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Shurayh that a man from Banu Asad was punished for theft, then he repented and his repentance was sincere. Later, he bore witness before Shurayh, so he asked, "Will you accept my testimony?" Shurayh said , "Yes, and I see you worthy of it."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “If a man gives a gift to a blood relative, he may not take it back.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «إِذَا وَهَبَ الرَّجُلُ لِذِي رَحِمٍ هِبَةً فَلَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِيهَا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Shurayh that he would not validate a charitable gift unless possession of it had been transferred to the recipient.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Shurayh that he would not permit a charity unless it was a charity that had been taken possession of.
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Shurayh that he would not validate a charitable gift unless possession of it had been transferred to the recipient.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Shurayh
records.matn_en: that he would not validate a charitable gift unless possession of it had been transferred to the recipient.
records.boundary_review_note: Shurayh’s practice begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “We do not consider a charitable gift valid until possession of it has been transferred to the recipient.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا نُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا نُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said "We do not consider a charity valid except as a charity that has been taken possession of."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا نُجِيزُ الصَّدَقَةَ إِلَّا صَدَقَةً مَقْبُوضَةً»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “We do not consider a charitable gift valid until possession of it has been transferred to the recipient.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding gifts and charitable donations: “They are valid only when the property is specified and possession has been transferred.” He added: “I do not know whether Ibrahim required the witnesses to see the transfer of possession before validating it.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْهِبَةِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ: «لَا تَجُوزُ إِلَّا مَقْبُوضَةً مَعْلُومَةً» وَقَالَ: لَا أَدْرِي، كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لَا يُجِيزُ حَتَّى يُعَايِنَ الشُّهُودُ الْقَبْضَ أَمْ لَا
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْهِبَةِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ: «لَا تَجُوزُ إِلَّا مَقْبُوضَةً مَعْلُومَةً» وَقَالَ: لَا أَدْرِي، كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ ⦗ص: 164⦘ لَا يُجِيزُ حَتَّى يُعَايِنَ الشُّهُودُ الْقَبْضَ أَمْ لَا
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding gifts and charity: "They are not valid except when taken possession of and known." And he said: "I do not know whether Ibrahim did not permit it until the witnesses actually observed the taking of possession or not."

records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim,

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s statement is followed by an additional uncertain “he said” about whether witnesses must observe possession; retained as supplied.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding a man who gives a gift to his wife or to one of his adult children who remains dependent on him: “The gift is valid if the intended recipient knows of it, even if the recipient has not yet taken possession.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «الرَّجُلِ يَهَبُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَوْ لِبَعْضِ وَلَدِهِ، وَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ وَهُوَ فِي عِيَالِهِ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْبِضْ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْهُوبُ لَهُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «الرَّجُلِ يَهَبُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَوْ لِبَعْضِ وَلَدِهِ، وَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ وَهُوَ فِي عِيَالِهِ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْبِضْ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْهُوبُ لَهُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding "a man who gifts to his wife or to one of his children who has reached maturity while still being dependent on him: that is permissible if he was aware of it, even if the recipient of the gift has not taken possession of it."

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «الرَّجُلِ يَهَبُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَوْ لِبَعْضِ وَلَدِهِ، وَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ وَهُوَ فِي عِيَالِهِ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ جَائِزٌ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْبِضْ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْهُوبُ لَهُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Salamah ibn Kuhayl from al-Mustawrid from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that a man came to him and said My uncle married me to his slave woman, and she bore me a child while he intends to sell her child. He said: He has no right to do that.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ كُهَيْلٍ، عَنِ الْمُسْتَوْرِدِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ إِنَّ عَمِّي زَوَّجَنِي أَمَتَهُ، فَوَلَدَتْ مِنِّي وَهُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ وَلَدَهَا، قَالَ: «لَيْسَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ»

He said: He has no right to do that.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar, ؓ, said: “Whoever owns a blood relative, that relative is automatically free.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ مَلَكَ ذَا رَحِمٍ مِنْ نَسَبٍ فَهُوَ حُرٌّ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ مَلَكَ ذَا رَحِمٍ مِنْ نَسَبٍ فَهُوَ حُرٌّ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar, ؓ, said "Whoever possesses a relative by blood, he is free."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said Whoever buys a relative within the prohibited degree, that relative is free.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنِ اشْتَرَى ذَا رَحِمٍ مَحْرَمٍ فَهُوَ حُرٌّ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said: “If a man emancipates half of his slave, the slave must work toward the value of the portion that was not emancipated. If two people own a slave and one emancipates his share while insolvent, the slave must work to satisfy the other owner’s share. If the emancipating owner is solvent, the other owner may choose either to claim compensation from him or to require the slave to work for him.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When a man emancipates half of his slave, the slave is required to work for the remaining half he has not been emancipated. If the slave is owned by two partners and one of them emancipates his share while being insolvent, the slave must work for the other partner. If the emancipator is solvent, the other partner has the choice: he may either claim compensation or require the slave to work for him.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ziyad or Yazid, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad that he manumitted a slave in whom his young brothers had a share. He mentioned this to Umar, ؓ, who ordered him to appraise the slave and then wait for them to reach maturity. If they wished, they could manumit him, and if they wished, they could take the value.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ زِيَادٍ، أَوْ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ الْأَسْوَدِ، أَنَّهُ أَعْتَقَ عَبْدًا وَلِإِخْوَةٍ لَهُ صِغَارٍ فِيهِ نَصِيبٌ فَذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ لِعُمَرَ رضي الله عنه «فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُقَوِّمَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَأْنِي بِهِمْ أَنْ يُدْرِكُوا، فَإِنْ شَاءُوا أَعْتَقُوا وَإِنْ شَاءُوا أَخَذُوا الْقِيمَةَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding a slave jointly owned by two men, when one emancipates his share: “The other is asked, ‘Will you emancipate your share or guarantee its value?’ If he emancipates it, the walāʾ (manumission-based clientage) is shared between them. If he pays the other’s share, the walāʾ belongs to the one who emancipated the slave. If the slave works to pay for the unfreed share, the walāʾ is shared between them.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي " الْعَبْدِ يَكُونُ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ فَيَعْتِقُ أَحَدُهُمَا، قَالَ: يُقَالُ لِلْآخَرِ أَتَعْتِقُ أَوْ تَضْمَنُ، فَإِنْ أَعْتَقَ فَالْوَلَاءُ بَيْنَهُمَا، وَإِنْ ضَمِنَ فَالْوَلَاءُ لِلَّذِي أَعْتَقَ وَإِنِ اسْتَسْعَى الْعَبْدُ فَالْوَلَاءُ بَيْنَهُمَا "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he used to recommend giving a small reward to someone who returns a runaway slave, so that people would return one another’s runaways.

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah said It reached me from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, a hadith different from the hadith of Sa'id, that he said regarding the runaway slave: "If he is found outside the city, his reward is forty dirhams."
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ : بَلَغَنِي عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه حَدِيثًا غَيْرَ حَدِيثِ سَعِيدٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْآبِقِ: " يُصَابُ خَارِجًا مِنَ الْمِصْرِ: جُعْلُهُ أَرْبَعُونَ دِرْهَمًا "
records.raw_text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ ⦗ص: 166⦘ : بَلَغَنِي عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه حَدِيثًا غَيْرَ حَدِيثِ سَعِيدٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْآبِقِ: " يُصَابُ خَارِجًا مِنَ الْمِصْرِ: جُعْلُهُ أَرْبَعُونَ دِرْهَمًا "

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Sa‘id ibn al-Marzuban, from Abu ‘Amr al-Shaybani, who said I was sitting with Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, when a man came to him and said, "A man has arrived with a runaway slave from Bahrain." The people said, "He has earned a reward." Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, said, "And a payment, if he wishes, of forty dirhams for each slave."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "The saying of God the Exalted, *'And take witnesses, two just men from among you'* (At-Talaq: 2) abrogated the testimony of the People of the Book during travel."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Bilal, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, ؓ, who said: “The practice of ʿumrā (a lifetime grant) became widespread during the Prophet’s time. The Prophet said, ‘People, hold on to your property and do not squander it. Whoever grants something as ʿumrā during his lifetime retains it after his death.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضي الله عنهما، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فَشَتِ الْعُمْرَى عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، احْبِسُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ وَلَا تُهْلِكُوهَا، فَإِنَّ مَنْ أَعْمَرَ شَيْئًا فِي حَيَاتِهِ فَهُوَ لَهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضي الله عنهما، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فَشَتِ الْعُمْرَى عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، احْبِسُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ وَلَا تُهْلِكُوهَا، فَإِنَّ مَنْ أَعْمَرَ شَيْئًا فِي حَيَاتِهِ فَهُوَ لَهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Bilal, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, ؓ, that he said The practice of *umra* became widespread during the time of the Prophet, ﷺ, so the Prophet, ﷺ, said: "O people, hold onto your properties and do not ruin them. For whoever grants something as *umra* during his lifetime, it belongs to him after his death."

records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Bilal, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, ؓ, who said: “The practice of ʿumrā (a lifetime grant) became widespread during the Prophet’s time. The Prophet said, ‘People, hold on to your property and do not squander it. Whoever grants something as ʿumrā during his lifetime retains it after his death.’”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضي الله عنهما،
records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ فَشَتِ الْعُمْرَى عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، احْبِسُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ وَلَا تُهْلِكُوهَا، فَإِنَّ مَنْ أَعْمَرَ شَيْئًا فِي حَيَاتِهِ فَهُوَ لَهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Bilal, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, ؓ,
records.matn_en: who said: “The practice of ʿumrā (a lifetime grant) became widespread during the Prophet’s time. The Prophet said, ‘People, hold on to your property and do not squander it. Whoever grants something as ʿumrā during his lifetime retains it after his death.’”
records.boundary_review_note: Jabir’s report about the practice of umra and the Prophet’s statement begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said that he had witnessed Ibn Umar, ؓ, when a Bedouin asked him about ʿumrā (a lifetime grant). Ibn Umar replied: “It is inherited by the person who grants it, but it belongs to the person who has it in his possession.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَبِيبِ بْنِ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ، قَالَ شَهِدْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما وَسَأَلَهُ أَعْرَابِيٌّ عَنِ الْعُمْرَى فَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهَا «مِيرَاثٌ لِلَّذِي يُعْطِيهَا، وَهُوَ للَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي يَدَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَبِيبِ بْنِ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ، قَالَ شَهِدْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما وَسَأَلَهُ أَعْرَابِيٌّ عَنِ الْعُمْرَى فَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهَا «مِيرَاثٌ لِلَّذِي يُعْطِيهَا، وَهُوَ للَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي يَدَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said I witnessed Ibn Umar, ؓ, when a Bedouin asked him about the *umra* (life grant), and he informed him that it is "an inheritance for the one to whom it is given, and it belongs to the one in whose possession it is."

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said that he had witnessed Ibn Umar, ؓ, when a Bedouin asked him about ʿumrā (a lifetime grant). records.matn_ar: قَالَ شَهِدْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما وَسَأَلَهُ أَعْرَابِيٌّ عَنِ الْعُمْرَى فَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهَا «مِيرَاثٌ لِلَّذِي يُعْطِيهَا، وَهُوَ للَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي يَدَيْهِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Habib ibn Abi Thabit’s account of Ibn Umar’s answer begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: “The right of pre-emption is determined by the entrances; the entrance nearest to the property has the strongest claim to pre-emption.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الشُّفْعَةُ بِالْأَبْوَابِ، أَقْرَبُ الْأَبْوَابِ إِلَيْهَا أَحَقُّ بِالشُّفْعَةِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الشُّفْعَةُ بِالْأَبْوَابِ، أَقْرَبُ الْأَبْوَابِ إِلَيْهَا أَحَقُّ بِالشُّفْعَةِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said "Pre-emption is through the doors; the nearest door to it has the greatest right to pre-emption."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ شُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الشُّفْعَةُ بِالْأَبْوَابِ، أَقْرَبُ الْأَبْوَابِ إِلَيْهَا أَحَقُّ بِالشُّفْعَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, ؓ, from Abu Rafi’, ؓ, who reported: Saʿd negotiated with him over a house. Saʿd said, “Take this house for four hundred. I have been offered eight hundred for it, but I am giving it to you because of a report I heard from the Messenger of God, ﷺ: ‘A neighbor has the stronger claim to his adjoining property.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنِ الْمِسْوَرِ بْنِ مَخْرَمَةَ رضي الله عنهما عَنْ أَبِي رَافِعٍ رضي الله عنه، سَاوَمَهُ سَعْدٌ بِبَيْتٍ، فَقَالَ سَعْدٌ: خُذْ هَذَا الْبَيْتَ بِأَرْبَعِمِائَةٍ، أَمَا إِنِّي قَدْ أُعْطِيتُ بِهِ ثَمَانِمِائَةٍ، وَلَكِنِّي أُعْطِيكَهُ لِحَدِيثٍ سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «الْجَارُ أَحَقُّ بِسَقَبِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنِ الْمِسْوَرِ بْنِ مَخْرَمَةَ رضي الله عنهما عَنْ أَبِي رَافِعٍ رضي الله عنه، سَاوَمَهُ سَعْدٌ بِبَيْتٍ، فَقَالَ سَعْدٌ: خُذْ هَذَا الْبَيْتَ بِأَرْبَعِمِائَةٍ، أَمَا إِنِّي قَدْ أُعْطِيتُ بِهِ ثَمَانِمِائَةٍ، وَلَكِنِّي أُعْطِيكَهُ لِحَدِيثٍ سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «الْجَارُ أَحَقُّ بِسَقَبِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, ؓ, from Abu Rafi’, ؓ, that Sa’d bargained with him for a house. Sa’d said "Take this house for four hundred, though I have been offered eight hundred for it. But I am giving it to you because of a hadith I heard from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, that he said: *The neighbor has the greatest right to his proximity.*"

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Rafi transmits the account of Sa’d’s offer and the Prophetic saying; Sa’d is a participant in the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Ishaq, from Asim, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, who said regarding lost property: “Announce it for a year. If its owner comes, [give it to him]; otherwise, give it in charity. If you wish, you may keep it. If its owner later comes, he has the choice: he may hold you liable, or he may choose the reward [of the charity].”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَاصِمٍ ⦗ص: 168⦘ ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي اللُّقَطَةِ: " عَرِّفْهَا حَوْلًا، فَإِنْ جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا وَإِلَّا فَتَصَدَّقْ بِهَا، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ أَمْسَكْتَ، فَإِنْ جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ: إِنْ شَاءَ ضَمِنَكَ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ اخْتَارَ الْأَجْرَ "

records.text_en: …That was mentioned, and Ibn Abbas said to him: “Must you pray when the prayer time comes, put on your clothes, and break your oath? Then put on your clothes, pray in the Sacred Mosque, and expiate your oath. Satan only wanted to toy with you.” He said: “I mentioned that to Ibn Umar, ؓ, and Ibn Umar said: ‘Who can match Ibn Abbas’s hidden insights, ؓ?’”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “The expiation for an oath is to feed ten poor people, clothe them (one garment for each), or give each person half a saʿ of wheat or flour, or one saʿ of dates; or to provide them with lunch and dinner; or to free a slave. Whoever cannot do so must fast three consecutive days. He may choose among these alternatives, for God says: ‘or … or …’”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Imran ibn Umayr, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who freed a slave of his. He said to him: “Your property is mine, but I will leave it to you.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, who reported that Hamzah’s daughter, ؓ, freed a slave of hers. The slave died leaving a daughter, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, allotted half to the slave’s daughter and half to Hamzah’s daughter.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ شَدَّادِ بْنِ الْهَادِ، «أَنَّ ابْنَةً لِحَمْزَةَ رضي الله عنهما أَعْتَقَتْ مَمْلُوكًا لَهَا، فَمَاتَ وَتَرَكَ ابْنَةً ⦗ص: 170⦘ ، فَأَعْطَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ابْنَتَهُ النِّصْفَ، وَابْنَةَ حَمْزَةَ النِّصْفَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, ؓ, disputed before Umar, ؓ, over a freedman of Safiyyah, ؓ. Ali said, ‘I am my aunt’s agnatic heir; I bear liability for her freedman’s blood-wit and inherit from him.’ Al-Zubayr said, ‘She is my mother, and I inherit from her freedman.’ Umar awarded the inheritance to al-Zubayr and charged Ali ibn Abi Talib with the blood-wit.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَالزُّبَيْرَ بْنَ الْعَوَّامِ رضي الله عنهما اخْتَصَمَا إِلَى عُمَرَ رضي الله عنه فِي مَوْلًى لِصَفِيَّةَ رضي الله عنها، فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: أَنَا عَصَبَةُ عَمَّتِي، وَأَنَا أَعْقِلُ عَنْ مَوْلَاهَا وَأَرِثُهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ الزُّبَيْرُ: أُمِّي، وَأَنَا أَرِثُ مَوْلَاهَا، «فَقَضَى عُمَرُ لِلزُّبَيْرِ بِالْمِيرَاثِ، وَقَضَى بِالْعَقْلِ عَلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَالزُّبَيْرَ بْنَ الْعَوَّامِ رضي الله عنهما اخْتَصَمَا إِلَى عُمَرَ رضي الله عنه فِي مَوْلًى لِصَفِيَّةَ رضي الله عنها، فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: أَنَا عَصَبَةُ عَمَّتِي، وَأَنَا أَعْقِلُ عَنْ مَوْلَاهَا وَأَرِثُهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ الزُّبَيْرُ: أُمِّي، وَأَنَا أَرِثُ مَوْلَاهَا، «فَقَضَى عُمَرُ لِلزُّبَيْرِ بِالْمِيرَاثِ، وَقَضَى بِالْعَقْلِ عَلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ali ibn Abi Talib and Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, ؓ, disputed before Umar, ؓ, regarding a freed slave of Safiyyah, ؓ. Ali said I am the closest male relative of my aunt, and I pay the blood money for her freed slave and inherit from him. Then Zubayr said: He is my maternal uncle, and I inherit from her freed slave. Umar ruled that the inheritance belonged to Zubayr and ruled that the blood money was upon Ali ibn Abi Talib.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Muhammad ibn Qays from Masruq a man from the people of al-Urdunn affiliated himself with a cousin, and the cousin became Muslim at his hand. The man died leaving property, so [the cousin] asked Ibn Masud, ؓ, about it. Ibn Masud instructed him to take his inheritance.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Muhammad ibn Qays from Masruq that a man from the people of al-Urdunn bequeathed to his cousin, and he had embraced Islam at his hands. The man died and left wealth, so he asked Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, about that, and he instructed him to take his inheritance.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah that a man asked Hudhayfah, ؓ, about an obligatory duty, so he said "I have no knowledge of it." Alqamah said: "Shall I answer him?" He said: "And do you know it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then answer him." So Alqamah answered him, and Hudhayfah said to him: "From where did you know it?" Alqamah said: "From our companion," meaning Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ. Hudhayfah said: "Does he teach you this?" He said: "Yes."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, a woman had illicit intercourse in pre-Islamic times and gave birth to a boy. Her brother bought a slave and emancipated him. The freedman died leaving six camels. The case was brought before Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he ordered the camels transferred to the charity camels. The man went to Ibn Masud and told him what happened. Ibn Masud went to Umar and said: “If you will not let him inherit by blood relationship, then let him inherit by the benefit of emancipation.” Umar asked, “Do you hold that view?” He said, “Yes.” Umar said, “I hold it too,” and awarded him the inheritance.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that a woman in the pre-Islamic era committed adultery and gave birth to a boy. The woman’s brother bought a slave and set him free. The slave later died, leaving behind six camels. The case was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, who ordered that the camels be given to the charity fund. The man then went to Ibn Mas‘ud and informed him. Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, went to Umar, ؓ, and said "If you do not grant him inheritance by kinship, then grant it to him by virtue of the favor (of freeing him)." Umar asked: "Do you see it that way?" Ibn Mas‘ud replied: "Yes." Umar said: "I see it the same way," and so he granted him the inheritance.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn al-Zubayr, that it reached him that Ibn Mas‘ud interpreted the verse regarding the maternal aunt and paternal aunt: *"But kindred by blood are nearer to one another in the decree of God."* Ibn al-Zubayr said "This verse was only revealed concerning: *'As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection until they emigrate.'* The Bedouin would not inherit from the Emigrant. Then it was later abrogated by: *'But kindred by blood are nearer to one another in the decree of God.'* So the Bedouin would inherit from the Emigrant."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Zakariyya ibn al-Harith, from someone who narrated to him, from al-Mundhir ibn Abi Humaysah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, sent him to some part of Syria—either Homs or elsewhere—and he allocated two shares for the horseman and one share for the foot soldier. When this reached Umar, he approved of it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ الْحَارِثِ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ، عَنِ الْمُنْذِرِ بْنِ أَبِي حُمَيْصَةَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ، رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «بَعَثَهُ عَلَى بَعْضِ الشَّامِ عَلَى حِمْصَ أَوْ غَيْرِهَا، فَقَسَمَ لِلْفَارِسِ سَهْمَيْنِ، وَلِلرَّاجِلِ سَهْمًا، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ عُمَرَ فَرَضِيَ بِهِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, that he said "All disbelief is one religion; we do not inherit from them, nor do they inherit from us."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim that a woman died, leaving behind her freed slaves, her father, and her son. Then the freed slave died, so Ibrahim said "Her father receives one-sixth, and whatever remains is for her son."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, visited Sa’d ibn Malik to check on him. Sa’d said O Messenger of God, shall I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth? He said: No. Sa’d said: Then half of it? He said: No. Sa’d said: Then one-third of it? He said: One-third, and one-third is much. It is better for you to leave your family wealthy than to leave them poor, begging from people.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم دَخَلَ عَلَى سَعْدِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه يَعُودُهُ، فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أُوصِي بِثُلُثَيْ مَالِي قَالَ: «لَا» قَالَ: فَبِنِصْفِهِ، قَالَ: «لَا» قَالَ: فَبِثُلُثِهِ، قَالَ: «الثُّلُثُ وَالثُّلُثُ كَثِيرٌ، إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَدَعْ أَهْلَكَ أَغْنِيَاءَ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَنْ تَدَعَهُمْ فُقَرَاءَ يَتَكَفَّفُونَ النَّاسَ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, from his father, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, visited Sa’d ibn Malik to check on him. records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “If someone bequeaths one-third of his estate and also emancipates a slave, the emancipation is given priority within the bequest. If he bequeaths one-third and a specified sum in dirhams, whether or not particular coins are designated, the dirhams are given priority over the one-third. If he emancipates a slave while in good health, it is charged against his entire estate.”

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَوْصَى بِالثُّلُثِ وَأَعْتَقَ بُدِئَ بِالْعِتْقِ فِي الْوَصِيَّةِ، وَإِذَا أَوْصَى بِالثُّلُثِ وَدَرَاهِمَ مُسَمَّاةٍ بِعَيْنِهَا أَوْ بِغَيْرِ عَيْنِهَا بُدِئَ بِالدَّرَاهِمِ قَبْلَ الثُّلُثِ، وَإِذَا أَعْتَقَهُ فِي صِحَّتِهِ كَانَ مِنْ جَمِيعِ مَالِهِ»

records.matn_en: who said: “If someone bequeaths one-third of his estate and also emancipates a slave, the emancipation is given priority within the bequest. If he bequeaths one-third and a specified sum in dirhams, whether or not particular coins are designated, the dirhams are given priority over the one-third. If he emancipates a slave while in good health, it is charged against his entire estate.”
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s legal explanation begins matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: “The guardian may take a loan from the orphan’s property, which is owed by the guardian.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «يَأْكُلُ الْوَصِيُّ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ قَرْضًا عَلَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «يَأْكُلُ الْوَصِيُّ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ قَرْضًا عَلَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said The guardian may consume the orphan’s wealth as a loan against him.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said The guardian of the orphan should consider; if he sees fit to invest the orphan’s wealth, give it as a profit-sharing venture, buy and sell on behalf of the orphan, or take it himself as a profit-sharing venture, he may do so.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «يَنْظُرُ الْوَصِيُّ لِلْيَتِيمِ، فَإِنْ رَأَى أَنْ يُبْضِعَ مَالَهُ أَوْ يُعْطِيَهُ مُضَارَبَةً، أَوْ يَشْتَرِيَ هُوَ لِلْيَتِيمِ وَيَبِيعَ أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُ هُوَ مُضَارَبَةً، فَعَلَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Aisha, ؓ, who said: “They used to set aside the orphan’s food separately from his siblings’ food.” Aisha said: “I would not keep him apart like a wild animal; I would mix my food with his, my milk with his, and my animal’s fodder with his animal’s fodder.” Then she recited: “If you mix with them, then they are your brothers.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها، قَالَتْ «كَانُوا يَضَعُونَ طَعَامَ الْيَتِيمِ عَلَى الْإِخْوَانِ عَلَى حِدَةٍ» ، فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ " مَا كُنْتُ لِأَدَعَهُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْوَحْشَى حَتَّى أَخْلِطَ طَعَامِي بِطَعَامِهِ وَلَبَنِي بِلَبَنِهِ وَعَلَفَ دَابَّتِي بِعَلَفِ دَابَّتِهِ، ثُمَّ قَرَأْتُ {وَإِنْ تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ} [البقرة: 220] "

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir from Aisha, ؓ, who said They used to place the orphan’s food separately from the brothers. Aisha then said, "I would not leave him in the state of a wild creature until I mix my food with his, my milk with his milk, and my animal’s fodder with his animal’s fodder." Then she recited, *"But if you mix their affairs with yours, they are your brothers."* [Al-Baqarah: 220]

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Muslim al-A‘war from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, set out from Medina to Mecca during Ramadan. Along the way, the people complained to him of hardship, so he broke his fast until he reached Mecca.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُسْلِمٍ الْأَعْوَرِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ «خَرَجَ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ إِلَى مَكَّةَ فِي رَمَضَانَ، فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ النَّاسُ فِي بَعْضِ الطَّرِيقِ الْجَهْدَ، فَأَفْطَرَ حَتَّى أَتَى مَكَّةَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, departed from Medina to Mecca when two nights of Ramadan had passed. He traveled until he reached Qudayd, then the people complained to him of exhaustion, so he broke his fast at Qudayd. He continued breaking his fast until he reached Mecca.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ إِلَى مَكَّةَ لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ خَلَتَا مِنْ رَمَضَانَ، فَسَارَ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى قُدَيْدٍ، ثُمَّ شَكَا النَّاسُ إِلَيْهِ الْجَهْدَ، فَأَفْطَرَ بِقُدَيْدٍ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَزَلْ مُفْطِرًا حَتَّى أَتَى مَكَّةَ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, departed from Medina to Mecca when two nights of Ramadan had passed. He traveled until he reached Qudayd, then the people complained to him of exhaustion, so he broke his fast at Qudayd. He continued breaking his fast until he reached Mecca.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ali ibn al-Aqmar that the Prophet, ﷺ, would keep fasting during Ramadan and then spend the night hungry, standing [in prayer], until just before dawn, when he drank some milk; that served as both his breaking of the fast and his pre-dawn meal. A man spent a night with the Prophet, ﷺ. They searched for something for him in his wives’ homes but found nothing. The Prophet said three times, “May God feed whoever fed me.” Then they saw that the she-goat was full of milk. He milked it, producing about as much as he usually drank, and the Prophet drank.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْأَقْمَرِ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَظَلُّ صَائِمًا فِي رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ يَبِيتُ طَاوِيًا قَائِمًا، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ السَّحَرُ شَرِبَ شَرْبَةَ لَبَنٍ فَكَانَتْ إِفْطَارَهُ وَسَحُورَهُ، وَإِنَّ رَجُلًا بَاتَ لَيْلَةً عِنْدُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَطَلَبُوا لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم شَيْئًا فِي بُيُوتِ أَزْوَاجِهِ فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا شَيْئًا، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَطْعَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ أَطْعَمَنِي» ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، ثُمَّ نَظَرُوا ⦗ص: 175⦘ إِلَى الْعَنْزِ فَإِذَا هِيَ حَافِلٌ، فَحَلَبَ مِنْهَا مِثْلَ مَا كَانَ يَشْرَبُ فَشَرِبَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ali ibn al-Aqmar that the Prophet, ﷺ, would spend the day of Ramadan fasting, then spend the night standing in prayer while hungry, until when it was the time before dawn, he would drink a sip of milk, and that would be his iftar and suhur. A man spent a night with the Prophet, ﷺ, and they searched for something in the houses of his wives for the Prophet, ﷺ, but found nothing. The Prophet, ﷺ, said , "May God feed the one who fed me," three times. Then they looked at the she-goat, and it was full of milk, so he milked from it as much as he used to drink, and the Prophet, ﷺ, drank.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib, that a man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, and said "I broke my fast on a day in Ramadan." The Prophet, ﷺ, said to him: "Can you afford to free a slave?" He said: "No." He said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "No." He said: "Can you afford to feed sixty poor people?" He said: "No." Then the Prophet, ﷺ, helped him with a basket containing fifteen *sa‘* of dates and said to him: "Give this in charity." The man said: "There is no household between the two lava fields more in need than me and my dependents." He said: "Then eat it and feed your dependents."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ قَدْ أَفْطَرَ يَوْمًا مِنْ رَمَضَانَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَتَقْدِرُ عَلَى تَحْرِيرِ رَقَبَةٍ؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «أَتَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَصُومَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «أَتَقْدِرُ أَنْ تُطْعِمَ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا؟» قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَأَعَانَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمِكْتَلٍ فِيهِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ صَاعًا مِنْ تَمْرٍ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: «تَصَدَّقْ بِهَا» فَقَالَ: مَا بَيْنَ لَابَتَيْهَا أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ أَحْوَجُ مِنِّي وَمِنْ عِيَالِي، قَالَ: «فَكُلْ وَأَطْعِمْ عِيَالَكَ»
