records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir from his father from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Himyari that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to one of his companions on the day of Ashura: "Instruct your people to fast this day." The man said, "They have already eaten." He said, "Even if they have eaten."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ⦗ص: 177⦘ الْمُنْتَشِرِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْحِمْيَرِيِّ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ: «مُرْ قَوْمَكَ فَلْيَصُومُوا هَذَا الْيَوْمَ» قَالَ: إِنَّهُمْ قَدْ طَعِمُوا، قَالَ: «وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ طَعِمُوا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who said "Fasting the day of ‘Ashura’ is equivalent to fasting a year, and fasting the day of ‘Arafah is equivalent to fasting two years."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «صَوْمُ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ يَعْدِلُ صَوْمَ سَنَةٍ، وَصَوْمُ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ يَعْدِلُ صَوْمَ سَنَتَيْنِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah from 'Amr ibn Maymun from 'Aishah, ؓ, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, used to kiss while fasting.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from Amir, from Masruq, from Aisha, ؓ, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would kiss her face while fasting.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها، «أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يُصِيبُ مِنْ وَجْهِهَا وَهُوَ صَائِمٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu al-Atuf from al-Zuhri from Sa'd ibn Malik and Zayd ibn Thabit, ؓ, that they would practice cupping while fasting and practice coitus interruptus.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَطُوفِ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، وَزَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُمَا «كَانَا يَحْتَجِمَانِ وَهُمَا صَائِمَانِ وَيَعْزِلَانِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Sawwar from Abu Hadir from Ibn Abbas, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, was cupped while he was fasting and in a state of ihram at Al-Qaha.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Musa ibn Abi Kathir Abu al-Sabbah from Mujahid that he said "This verse was revealed concerning these people: *And upon those who are able to fast [but with hardship] – a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person.*" He said: "The elderly man feeds [the poor] and does not fast."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ أَبِي الصَّبَّاحِ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ " فِي هَؤُلَاءِ أُنْزِلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ {وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ} [البقرة: 184] " قَالَ: «الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ يُطْعِمُ وَلَا يَصُومُ»

records.boundary_review_note: Mujahid’s interpretation and explanation begin matn; the second “he said” is kept within the transmitted content.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, and from someone who narrated to Abu Yusuf, from Amir, that they both said "Making up the fasts of Ramadan consecutively is more beloved to us."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَمَّنْ، حَدَّثَ أَبَا يُوسُفَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّهُمَا قَالَا جَمِيعًا: «قَضَاءُ رَمَضَانَ مُتَتَابِعًا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَمَّنْ، حَدَّثَ أَبَا يُوسُفَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّهُمَا قَالَا جَمِيعًا: «قَضَاءُ رَمَضَانَ مُتَتَابِعًا أَحَبُّ إِلَيْنَا»

records.boundary_review_note: The Arabic groups two routes—through Ibrahim and through an unnamed transmitter to Abu Yusuf from Amir—before attributing a joint statement; Amir’s fuller identity is unspecified.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said regarding making up Ramadan: "Separate them if you wish." And Ibrahim said: "Consecutively is more beloved to me."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding the fasting person who uses the tooth-stick: "There is no harm in it, whether it is moist or dry, and there is no harm in using water to clean the teeth."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الصَّائِمِ يَسْتَاكُ: «لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ رَطْبًا كَانَ أَوْ يَابِسًا، وَلَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَسْتَاكَ بِالْمَاءِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Masruq, who said I entered upon Aisha, ؓ, on the Day of Arafah, and she said, "Are you fasting?" I said, "No." She said, "O servant girl, mix some sawiq for him and sweeten it." Then she said, "If I were not fasting, I would have tasted it." I said, "Nothing prevented me from fasting except that I thought it was the Day of Sacrifice." She said, "The Day of Sacrifice is only the day when the people sacrifice, and the Day of Breaking the Fast is the day when they break their fast."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْأَقْمَرِ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ فَقَالَتْ: أَصَائِمٌ أَنْتَ؟ قُلْتُ: لَا، قَالَتْ: يَا جَارِيَةُ خَوِّضِي لَهُ سُوَيْقًا وَأَحْلِيهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَتْ: لَوْمَا أَنِّي صَائِمَةٌ لَذُقْتُهُ، قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: مَا مَنَعَنِي مِنَ الصَّوْمِ إِلَّا أَنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ، فَقَالَتْ: «إِنَّمَا يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ يَوْمَ يَنْحَرُ النَّاسُ، وَيَوْمُ الْفِطْرِ يَوْمَ يُفْطِرُونَ»

When twenty-nine days had passed, he sent for Aisha, ؓ, and she said , "Only twenty-nine days have passed." He said, "The month may be twenty-nine days or it may be thirty."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, was on a cloudy day in Ramadan. He thought the sun had set, so he and his companions broke their fast. Then the sun appeared afterward, so Umar said "We did not deliberately commit a sin. We will complete the fast of this day and fast another day in its place."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, used to give the ruling that whoever reached dawn in a state of major ritual impurity had thereby broken the fast. This reached Aisha, ؓ, and she said: “May God have mercy on Abu Hurayrah; he did not retain it correctly. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, would reach dawn with water dripping from his head after washing from janabah, then he would fast.” This reached Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, and he said, “She knows better than I do,” and withdrew his ruling.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Yahya, from someone who narrated to him from ‘Attab ibn Asid, ؓ, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, appointed him governor of Mecca and said: “I am sending you to the people of the Sacred House. Forbid them from four practices: profiting from what one does not bear liability for, selling what one has not taken possession of, stipulating two conditions in a single sale, and combining a loan with a sale.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said Whoever sells a pollinated palm tree or a slave, the fruit of the palm and the slave’s wealth belong to the seller unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Masud, ؓ, sold al-Ashath some slaves from the governorship’s holdings. Al-Ashath said, “I bought them for ten thousand,” while Abdullah said, “For twenty thousand.” Abdullah said, “Let us appoint someone to arbitrate between us.” Al-Ashath replied, “You decide between us.” Abdullah said, “I will judge this according to the Messenger of God’s judgment.” He then quoted: “When the two parties to a sale disagree, the seller’s word is accepted, or they rescind the sale.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ بَاعَ مِنَ الْأَشْعَثِ رَقِيقًا مِنْ رَقِيقِ الْإِمَارَةِ، فَقَالَ الْأَشْعَثُ: أَخَذْتُهُمْ بِعَشْرَةِ آلَافٍ، وَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: بِعِشْرِينَ أَلْفًا، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: اجْعَلْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ رَجُلًا، فَقَالَ الْأَشْعَثُ: أَنْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: لَأَقْضِيَنَّ فِيهَا بِقَضَاءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قَالَ: «إِذَا اخْتَلَفَا الْمُتَبَايِعَانِ فَالْقَوْلُ قَوْلُ الْبَائِعِ أَوْ يَتَرَادَّانِ الْبَيْعَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ بَاعَ مِنَ الْأَشْعَثِ رَقِيقًا مِنْ رَقِيقِ الْإِمَارَةِ، فَقَالَ الْأَشْعَثُ: أَخَذْتُهُمْ بِعَشْرَةِ آلَافٍ، وَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: بِعِشْرِينَ أَلْفًا، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: اجْعَلْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ رَجُلًا، فَقَالَ الْأَشْعَثُ: أَنْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: لَأَقْضِيَنَّ فِيهَا بِقَضَاءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، قَالَ: «إِذَا اخْتَلَفَا الْمُتَبَايِعَانِ فَالْقَوْلُ قَوْلُ الْبَائِعِ أَوْ يَتَرَادَّانِ الْبَيْعَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he sold a slave from the slaves of the emirate to Al-Ash'ath. Al-Ash'ath said , "I took them for ten thousand," while Abdullah said, "For twenty thousand." Abdullah then said, "Let us appoint a man between us." Al-Ash'ath replied, "You are between me and yourself." Abdullah said, "I will surely judge in this matter by the judgment of the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'When the two buyers differ, the statement is that of the seller, or they may rescind the sale.'"

records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Masud, ؓ, sold al-Ashath some slaves from the governorship’s holdings. Al-Ashath said, “I bought them for ten thousand,” while Abdullah said, “For twenty thousand.” Abdullah said, “Let us appoint someone to arbitrate between us.” Al-Ashath replied, “You decide between us.” Abdullah said, “I will judge this according to the Messenger of God’s judgment.” He then quoted: “When the two parties to a sale disagree, the seller’s word is accepted, or they rescind the sale.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ،

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a commodity a man sells on credit: "He must not buy it back for less than that until the sold item changes."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Walid ibn Sari from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, who said: “I asked him, saying: ‘I bought [it] against ten for seven and a half and seven [the wording and relation between these amounts are unclear in the Arabic].’” He said: “A finely made vessel was brought to Umar, ؓ, and he ordered me to sell it for him. I was offered its weight and something extra. I told him about that, and Umar said: ‘No: only like for like, for any excess is usury.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ سَرِيعٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ: إِنِّي اشْتَرَيْتُ بِغَايَةِ الْعَشْرَةِ بِسَبْعَةٍ وَنِصْفٍ وَبِسَبْعَةٍ، فَقَالَ: أُتِيَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه بِإِنَاءٍ قَدْ أُحْكِمَتْ صِنَاعَتُهُ فَأَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَبِيعَهُ لَهُ فَأَعْطَيْتُ بِهِ وَزْنَهُ وَزِيَادَةً، فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: «لَا إِلَّا مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ، وَإِنَّ الْفَضْلَ رِبًا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ سَرِيعٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ: إِنِّي اشْتَرَيْتُ بِغَايَةِ الْعَشْرَةِ بِسَبْعَةٍ وَنِصْفٍ وَبِسَبْعَةٍ، فَقَالَ: أُتِيَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه بِإِنَاءٍ قَدْ أُحْكِمَتْ صِنَاعَتُهُ فَأَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَبِيعَهُ لَهُ فَأَعْطَيْتُ بِهِ وَزْنَهُ وَزِيَادَةً، فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: «لَا إِلَّا مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ، وَإِنَّ الْفَضْلَ رِبًا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Walid ibn Sari from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, who said I asked him and said, "I bought something worth ten for seven and a half and for seven." He said: Umar, ؓ, was brought a vessel whose craftsmanship was perfected, so he ordered me to sell it for him. I sold it for its weight and more, then I mentioned that to him. Umar said, "No, except like for like, and the excess is usury."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Atiyyah al-Awfi from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said Gold for gold, weight for weight, hand to hand, and any excess is usury. Silver for silver, weight for weight, hand to hand, and any excess is usury. Wheat for wheat, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Barley for barley, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Dates for dates, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Salt for salt, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Abu Hanifah said: We mentioned selling a cat in the presence of Ata’, and he did not disapprove of it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطِيَّةَ الْعَوْفِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الذَّهَبُ بِالذَّهَبِ وَزْنًا بِوَزْنٍ، يَدًا بِيَدٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْفِضَّةُ بِالْفِضَّةِ وَزْنًا بِوَزْنٍ يَدًا بِيَدٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْحِنْطَةُ بِالْحِنْطَةِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالشَّعِيرُ بِالشَّعِيرِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالتَّمْرُ بِالتَّمْرِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْمِلْحُ بِالْمِلْحِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا» وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: ذَكَرْنَا بَيْعَ الْهِرِّ عِنْدَ عَطَاءٍ فَلَمْ يَعِبْهُ

Barley for barley, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Dates for dates, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Salt for salt, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Abu Hanifah said: We mentioned selling a cat in the presence of Ata’, and he did not disapprove of it.
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَطِيَّةَ الْعَوْفِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رضي الله عنه
records.matn_ar: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «الذَّهَبُ بِالذَّهَبِ وَزْنًا بِوَزْنٍ، يَدًا بِيَدٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْفِضَّةُ بِالْفِضَّةِ وَزْنًا بِوَزْنٍ يَدًا بِيَدٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْحِنْطَةُ بِالْحِنْطَةِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالشَّعِيرُ بِالشَّعِيرِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالتَّمْرُ بِالتَّمْرِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا، وَالْمِلْحُ بِالْمِلْحِ كَيْلًا بِكَيْلٍ وَالْفَضْلُ رِبًا» وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: ذَكَرْنَا بَيْعَ الْهِرِّ عِنْدَ عَطَاءٍ فَلَمْ يَعِبْهُ
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Atiyyah al-Awfi from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ,
records.matn_en: that the Prophet, ﷺ, said Gold for gold, weight for weight, hand to hand, and any excess is usury. Silver for silver, weight for weight, hand to hand, and any excess is usury. Wheat for wheat, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Barley for barley, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Dates for dates, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Salt for salt, measure for measure, and any excess is usury. Abu Hanifah said: We mentioned selling a cat in the presence of Ata’, and he did not disapprove of it.
records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hanifah's appended cat-sale comment remains in the matn, not the transmission path.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, who raised it to the Prophet, ﷺ, that it was said to him: "Fix prices." He said: "Verily, cheapness and high prices are from God, and I would love to meet God the Exalted with no injustice toward anyone from me."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Masud, ؓ, lent a man some dirhams. The man brought back dirhams of better quality, but Ibn Masud refused to accept them and said: “Bring us dirhams like the ones we lent you.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَقْرَضَ رَجُلًا دَرَاهِمَ، فَأَتَاهُ بِدَرَاهِمَ أَجْوَدَ مِنْهَا فَأَعْطَاهَا إِيَّاهُ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَقْبَلَهَا وَقَالَ «ائْتِنَا بِمِثْلِ دَرَاهِمِنَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَقْرَضَ رَجُلًا دَرَاهِمَ، فَأَتَاهُ بِدَرَاهِمَ أَجْوَدَ مِنْهَا فَأَعْطَاهَا إِيَّاهُ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَقْبَلَهَا وَقَالَ «ائْتِنَا بِمِثْلِ دَرَاهِمِنَا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, lent a man some dirhams. The man then brought him dirhams of better quality, so Ibn Mas'ud gave them to him, but the man refused to accept them and said "Bring us dirhams like ours."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he used to disapprove of a man taking dirhams as a loan from another man on the condition that he would repay him in another land.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ الدَّرَاهِمَ قَرْضًا عَلَى أَنْ يُوَفِّيَهُ إِيَّاهَا فِي أَرْضٍ أُخْرَى»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ الدَّرَاهِمَ قَرْضًا عَلَى أَنْ يُوَفِّيَهُ إِيَّاهَا فِي أَرْضٍ أُخْرَى»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ الدَّرَاهِمَ قَرْضًا عَلَى أَنْ يُوَفِّيَهُ إِيَّاهَا فِي أَرْضٍ أُخْرَى»

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim is the final named transmitter and the matn reports his view.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Marzuq Abu Bukayr, from Abu Jabalah, from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he was asked: "We arrive in a land with our light, widely accepted silver coins, while their heavy, sluggish silver coins are there. Should we buy their silver with our silver?" He said "No. Instead, sell your silver for gold dinars, then buy their silver with the dinars. Do not part from him until you take possession. If he ascends to an upper room, ascend with him, and if he jumps, jump with him."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مَرْزُوقٍ أَبِي بُكَيْرٍ ⦗ص: 185⦘ ، عَنْ أَبِي جَبَلَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ فَقَالَ إِنَّا نَقْدُمُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَعَنَا الْوَرِقُ الْخِفَافُ النَّافِقَةُ، وَبِهَا الْوَرِقُ الثِّقَالُ الْكَاسِدَةُ، أَفَنَشْتَرِي وَرِقَهُمْ بِوَرِقِنَا، فَقَالَ: «لَا، وَلَكِنْ بِعْ وَرِقَكَ بِالدَّنَانِيرِ وَاشْتَرِ وَرِقَهُمْ بِالدَّنَانِيرِ وَلَا تُفَارِقْهُ حَتَّى تَقْبِضَ، وَإِنْ صَعِدَ فَوْقَ بَيْتٍ فَاصْعَدْ مَعَهُ وَإِنْ وَثَبَ فَثِبْ مَعَهُ»

records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Marzuq Abu Bukayr, from Abu Jabalah, from Ibn Umar, ؓ,
records.matn_en: that he was asked: "We arrive in a land with our light, widely accepted silver coins, while their heavy, sluggish silver coins are there. Should we buy their silver with our silver?" He said "No. Instead, sell your silver for gold dinars, then buy their silver with the dinars. Do not part from him until you take possession. If he ascends to an upper room, ascend with him, and if he jumps, jump with him."
records.boundary_review_note: The question is posed to Ibn Umar, whose answer follows in the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ziyad ibn Maysarah, from his father, who said I asked Ibn Umar, ؓ, about a man to whom I owed four thousand dirhams due at a fixed time, and he said, "Give me two thousand now, and I will cancel the other two thousand." Then I asked him again, so Ibn Umar stood up, took my hand, and said: "This man wants me to feed him usury."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from a man of the people of Mecca from his father that a man had a debt owed to another, who said to him, “Pay me sooner and I will reduce what you owe.” He asked Ibn Umar, ؓ, about it, and Ibn Umar forbade it. The man said, “It is only his money; he is gifting me a portion of it.” Ibn Umar forbade him again. The man repeated his request, so Ibn Umar took his hand and said: “This man wants me to feed him usury.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ لِرَجُلٍ عَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ، فَقَالَ عَجِّلْ لِي وَأَضَعُ عَنْكَ، فَسَأَلَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما فَنَهَاهُ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّمَا هُوَ مَالُهُ يَهَبُ لِي مِنْهُ، فَنَهَاهُ فَأَعَادَ عَلَيْهِ فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ وَقَالَ: «إِنَّ هَذَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ أُطْعِمَهُ الرِّبَا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from a man of the people of Mecca from his father that a man owed a debt to another. The creditor said , "Hasten to pay me, and I will reduce it for you." He asked Ibn Umar about that, and he forbade him. The creditor said, "It is only his wealth; he is giving me some of it as a gift." Ibn Umar forbade him again, but he repeated it, so Ibn Umar took his hand and said, "This man wants me to feed him usury."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Ishaq, from the wife of Abu al-Safar, that a woman asked Aisha, ؓ, saying: "Zayd ibn Arqam sold me a slave girl for eight hundred dirhams on credit, then bought her back from me for six hundred." Aisha said "Tell Zayd ibn Arqam, ؓ, that God the Exalted has nullified his jihad if he does not repent."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Masud, ؓ, gave Zayd ibn Khulayda capital for a profit-sharing venture. Zayd then entered into a salam (advance-payment) contract with Atris ibn Urqub for a specified number of young she-camels of specified ages, deliverable at a specified time. When the term came due, Atris delivered some of them, leaving the rest outstanding, and pressed Zayd for the balance. Zayd went to Abdullah [Ibn Masud] and asked him to grant Atris more time for what remained. Abdullah sent for Zayd and asked, “What did you contract to receive by advance payment?” Zayd said, “A specified number of young she-camels, of specified ages, at a specified time.” Abdullah said: “Return what you received from him and take back your capital. Do not put any of our capital into an advance-payment contract for livestock.”

He then entrusted it to ‘Atris ibn ‘Urqub in the form of young she-camels of a known description for a known term. When the term fell due, he took some of them and some remained. ‘Atris pressed him for what remained, so he went to ‘Abdullah (Ibn Mas‘ud) and spoke to him about giving him more time for what remained. ‘Abdullah sent for Zayd and asked him, “What did you entrust?” He said , “I entrusted to him young she-camels of a known description, of known ages, for a known term.” ‘Abdullah said, “Return what you have taken from him and take your capital. Do not entrust any of our wealth in livestock.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “Enter into a salam contract for goods measured by volume in exchange for goods measured by weight, and for goods measured by weight in exchange for goods measured by volume. Do not make a salam contract for volume-measured goods against goods of the same measure, or for weighed goods against goods of the same measure. If the goods are of different kinds and are neither measured by volume nor weighed, there is no harm in exchanging two for one on the spot, but there is no good in doing so on credit.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "Sell what is measured by volume in exchange for what is weighed, and sell what is weighed in exchange for what is measured by volume. But do not sell what is measured by volume in exchange for the same, nor what is weighed in exchange for the same. If it is of one type that is neither measured by volume nor weighed, there is no harm in exchanging two for one, hand to hand. But there is no good in it if delayed."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “Accept nothing except your principal or the very commodity for which you paid in advance. If the goods are of two different kinds and are neither measured by volume nor weighed, there is no harm in exchanging two for one on the spot, nor in doing so on credit.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who reported to him from Amir, who said: “When the two kinds differ, there is no harm in making an advance-payment contract for goods measured by weight in exchange for goods measured by weight, or for goods measured by volume in exchange for goods measured by volume.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, and from Amir, al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata, and Mujahid that they "used to disapprove of cultivation for a third [of the produce]," while Salim and Tawus saw no harm in it. This was because Tawus had land that he would lease out.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَنْ عَامِرٍ، وَالْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ، وَسَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، وَعَطَاءٍ، وَمُجَاهِدٍ، أَنَّهُمْ «كَانُوا يَكْرَهُونَ الزِّرَاعَةَ بِالثُّلُثِ» ، وَإِنَّ سَالِمًا وَطَاوُسًا كَانَا لَا يَرَيَانِ بِذَلِكَ بَأْسًا، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ لِطَاوُسٍ أَرْضٌ يُؤَاجِرُهَا

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ubaydullah ibn Dawud, from Ja'far, who said I said to Salim, "Do you disapprove of sharecropping?"—and he used to practice sharecropping—He replied, "I would not abandon my livelihood on the word of a single man."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ دَاوُدَ، عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ، قَالَ قُلْتُ لِسَالِمٍ: أَتَكْرَهُ الْمُزَارَعَةَ؟ وَكَانَ يُزَارِعُ: قَالَ: «مَا كُنْتُ لِأَدَعَ مَعِيشَتِي لِقَوْلِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Zayd ibn al-Walid, from Jabir ibn Abdillah, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, forbade muhaqalah and muzabanah, and said: “Do not sell the dates of palm trees for two or three years [in advance].”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Husayn from Ibn Rafi ibn Khudayj from his father, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, passed by an orchard and asked, “Whose is this?” I said, “Mine.” He asked, “How did it come to belong to you?” I said, “I rented it.” He said, “Do not rent it in return for any of its produce.” Abu Hanifah added that Ibn Masud, Khabbab, Husayn ibn Ali, and Shurayh each had kharaj land (land subject to a land levy).
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي حُصَيْنٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ ⦗ص: 190⦘ رَافِعِ بْنِ خُدَيْجٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ مَرَّ عَلَى حَائِطٍ، فَقَالَ «لِمَنْ هَذَا؟» قُلْتُ: لِي، قَالَ: «مِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ لَكَ» قَالَ: قُلْتُ: اسْتَأْجَرْتُهُ، قَالَ: «لَا تَسْتَأْجِرَنَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهُ» وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: أَنَّهُ كَانَ لِابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَرْضُ خَرَاجٍ وَلِخَبَّابٍ رضي الله عنه أَرْضُ خَرَاجٍ وَلِحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ رضي الله عنهما، أَرْضُ خَرَاجٍ وَلِشُرَيْحٍ أَرْضُ خَرَاجٍ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Husayn from Ibn Rafi ibn Khudayj from his father, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, passed by a garden and said "To whom does this belong?" I said: "To me." He said: "From where did you get it?" I said: "I rented it." He said: "Do not rent it for any of its produce." Abu Hanifah said that Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, had a land of kharaj, and Khubbab, ؓ, had a land of kharaj, and Husayn ibn Ali, ؓ, had a land of kharaj, and Shurayh had a land of kharaj.

records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Husayn from Ibn Rafi ibn Khudayj from his father, ؓ,
records.matn_en: that the Prophet, ﷺ, passed by an orchard and asked, “Whose is this?” I said, “Mine.” He asked, “How did it come to belong to you?” I said, “I rented it.” He said, “Do not rent it in return for any of its produce.” Abu Hanifah added that Ibn Masud, Khabbab, Husayn ibn Ali, and Shurayh each had kharaj land (land subject to a land levy).

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he said regarding the slave who has a contract of manumission: "He is freed in proportion to what he has paid, and remains enslaved in proportion to what he has not paid."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: “When a mukatab has paid the value of his person, he becomes a creditor [for any amount paid beyond that value].”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «إِذَا أَدَّى قِيمَةَ رَقَبَتِهِ فَهُوَ غَرِيمٌ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «إِذَا أَدَّى قِيمَةَ رَقَبَتِهِ فَهُوَ غَرِيمٌ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said "When one pays the value of his own neck (i.e., his blood money), he is a debtor."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه قَالَ «إِذَا أَدَّى قِيمَةَ رَقَبَتِهِ فَهُوَ غَرِيمٌ»

records.matn_ar: إِذَا أَدَّى قِيمَةَ رَقَبَتِهِ فَهُوَ غَرِيمٌ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said "
records.matn_en: that Ibn Masud, ؓ, said: “When a mukatab has paid the value of his person, he becomes a creditor [for any amount paid beyond that value].”
records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with Ibn Masud’s quoted ruling.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Zayd ibn Thabit, ؓ, who said "He is a slave as long as a dirham remains upon him." And Zayd said: "If he dies, his master takes all his wealth."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Ali, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Shurayh, ؓ, that they said regarding the slave who has a contract of manumission and dies leaving sufficient wealth: "He pays the remainder of his contract, and what remains is inheritance for his heirs."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said The opinion of Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and Shurayh, ؓ, regarding the slave who has a contract of manumission and then dies is more preferable to me than the opinion of Zayd. However, the opinion of Zayd during his lifetime is more preferable to me than their opinion.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ وَابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ وَشُرَيْحٌ رضي الله عنهم فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ إِذَا مَاتَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ ⦗ص: 191⦘ مِنْ قَوْلِ زَيْدٍ، وَقَوْلُ زَيْدٍ فِي الْحَيَاةِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ قَوْلِهِمْ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ وَابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ وَشُرَيْحٌ رضي الله عنهم فِي الْمُكَاتَبِ إِذَا مَاتَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ ⦗ص: 191⦘ مِنْ قَوْلِ زَيْدٍ، وَقَوْلُ زَيْدٍ فِي الْحَيَاةِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ قَوْلِهِمْ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from a man from Aisha, ؓ, that she had a slave who had a contract of manumission with her, and some of his payment was still due. He used to enter upon her, but when he heard the statement of Zayd, he said "He wants to enslave me again." So he paid her what was due, and she then veiled herself from him.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim and Shurayh, that they both said: “The master of a mukatab ranks alongside the creditors for whatever remains due on the mukatab’s emancipation contract.”

records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَشُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّهُمَا قَالَا «يَضْرِبُ مَوْلَى الْمُكَاتَبِ مَعَ الْغُرَمَاءِ مَا بَقَى عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ»

records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَشُرَيْحٍ، أَنَّهُمَا قَالَا «يَضْرِبُ مَوْلَى الْمُكَاتَبِ مَعَ الْغُرَمَاءِ مَا بَقَى عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim that he said regarding a slave jointly owned by two men, where one of them granted his share in *kitabah* (contract of manumission): "That is not permissible except with the permission of his partner."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي عَبْدٍ بَيْنَ رَجُلَيْنِ، كَاتَبَ أَحَدُهُمَا نَصِيبَهُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ «لَا يَجُوزُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ شَرِيكِهِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said When a man writes a single contract of manumission by payment for his slaves, making their installments the same, and says, “If you pay, you are free, and if you are unable, you remain slaves,” then if one of them dies, it does not reduce anything from their obligation.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ " إِذَا كَاتَبَ الرَّجُلُ عَبِيدَهَ مُكَاتَبَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَجَعَلَ نُجُومَهُمْ وَاحِدَةً، وَقَالَ: إِنْ أَدَّيْتُمَ فَأَنْتُمْ أَحْرَارٌ، وَإِنْ عَجَزْتُمْ فَأَنْتُمْ رَقِيقٌ، فَمَاتَ وَاحِدٌ لَمْ يَرْفَعْ عَنْهُمْ بِهِ شَيْئًا "
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ " إِذَا كَاتَبَ الرَّجُلُ عَبِيدَهَ مُكَاتَبَةً وَاحِدَةً، فَجَعَلَ نُجُومَهُمْ وَاحِدَةً، وَقَالَ: إِنْ أَدَّيْتُمَ فَأَنْتُمْ أَحْرَارٌ، وَإِنْ عَجَزْتُمْ فَأَنْتُمْ رَقِيقٌ، فَمَاتَ وَاحِدٌ لَمْ يَرْفَعْ عَنْهُمْ بِهِ شَيْئًا "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that a man guaranteed to another the amount owed by his mukatab. That guarantee is invalid. How could it be valid? He has only guaranteed his own money on behalf of his own slave.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ رَجُلًا، تَكَفَّلَ لِرَجُلٍ بِمَالٍ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ، إِنَّ ذَلِكَ بَاطِلٌ، وَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ، وَإِنَّمَا كُفِلَ بِمَالِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ رَجُلًا، تَكَفَّلَ لِرَجُلٍ بِمَالٍ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ، إِنَّ ذَلِكَ بَاطِلٌ، وَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ، وَإِنَّمَا كُفِلَ بِمَالِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that a man guaranteed a sum of money on behalf of another man’s slave who was under a contract of manumission by paying it for him. That is invalid. How can it be permissible when the guarantee was for his own wealth on behalf of his slave?
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، «أَنَّ رَجُلًا، تَكَفَّلَ لِرَجُلٍ بِمَالٍ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِهِ، إِنَّ ذَلِكَ بَاطِلٌ، وَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ، وَإِنَّمَا كُفِلَ بِمَالِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِهِ»

records.text_en: Abu Yusuf said A narrator related to me from Amir that he said: "It is neither to be sold nor gifted. If a slave woman is contracted for emancipation and her master has intercourse with her, her child holds the same status as her and is emancipated from one-third [of the estate]."
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو يُوسُفَ: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَدِّثٌ عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَا يُبَاعُ وَلَا يُوهَبُ، وَإِنْ كَاتَبَ جَارِيَةً فَوَطِئَهَا مَوْلَاهَا فَوَلَدُهَا بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا يُعْتَقُ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ»
records.raw_text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو يُوسُفَ: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَدِّثٌ عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَا يُبَاعُ وَلَا يُوهَبُ، وَإِنْ كَاتَبَ جَارِيَةً فَوَطِئَهَا مَوْلَاهَا فَوَلَدُهَا بِمَنْزِلَتِهَا يُعْتَقُ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, would announce from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, that "the sale of mothers of children is forbidden. When a slave woman gives birth to her master’s child, she is no longer subject to slavery thereafter."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, ؓ, who said When the Prophet, ﷺ, sent out an army or a detachment, he would advise its leader to fear God in his own conduct and to treat those with him well. Then he would say: "March forth in the cause of God, in the name of God. Fight those who disbelieve in God. Do not embezzle, do not betray, do not kill a child, and do not mutilate. When you meet your enemy from the polytheists, call them to Islam. If they accept, then accept it from them and refrain from fighting them. Then call them to migrate from their land to the abode of the emigrants. If they refuse, inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims—God’s ruling applies to them as it does to the believers, but they will have no share in the spoils of war or booty. If they refuse, then call them to pay the jizyah. If they accept, then accept it from them and refrain from fighting them. If they do not accept, then fight them. If you besiege the people of a fortress, do not grant them the covenant of God or the covenant of His Messenger, but grant them your own covenant and the covenant of your fathers. If you violate your covenant, it is less severe than violating God’s covenant. If they ask you to let them surrender to God’s judgment, do not do so. Instead, let them surrender to your judgment, then decide their fate as you see fit."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Rawḥ ibn Musāfir, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from Muslim ibn Haysam, from al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Muqarrin al-Muzanī, ؓ, who said Whenever the Messenger of God, ﷺ, sent a commander over an army or a detachment, he would advise him personally to fear God and to treat well those Muslims with him. Then he would say to them: "March forth in the name of God and in the path of God. Fight those who disbelieve in God. Do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill children. When you meet your enemy from the polytheists, call them to three matters—invite them to Islam. If they accept, then refrain from fighting them and accept from them. Then call them to migrate from their land to the land of the emigrants, and inform them that if they do so, they will have what the emigrants have, and upon them will be what is upon the emigrants. If they enter Islam but choose to remain in their land, inform them that they are like the Bedouin Muslims—God’s ruling applies to them as it applies to the Muslims, but they will have no share in the spoils of war or booty unless they fight alongside you. If they refuse, then call them to pay the jizyah. If they accept, then refrain from fighting them and accept it from them. If they refuse, then seek God’s help against them and fight them. If you besiege the people of a fortress and they wish for you to grant them the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger, do not grant them the protection of God or the protection of His Messenger. Instead, grant them your protection and the protection of your companions, for if you violate your protection or that of your companions, it is better for you than violating the protection of God and His Messenger. If you besiege the people of a fortress and they wish to surrender to God’s judgment, do not grant them God’s judgment. Instead, grant them your judgment and the judgment of your companions, for you do not know whether you will judge among them according to God’s judgment or not." Muqātil said: "I examined the lands of Khurāsān that were conquered during the time of ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, ؓ, and I did not find in any of them the protection of God or the protection of His Messenger, but only the protection of the Imam and his companions among the Muslims."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ رَوْحِ بْنِ مُسَافِرٍ، عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ حَيَّانَ، عَنْ مُسْلِمِ بْنِ هَيْصَمٍ، عَنِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ الْمُقَرَّنِ الْمُزَنِيِّ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا بَعَثَ أَمِيرًا عَلَى جَيْشٍ أَوْ سَرِيَّةٍ أَوْصَاهُ فِي خَاصَّةِ نَفْسِهِ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ خَيْرًا ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمُ: " اغْزُوا بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، قَاتِلُوا مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا تَغُلُّوا، وَلَا تَغْدِرُوا، وَلَا تُمَثِّلُوا، وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا وَلِيدًا، وَإِذَا لَقِيتَ عَدُوَّكَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى ثَلَاثِ خِصَالٍ أَوْ ثَلَاثِ خِلَالٍ: ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، فَإِنْ قَبِلُوا فَكُفُّوا عَنْهُمْ، وَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ، وَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى التَّحَوُّلِ مِنْ دَارِهِمْ إِلَى دَارِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ، وَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ إِنْ فَعَلُوا لَهُمْ مَا لِلْمُهَاجِرِينَ، وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ مَا عَلَى الْمُهَاجِرِينَ، وَإِنْ دَخَلُوا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَاخْتَارُوا دَارَهُمْ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَأَعْرَابِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، يَجْرِي عَلَيْهِمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ مَا يَجْرِي عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَلَا يَكُونُ لَهُمْ مِنَ الْفَيْءِ وَالْغَنِيمَةِ شَيْءٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا مَعَهُمْ، وَإِنْ أَبَوْا فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى إِعْطَاءِ الْجِزْيَةِ، فَإِنْ قَبِلُوا فَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ وَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ ⦗ص: 194⦘ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ أَبَوْا فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَقَاتِلْهُمْ، وَإِذَا حَاصَرْتَ أَهْلَ حِصْنٍ فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ تَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ فَلَا تَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَلَا ذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، وَلَكِنِ اجْعَلْ لَهُمْ ذِمَّتَكَ وَذِمَّةَ أَصْحَابِكَ؛ فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ تَخْفِرْ ذِمَّتَكَ وَذِمَّةَ أَصْحَابِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَنْ تَخْفِرَ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، وَإِذَا حَاصَرْتَ أَهْلَ حِصْنٍ فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ يَنْزِلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ حُكْمَ اللَّهِ، وَلَكِنِ اجْعَلْ لَهُمْ حُكْمَكَ وَحُكْمَ أَصْحَابِكَ، فَإِنَّكَ لَا تَدْرِي هَلْ تُصِيبُ فِيهِمْ حُكْمَ اللَّهِ أَمْ لَا؟ " قَالَ مُقَاتِلٌ: فَنَظَرْتُ فِيمَا فُتِحَ مِنْ أَرْضِ خُرَاسَانَ فِي عَهْدِ عُمَرَ وَعُثْمَانَ رضي الله عنهما فَلَمْ أَجِدْ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْهَا ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَلَا ذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، إِلَّا ذِمَّةَ الْإِمَامِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ مِمَّنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ

الْإِسْلَامِ وَاخْتَارُوا دَارَهُمْ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَأَعْرَابِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، يَجْرِي عَلَيْهِمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ مَا يَجْرِي عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَلَا يَكُونُ لَهُمْ مِنَ الْفَيْءِ وَالْغَنِيمَةِ شَيْءٌ إِلَّا أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا مَعَهُمْ، وَإِنْ أَبَوْا فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى إِعْطَاءِ الْجِزْيَةِ، فَإِنْ قَبِلُوا فَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ وَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ أَبَوْا فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَقَاتِلْهُمْ، وَإِذَا حَاصَرْتَ أَهْلَ حِصْنٍ فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ تَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ فَلَا تَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَلَا ذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، وَلَكِنِ اجْعَلْ لَهُمْ ذِمَّتَكَ وَذِمَّةَ أَصْحَابِكَ؛ فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ تَخْفِرْ ذِمَّتَكَ وَذِمَّةَ أَصْحَابِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَنْ تَخْفِرَ ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، وَإِذَا حَاصَرْتَ أَهْلَ حِصْنٍ فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ يَنْزِلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ حُكْمَ اللَّهِ، وَلَكِنِ اجْعَلْ لَهُمْ حُكْمَكَ وَحُكْمَ أَصْحَابِكَ، فَإِنَّكَ لَا تَدْرِي هَلْ تُصِيبُ فِيهِمْ حُكْمَ اللَّهِ أَمْ لَا؟ " قَالَ مُقَاتِلٌ: فَنَظَرْتُ فِيمَا فُتِحَ مِنْ أَرْضِ خُرَاسَانَ فِي عَهْدِ عُمَرَ وَعُثْمَانَ رضي الله عنهما فَلَمْ أَجِدْ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْهَا ذِمَّةَ اللَّهِ وَلَا ذِمَّةَ رَسُولِهِ، إِلَّا ذِمَّةَ الْإِمَامِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ مِمَّنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Rawḥ ibn Musāfir, from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from Muslim ibn Haysam, from al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Muqarrin al-Muzanī, ؓ, who said Whenever the Messenger of God, ﷺ, sent a commander over an army or a detachment, he would advise him personally to fear God and to treat well those Muslims with him. Then he would say to them: "March forth in the name of God and in the path of God. Fight those who disbelieve in God. Do not embezzle, do not betray, do not mutilate, and do not kill children. When you meet your enemy from the polytheists, call them to three matters—invite them to Islam. If they accept, then refrain from fighting them and accept from them. Then call them to migrate from their land to the land of the emigrants, and inform them that if they do so, they will have what the emigrants have, and upon them will be what is upon the emigrants. If they enter Islam but choose to remain in their land, inform them that they are like the Bedouin Muslims—God’s ruling applies to them as it applies to the Muslims, but they will have no share in the spoils of war or booty unless they fight alongside you. If they refuse, then call them to pay the jizyah. If they accept, then refrain from fighting them and accept it from them. If they refuse, then seek God’s help against them and fight them. If you besiege the people of a fortress and they wish for you to grant them the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger, do not grant them the protection of God or the protection of His Messenger. Instead, grant them your protection and the protection of your companions, for if you violate your protection or that of your companions, it is better for you than violating the protection of God and His Messenger. If you besiege the people of a fortress and they wish to surrender to God’s judgment, do not grant them God’s judgment. Instead, grant them your judgment and the judgment of your companions, for you do not know whether you will judge among them according to God’s judgment or not." Muqātil said: "I examined the lands of Khurāsān that were conquered during the time of ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, ؓ, and I did not find in any of them the protection of God or the protection of His Messenger, but only the protection of the Imam and his companions among the Muslims."
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ رَوْحِ بْنِ مُسَافِرٍ، عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ حَيَّانَ، عَنْ مُسْلِمِ بْنِ هَيْصَمٍ، عَنِ النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ الْمُقَرَّنِ الْمُزَنِيِّ رضي الله عنه،

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he "used to prefer that the leader grant an extra share to incite the people, but as for the extra share while the troops are already engaged in battle..."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يُحِبُّ لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُنَفِّلَ لِيُغْرِيَ النَّاسَ، وَأَمَّا النَّفَلُ وَالْقَوْمُ فِي الْقِتَالِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يُحِبُّ لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُنَفِّلَ لِيُغْرِيَ النَّاسَ، وَأَمَّا النَّفَلُ وَالْقَوْمُ فِي الْقِتَالِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah al-Thaqafi from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, assessed a levy of one dirham and one qafiz per jarib on each cultivable tract, ten dirhams on vineyards, and five dirhams on fields of green fodder crops (al-ruṭba), while exempting date palms.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الثَّقَفِيِّ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «فَرَضَ عَلَى كُلِّ أَرْضٍ تَصْلُحُ لِلزَّرْعِ دِرْهَمًا وَقَفِيزًا عَلَى الْجَرِيبِ، وَعَلَى الْكَرْمِ عَشْرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ، وَعَلَى الرُّطَبَةِ خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَأَهْدَرَ النَّخْلَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الثَّقَفِيِّ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ «فَرَضَ عَلَى كُلِّ أَرْضٍ تَصْلُحُ لِلزَّرْعِ دِرْهَمًا وَقَفِيزًا عَلَى الْجَرِيبِ، وَعَلَى الْكَرْمِ عَشْرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ، وَعَلَى الرُّطَبَةِ خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَأَهْدَرَ النَّخْلَ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah al-Thaqafi from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, imposed on every cultivable land a dirham and a qafiz per jarib, on vineyards ten dirhams, and on fresh dates five dirhams, and he exempted palm trees.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said If the enemy seizes a slave or property belonging to a man, and the Muslims then capture it, if the owner finds it before the division, he may take it without payment. But if he finds it after the division, he may take it by paying its value.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ «إِذَا أَحْرَزَ الْعَدُوُّ الْعَبْدَ الْمَتَاعَ لِرَجُلٍ، فَأَصَابَهُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ، فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ مَوْلَاهُ قَبْلَ الْقِسْمَةِ أَخَذَهُ بِغَيْرِ شَيْءٍ، وَإِنْ وَجَدَهُ بَعْدَ الْقِسْمَةِ أَخَذَهُ بِالْقِيمَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the slave captured by the enemy and then recovered by the Muslims: "If his owner finds him before he is divided [among the soldiers], he may take him. If he finds him after he has been divided, he may take him by paying its price. The same applies to goods."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he used to disapprove of carrying weapons and horses to the people of war, but saw no harm in other trade besides that. He said , "And that nothing be carried to them is more beloved to me."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “The walāʾ (the bond of clientage created by emancipation) is neither sold nor inherited; it is like blood lineage.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said "Loyalty is not sold, nor is it inherited; it is in the position of lineage."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said When the collateral is for more than its value and it perishes, the creditor is a trustee regarding the excess. But if it is for less than its value and it perishes, the debtor compensates for the difference.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said "Guaranteeing for a slave under contract of manumission is invalid because what is guaranteed for him is his own property."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, that he said Conceal whatever you wish. Whoever conceals a secret of goodness, God will clothe him in its robe, and whoever conceals a secret of evil, God will clothe him in its robe.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Aisha, ؓ, that she said: “Misfortune is bound up with what is said.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said When two matters perplex you, assume that the one more beloved to God is the easier of the two.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from a companion of his called Khateer, from al-Hasan, that he said regarding the child: "When he reaches the age of twelve, his good deeds are recorded for him, but his bad deeds are not recorded against him, until he reaches maturity, at which point his good deeds are recorded for him and his bad deeds are recorded against him."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Habibah, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda, ؓ, say: I was riding behind the Messenger of God, ﷺ, when he said , "O Abu al-Darda, whoever testifies that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God sincerely, Paradise is obligatory for him." I said to him, "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He remained silent for a while, then repeated his statement. I said again, "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He remained silent for a while, then repeated his statement. I said once more, "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He said, "Even if he commits adultery and steals, even if it displeases Abu al-Darda." Abu al-Darda used to narrate this hadith every Friday near the pulpit of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, placing his finger on his nose and saying, "Even if he commits adultery and steals, even if it displeases Abu al-Darda."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Hind, from Amir, that Amir accompanied Ibn Abbas (ؓ) on a ship to Wasit. Amir began cursing his servant, so Ibn Abbas forbade him from doing so and said "I see you frequently cursing your servants or slaves." Amir replied: "Every male or female slave I have ever cursed is free for the sake of God."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Awn, who said There was a man so sharp-tongued and hard to put up with that people could not bear him. Another man insulted him, saying: “By God, you are not attributed to the father whose name you bear; ask your mother about that.” The man went to his mother and asked her, threatening: “By God, I will strike you with a sword unless you tell me the truth.” She said: “Your father is so-and-so, not the man whose name you bear.” And that was true. He struck and killed her. When this reached the Prophet, ﷺ, he said: “For that, he is the worst of the three.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَوْنٍ، قَالَ كَانَ رَجُلٌ لَهُ لِسَانٌ وَجِلْدٌ لَا يُطَاقُ، فَشَاتَمَهُ رَجُلٌ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: وَاللَّهِ مَا تُدْعَى إِلَى أَبِيكَ الَّذِي أَنْتَ لَهُ، فَسَلْ عَنْ ذَلِكَ أُمَّكَ، قَالَ: فَأَتَاهَا فَسَأَلَهَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهِ لَأَضْرِبَنَّكِ بِالسَّيْفِ إِنْ لَمْ تَصْدُقِينِي، فَقَالَتْ: إِنَّ أَبَاكَ فُلَانٌ، لِغَيْرِ الَّذِي كَانَ يُدْعَى لَهُ، وَكَانَ كَذَلِكَ فَضَرَبَهَا بِالسَّيْفِ فَقَتَلَهَا، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ: «هُوَ شَرُّ الثَّلَاثَةِ لِذَلِكَ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Awn, who said There was a man with a sharp tongue and tough skin who could not be matched. Another man insulted him, so he said to him, "By God, you are not called to the father you claim. Ask your mother about that." The man went to his mother and asked her about it, saying, "By God, I will strike you with the sword if you do not tell me the truth." She said, "Your father is so-and-so, not the one you were called to." And it was indeed so. Then he struck her with the sword and killed her. This reached the Prophet, ﷺ, and he said, "He is the worst of the three for that."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abd al-A'la the Judge—or the Preacher, Abu Bakr was uncertain—who said that the disciples longed to see Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both, and said to Isa ibn Maryam, ﷺ: “Father, if you would bring him out to us, we could see him and greet him.” Isa took them to Yahya’s grave and called, “Yahya, rise by God’s permission.” Yahya emerged from his grave, shaking his head; half of it had turned white. The disciples said: “You left us with a black head. What happened to it?” Yahya said: “I heard Isa’s voice and thought the Hour had come.” Isa said: “Would you like me to supplicate to God to revive you so you could live in this world?” Yahya said: “I adjure you by God and by our kinship”—for he was Isa’s maternal cousin—“By God, the bitterness of death has not yet left my chest”—or, he said, “my throat.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْأَعْلَى الْقَاضِي أَوِ الْقَاصِّ، شَكَّ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، قَالَ بَلَغَنِي " أَنَّ الْحَوَارِيِّينَ اشْتَاقُوا إِلَى يَحْيَى بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا عَلَيْهِمَا الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ فَقَالُوا يَا أَبَهْ: لِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ عليه الصلاة والسلام، يَا أَبَهْ، إِنْ رَأَيْتَ أَنْ تُخْرِجَهُ لَنَا فَنَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهِ وَنُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْهِ، فَذَهَبَ بِهِمْ إِلَى قَبْرِهِ فَنَادَاهُ: يَا يَحْيَى، قُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: فَخَرَجَ مِنْ قَبْرِهِ يَنْفُضُ رَأْسَهُ قَدِ ابْيَضَّ نِصْفُ رَأْسِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ: فَارَقْتَنَا وَأَنْتَ أَسْوَدُ الرَّأْسِ، فَمَا شَأْنُ رَأْسِكَ؟ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ عِيسَى فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهَا السَّاعَةُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عِيسَى عليه السلام: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ أَدْعُوَ اللَّهَ فَيُحْيِيَكَ ⦗ص: 199⦘ وَتَعِيشَ فِي الدُّنْيَا، فَقَالَ: أَنْشُدُكَ اللَّهَ وَالرَّحِمَ، وَكَانَ ابْنَ خَالَتِهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا ذَهَبَتْ مَرَارَةُ الْمَوْتِ مِنْ صَدْرِي، أَوْ مِنْ حَلْقِي بَعْدُ "

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abd al-A'la the Judge—or the Preacher, Abu Bakr was uncertain—who said It reached me that the disciples longed for Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace and blessings be upon them both, so they said, "O father"—to Isa ibn Maryam, ﷺ—"O father, if you see fit, bring him out to us so we may look at him and greet him." So he took them to his grave and called out to him, "O Yahya, rise by the permission of God." He said: He emerged from his grave, shaking his head, half of which had turned white. The disciples said to him, "You left us with a black head, so what has happened to your head?" He said, "I heard the voice of Isa and thought it was the Hour." Isa, ﷺ, said to him, "Would you like me to supplicate to God to revive you and you live in this world?" He said, "I adjure you by God and kinship—for he was his cousin—by God, the bitterness of death has not yet left my chest—or my throat."

records.matn_en: that the disciples longed to see Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both, and said to Isa ibn Maryam, ﷺ: “Father, if you would bring him out to us, we could see him and greet him.” Isa took them to Yahya’s grave and called, “Yahya, rise by God’s permission.” Yahya emerged from his grave, shaking his head; half of it had turned white. The disciples said: “You left us with a black head. What happened to it?” Yahya said: “I heard Isa’s voice and thought the Hour had come.” Isa said: “Would you like me to supplicate to God to revive you so you could live in this world?” Yahya said: “I adjure you by God and by our kinship”—for he was Isa’s maternal cousin—“By God, the bitterness of death has not yet left my chest”—or, he said, “my throat.”
records.boundary_review_note: The source itself is unsure whether Abd al-Ala was al-Qadi or al-Qass. It says Abu Bakr expressed the uncertainty, then reports a “reached me” account; retain the ambiguity without resolving the route.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham that a group of people passed by some water. They asked its owners, "Where is the well?" But they refused to guide them and refused to give them the bucket. The people said , "Woe to you! Our necks and the necks of our mounts are about to be severed from thirst." Yet they still refused to give them or guide them. This was mentioned to Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, and he said, "Why did you not strike them with weapons?"

As for the house, its bad luck is its narrowness and the wickedness of its neighbors. As for the bad luck in the woman, it is her bad character and the barrenness of her womb. As for the horse, it is that it is unruly.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, that a woman came to the Prophet of God, ﷺ. After she left, Aisha, ؓ, said: “Messenger of God, she is short.” The Prophet said to her: “Ask her to pardon you for that.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq from Mujahid who said Gabriel said to the Prophet, ﷺ, "I came to you last night, but nothing prevented me from entering upon you except this curtain that has images on it and this statue at the door. So remove this dog, make this curtain into two cushions to be stepped on, and cut off the head of the statue at this door so that it becomes like a tree." He said: The Prophet, ﷺ, did that, and the dog belonged to a child.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، قَالَ قَالَ جِبْرِيلُ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَتَيْتُكَ الْبَارِحَةَ فَلَمْ يَمْنَعْنِي مِنَ الدُّخُولِ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا هَذَا السِّتْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَمَاثِيلُ، وَإِلَّا هَذَا التِّمْثَالُ الَّذِي فِي الْبَابِ، فَأَخْرِجُوا هَذَا الْكَلْبَ، وَاجْعَلُوا هَذَا السِّتْرَ وِسَادَتَيْنِ تُوطَآنِ، وَاقْطَعُوا رَأْسَ التِّمْثَالِ فِي هَذَا ⦗ص: 201⦘ الْبَابِ فَيَكُونُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الشَّجَرَةِ» قَالَ: فَفَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذَلِكَ، وَكَانَ الْكَلْبُ لِصَبِيٍّ

records.text_en: Yusuf related to us from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Ishaq that the Prophet, ﷺ, hung a curtain with images in his house. Gabriel was delayed in coming to him, then he came and the Prophet said , "What delayed you from me?" He replied, "We do not enter a house in which there is a dog or images. Spread out this curtain, cut off the heads of the images, and remove this dog."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, and Abu Hanifah said that the Prophet, ﷺ, spoke of stabbing, plague, drowning, burning, death in a collapse, being devoured by a wild beast, abdominal illness, a woman who dies in childbirth or postpartum, and a pregnant woman who dies [with her fetus], saying: “All of these are martyrdom.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ «قَالَ فِي الطَّعْنِ وَالطَّاعُونِ وَالْغَرَقِ وَالْحَرَقِ وَالْهَدْمِ وَأَكْلِ السَّبْعِ وَالْبَطْنِ وَالنُّفَسَاءِ وَالْمَرْأَةِ تَمُوتُ جُمَعًا، كُلُّ ذَلِكَ شَهَادَةٌ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, and Abu Hanifah said It reached me from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said regarding being stabbed, plague, drowning, burning, collapse, being eaten by a beast, abdominal illness, a woman who dies in childbirth, and a woman who dies with a group—all of these are martyrdom.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said "The Smoke has passed, the Great Seizure has passed, and the moon has split."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ayyub al-Ta'i, who said I think it is from Mujahid, that a woman came to the Prophet, ﷺ, while she was pregnant, carrying an infant with her, and a weaned child who was holding her hand and walking with her. He said: That day, she did not ask the Messenger of God, ﷺ, for anything except that he gave it to her. Then he said: "They are bearers, mothers, compassionate toward their children. Were it not for what they do to their husbands, their praying women would enter Paradise."

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ امْرَأَةً أَتَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهِيَ حُبْلَى، تَحْمِلُ مَعَهَا صَبِيًّا رَضِيعًا، وَمَعَهَا صَبِيُّ فَطِيمٌ تَمَسَّكَ بِيَدِهَا يَمْشِي مَعَهَا، قَالَ: فَمَا سَأَلَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَئِذٍ شَيْئًا إِلَّا أَعْطَاهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: «حَامِلَاتٌ وَالِدَاتٌ رَحِيمَاتٌ بِأَوْلَادِهِنَّ، وَلَوْلَا مَا يَصْنَعْنَ بِأَزْوَاجِهِنَّ دَخَلَ مُصَلِّيَاتُهُنَّ الْجَنَّةَ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ayyub al-Ta'i, who said I think it is from Mujahid,
records.matn_en: that a woman came to the Prophet, ﷺ, while she was pregnant, carrying an infant with her, and a weaned child who was holding her hand and walking with her. He said: That day, she did not ask the Messenger of God, ﷺ, for anything except that he gave it to her. Then he said: "They are bearers, mothers, compassionate toward their children. Were it not for what they do to their husbands, their praying women would enter Paradise."
records.boundary_review_note: Ayyub explicitly says he thinks the report is from Mujahid; preserve that uncertainty. The woman and Prophet are participants in the report, not additional named transmitters.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Hakam ibn Ziyad al-Jazari that a woman was proposed to her father, so she said I will not marry until I come to the Prophet, ﷺ, and ask him about the husband’s right over his wife. He said: So she came to him and said: O Messenger of God, what is the husband’s right over the wife? He said: If she leaves his house without his permission, God, the angels, the Trustworthy Spirit, the keepers of the Abode of Mercy, and the keepers of the Abode of Punishment will continue to curse her until she returns to his house. She said: O Messenger of God, what is the husband’s right over his wife? He said: If he calls her while she is on the back of a saddle, she has no right to refuse him. Then she said: O Messenger of God, what is the husband’s right over his wife? He said: She should please him when he is angry. A man said: Even if he is unjust? He said: Even if he is unjust. The woman said: I will not marry after what I have heard.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah that he said It reached me that a Bedouin said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, "Shall I prostrate to you?" The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said, "It is not proper for anyone to prostrate to anyone. If I were to command anyone to prostrate, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah, from someone who narrated from Sa'd, ؓ, that he said The believer will be seated in his grave and asked, "Who is your Lord?" He will say, "God." Then he will be asked, "What is your religion?" He will say, "Islam." Then he will be asked, "Who is your prophet?" He will say, "Muhammad." Then God will expand his grave, and he will see his place in Paradise. The disbeliever will be seated in his grave and asked, "Who is your Lord?" He will say, "Hah," like one who is confused about something. Then he will be asked, "What is your religion?" He will say, "Hah," like one who is confused about something. Then he will be asked, "Who is your prophet?" He will say, "Hah," like one who is confused about something. records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from some of his companions that Gabriel came to the Prophet, ﷺ, wearing a turban, the end of which he had let hang down behind him.

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah said Abu Bakr borrowed seven thousand dirhams from the public treasury, which remained as his debt, so he bequeathed that it be repaid on his behalf.
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: «إِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ اسْتَقْرَضَ مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَالِ سَبْعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَهِيَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَوْصَى بِهَا أَنْ تُقْضَى عَنْهُ»
records.raw_text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: «إِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ اسْتَقْرَضَ مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَالِ سَبْعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَهِيَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَوْصَى بِهَا أَنْ تُقْضَى عَنْهُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said On the Day of Resurrection, something like clouds will be brought to a man, and it will be said: "This is the good you did for the people, which continued to be practiced after you."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Awn ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said People will come forward on the Day of Resurrection in three registers: a register containing the account, a register containing the blessings, and a register containing the sins. The blessings will be weighed against the account and will consume it, leaving the sins, and it is in them that forgiveness lies.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from a man of the people of Syria, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that a man came to him asking, “Should I marry so-and-so?” He discouraged him from marrying her. The man came again and asked the same, and he discouraged him again. Then the Prophet said: “A dark-complexioned, fertile woman is dearer to me than a beautiful, barren one. Do you not know that I will take pride in your numbers before the nations? You may even see a miscarried child standing in indignation [at the gate of Paradise]. It will be told, ‘Enter Paradise,’ and it will say, ‘No, not until my parents enter it.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّامِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ أَتَزَوَّجُ ⦗ص: 205⦘ فُلَانَةً؟ فَنَهَاهُ عَنْهَا، ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ أَيْضًا فَقَالَ: أَتَزَوَّجُ فُلَانَةً؟ فَنَهَاهُ عَنْهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: " سَوْدَاءُ وَلُودٌ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ حَسْنَاءَ عَاقِرٍ، أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنِّي مُكَاثِرٌ بِكُمُ الْأُمَمَ، حَتَّى إِنَّكَ لَتَرَى السَّقْطَ مُحَبْنَطًا، يُقَالُ لَهُ: ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ فَيَقُولُ: لَا، حَتَّى يَدْخُلَهَا أَبَوَايَ "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ata ibn Abi Rabah from Abu Hurayrah, ؓ, who said When the star rises, the affliction is lifted from the people of every land.

records.boundary_review_note: The saying is attributed to Abu Hurayrah through Ata ibn Abi Rabah.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah, who said It reached me that a king of the Children of Israel died, so they came to a devout monk and wanted to make him king. He refused unless they allowed him to wander for six months and then look into their affairs for six months. They agreed to that. While he was wandering during those six months, he came upon a household and stayed with them. Their cow returned to them, and they milked it. They sold some of the milk for their food and kept some. He said, "Do you have no livelihood except this?" They said, "No." He said, "If I took this, I could live on it." So he stayed with them. The next day, the cow returned, but there was not a drop in its udder. He asked, "What is the matter with your cow?" They said, "It has never happened like this before." He asked, "What do you think is the matter with it?" The head of the household said, "I think the king has entertained an unjust thought in his heart, so the blessing has been lifted." He recognized that and abandoned what he had intended. He stayed with them, and the next day, the cow returned with a full udder. He asked, "What is the matter with it?" The old man said, "The king has abandoned what his heart was entertaining."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Al-Haytham that the Prophet, ﷺ, was fair-complexioned with a reddish tinge, full-bodied and broad-shouldered, with a line of hair on his chest. records.boundary_review_note: The report describes the Prophet through al-Haytham.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Sakhrah that a group from the tribe of Muharib camped near Medina. The Prophet, ﷺ, bought a camel from them in exchange for a wasq of dates. When he took the camel and disappeared among the houses of Medina, they said , "We gave it to a man we do not know." An old woman among them said, "I have seen the face of this man—God would never clothe him in treachery." Soon after, he sent for them and invited them. He ordered the dates to be brought and spread on a leather mat. He said, "Eat," and they ate until they were full. Then he gave them their full measure of dates. They said, "We have never seen the like of this day in fulfillment."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي صَخْرَةَ، " أَنَّ رَكْبًا مِنْ مُحَارِبٍ نَزَلُوا إِلَى جَنْبِ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَاشْتَرَى مِنْهُمُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَزُورًا بِوَسْقٍ مِنْ تَمْرٍ، فَلَمَّا أَنْ ذَهَبَ بِهَا وَتَوَارَى فِي بُيُوتِ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَقَالُوا أَعْطَيْنَاهَا رَجُلًا لَا نَعْرِفُهُ، فَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ مِنْهُمْ: لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ صَفْحَةَ الرَّجُلِ، مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُلْبِسَهُ غَدَرَةً ⦗ص: 207⦘ ، فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّا أَنْ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ فَدَعَاهُمْ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِالتَّمْرِ ثُمَّ نُثِرَ عَلَى نِطَعٍ، فَقَالَ: كُلُوا فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى شَبِعُوا، ثُمَّ أَوْفَاهُمْ تَمْرَهُمْ، فَقَالُوا: مَا رَأَيْنَا كَالْيَوْمِ فِي الْوَفَاءِ "

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Dhawbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from ‘Awn ibn ‘Abd Allah that Abu al-Darda’, ؓ, said "Nothing prevents me from memorizing the Quran except that I fear I may not fulfill its rights." A man from the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, said: "Sleeping as a scholar is better than sleeping as an ignorant one." Another man from the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, said to him: "Learn it and act upon what is in it while you are awake, and I guarantee what you speak of in your sleep."

He said: No. Ali said: Have you seen Abu Bakr and Umar, ؓ? He said: No. Ali said: If you had told me that you had seen the Prophet, ﷺ, I would have struck your neck, and if you had told me that you had seen Abu Bakr and Umar, I would have punished you severely.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, that Ibn Abbas entered upon Umar when he was wounded and said: “Rejoice! By God, your Islam brought honor, your migration brought victory, and your rule was just. You accompanied the Messenger of God until he died pleased with you; then you accompanied Abu Bakr until he died pleased with you. You were given authority, and no two people disputed your leadership.” Umar asked, “Do you bear witness to that?” Ibn Abbas hesitated. Ali said: “Yes, we bear witness to that on his behalf.”

records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham,
records.matn_en: that Ibn Abbas entered upon Umar when he was wounded and said: “Rejoice! By God, your Islam brought honor, your migration brought victory, and your rule was just. You accompanied the Messenger of God until he died pleased with you; then you accompanied Abu Bakr until he died pleased with you. You were given authority, and no two people disputed your leadership.” Umar asked, “Do you bear witness to that?” Ibn Abbas hesitated. Ali said: “Yes, we bear witness to that on his behalf.”
records.boundary_review_note: Al-Haytham introduces the account; the exchange between Ibn Abbas, Umar, and Ali is in the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah, who said It reached me that a man insulted Abu Bakr, ؓ, while the Prophet, ﷺ, was sitting, and Abu Bakr remained patient. Then Abu Bakr responded to him, so the Prophet, ﷺ, stood up. Abu Bakr said: He insulted me and you did not stand, but you stood when I responded to him. The Prophet, ﷺ, said: An angel was responding on your behalf, but when you responded yourself, the angel left, so I stood.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ali ibn al-Aqmar that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, passed by a man who was eating with his left hand while Umar was overseeing the people as they ate. Umar said to him, "Eat with your right hand, O servant of God." The man replied, "It is occupied." Umar passed by him a second time and said the same, then a third time and said the same. The man said, "What is it occupied with?" He replied, "It was cut off on the day of Mu'tah." Umar was startled by this and said, "Who washes your clothes? Who oils your head? Who takes care of you?" The man listed similar tasks. Then Umar ordered that a servant girl, a mount, food, and provisions be given to him. The people then said, "May God reward Umar well on behalf of his subjects."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported to me from his father from Abu Hanifah who said It reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, used to come to the mosque of Quba every Saturday, bring a palm branch, and sweep it himself.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Ali, ؓ, that Ali, ؓ, said to Abu Musa, ؓ, when he appointed him as arbitrator: “Relieve me of this [burden], even if it costs me my life. Whoever contends with them will have to use the vilest means. I wish I had a thousand horsemen from Banu Firas ibn Ghanm in their place. Their unity in falsehood is stronger than your unity in the truth.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِأَبِي مُوسَى رضي الله عنه حِينَ حَكَّمَهُ: «خَلِّصْنِي مِنْهَا وَلَوْ بِعِرْقِ رَقَبَتِي؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَنْ يَصُولَ بِهِمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا صَالَ بِالسَّهْمِ الْأَخْبَثِ، وَلَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّ مَعِي مَكَانَهُمْ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ مِنْ بَنِي فِرَاسِ بْنِ غَنْمٍ، وَلَاجْتِمَاعُ هَؤُلَاءِ عَلَى بَاطِلِهِمْ أَشَدُّ مِنَ اجْتِمَاعِكُمْ عَلَى حَقِّكُمْ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Ali, ؓ, that he said to Abu Musa, ؓ, when he appointed him as an arbitrator: "Save me from this, even if it costs me the vein of my neck. No one will prevail with them except by the most wicked arrow. I wish I had a thousand horsemen from Banu Firas ibn Ghanm instead of them. Their unity in falsehood is stronger than your unity in the truth."
