records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he preached in Kufa when Uthman, ؓ, was appointed caliph, and said: “In choosing him, we did not fail to select the best among us—the foremost of the candidates.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ خَطَبَ بِالْكُوفَةِ حِينَ اسْتُخْلِفَ عُثْمَانُ رضي الله عنه ⦗ص: 209⦘ ، وَقَالَ «مَا أَلَوْنَا عَنْ أَعْلَاهَا ذِي فَوْقٍ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ خَطَبَ بِالْكُوفَةِ حِينَ اسْتُخْلِفَ عُثْمَانُ رضي الله عنه ⦗ص: 209⦘ ، وَقَالَ «مَا أَلَوْنَا عَنْ أَعْلَاهَا ذِي فَوْقٍ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he delivered a sermon in Kufah when Uthman, ؓ, was appointed as caliph. He said "We have not deviated from its highest part, the one above."

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he preached in Kufa when Uthman, ؓ, was appointed caliph, and said: “In choosing him, we did not fail to select the best among us—the foremost of the candidates.”

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ خَطَبَ بِالْكُوفَةِ حِينَ اسْتُخْلِفَ عُثْمَانُ رضي الله عنه ، وَقَالَ «مَا أَلَوْنَا عَنْ أَعْلَاهَا ذِي فَوْقٍ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abdul-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ,

records.boundary_review_note: The report describes Ibn Masud’s sermon in Kufa.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, that Abdullah arrived in Kufa when Uthman, ؓ, had been chosen caliph, and said: “In choosing him, we did not fail to select the best among us—the foremost of the candidates.” Abu Hanifah said: “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘There is no one in Iraq like al-Hasan al-Basri.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ بَيَانِ بْنِ بِشْرٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، قَالَ قَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ رضي الله عنه الْكُوفَةَ حِينَ اسْتَخْلَفُوا عُثْمَانَ رضي الله عنه، فَقَالَ: «مَا أَلَوْنَا عَنْ أَعْلَاهَا ذِي فَوْقٍ» وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ يَقُولُ: مَا بِالْعِرَاقِ مِثْلُ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said Abdullah arrived in Kufa when they had pledged allegiance to Uthman, and he said, "We have not deviated from its highest peak." Abu Hanifah said: I heard Abu Ja'far say, "There is no one in Iraq like Al-Hasan Al-Basri."

records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, that Abdullah arrived in Kufa when Uthman, ؓ, had been chosen caliph, and said: “In choosing him, we did not fail to select the best among us—the foremost of the candidates.” Abu Hanifah said: “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘There is no one in Iraq like al-Hasan al-Basri.’”

records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Bayan ibn Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim,
records.matn_en: that Abdullah arrived in Kufa when Uthman, ؓ, had been chosen caliph, and said: “In choosing him, we did not fail to select the best among us—the foremost of the candidates.” Abu Hanifah said: “I heard Abu Jafar say, ‘There is no one in Iraq like al-Hasan al-Basri.’”
records.boundary_review_note: The report combines Qays’s account about Abdullah with a separate appended statement from Abu Hanifah quoting Abu Jaafar; the latter is retained in matn but is not part of the first chain.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Awn ibn Abdillah from Amir from Aisha, ؓ, who said: “I have seven qualities not shared by any of the Prophet’s other wives: The Prophet married me as a virgin, and none of his other wives was a virgin when he married her. Gabriel came to him in my image before he married me; he did not come in the image of any other wife. I saw Gabriel, and none of his other wives did. I was among the wives dearest to him, both in my own person and through my father. Gabriel would bring him revelation while I was beneath the same covering with him; he did not come to him while he was with any other wife. Verses of the Quran were revealed concerning me that nearly caused large groups of people to perish. He died on my day and night, between my chest and throat.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said "My illness was made easy for me when I saw Aisha with me in Paradise."

The world remained harsh and troubled until Muhammad died. When he died, the world’s bounty was poured out upon us.”

records.matn_ar: قَالَ بَلَغَنِي عَنِ «ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ كَانَ صَاحِبَ وَضُوءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَحَصِيرِهِ وَسِوَاكِهِ وَنَعْلَيْهِ وَعَصَاهُ، وَيَسْتُرُهُ إِذَا اغْتَسَلَ، وَيَمْشِي مَعَهُ فِي الْوَحْشَةِ، وَيُرَحِّلُ لَهُ إِذَا سَافَرَ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَشَدِّ النَّاسِ بِهِ شَبَهًا إِذْا دَخَلَ وَخَرَجَ، وَكَانَ يُرْسِلُ أُمَّ عَبْدٍ إِلَيْهِ فَتُخْبِرُهُ بِذَلِكَ وَشَمَائِلِهِ فَيُشَبَّهُ بِهِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, who said
records.matn_en: It reached me from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, that he was the keeper of the Messenger of God’s, ﷺ, ablution water, his mat, his tooth-stick, his sandals, and his staff. He would screen him when he bathed, walk with him in desolate places, and prepare his mount when he traveled. He was one of the people who most resembled him in his entry and exit. Umm ‘Abd would be sent to him to inform him of that and his characteristics, so he would be likened to him.
records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hanifah gives a balagh from Ibn Masud with no intermediary specified.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he accompanied a Christian on a journey. The Christian went away, so Abdullah said to him: "Peace be upon you." It was said to him: "Why did you do that?" He said: "For the right of companionship."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ صَحِبَ نَصْرَانِيًّا فِي طَرِيقٍ، فَذَهَبَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: «عَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ» ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ: لِمَ فَعَلْتَ؟ قَالَ: «لِحَقِّ الصُّحْبَةِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated to me from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Hind from one of their elders that ‘Amir used to narrate in a gathering where Ibn ‘Umar, ؓ, was present about the military campaigns of the Prophet, ﷺ. Ibn ‘Umar said , "He narrates as if he had witnessed the people himself."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from someone who narrated to him, from ‘Amir, that he said Six individuals from the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, were jurists. Three of them would consult one another, and three others would consult one another. Ibn Mas‘ud, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Zayd ibn Thabit would consult one another, while ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari, and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b would consult one another.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Al-Haytham, that a man from the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, devoted himself to worship. When the Prophet, ﷺ, passed away, a man came to him asking a question. He said , "I do not know," or "I have no knowledge of this." The man said, "If the companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, had taken what you have taken, knowledge would have been lost."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, that when Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, arrived in Syria, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, ؓ, went out to meet him. When they met, each embraced the other.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, visited the Prophet, ﷺ, during an illness. He found him on a Qatwani cloak, with a wool cushion stuffed with idhkhir grass beneath his head. Umar said: “May my father be sacrificed for you, Messenger of God! Chosroes and Caesar recline on brocade, while you lie on this.” The Prophet said: “Umar, are you not content that they have this world and we have the Hereafter?” Umar touched him and found that he had a severe fever. Umar said: “You suffer such fever while you are God’s Messenger?” The Prophet replied: “The most severely tested of this community are its prophets, then the best, then the next best. The prophets before you and their communities were likewise tested.”

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, visited the Prophet, ﷺ, while he was ill. He found him lying on a coarse cloak made of Qatwani fabric and a leather pillow stuffed with Idhkhir grass. Umar said , "May my father be ransomed for you, O Messenger of God! Chosroes and Caesar recline on silk brocade, while you lie on this?" The Prophet replied, "O Umar, are you not satisfied that they have this world while we have the Hereafter?" Then Umar touched him and found him with a severe fever. He said, "You suffer such fever while you are the Messenger of God?" The Prophet said, "The most severely tested among this nation are its prophets, then the best, then the next best. This was the case with the prophets before you and their nations."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah ibn Qays, who said "At the gates of the ruler are the resting places of camels of tribulations. Whoever exposes himself to them will be exposed to them. You will never attain anything from their worldly life except that they will take from your religion something better than it."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah who said It reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: "Were it not that I humble my face for God, or that a breath praising God leaves me, or that I sit with people who carefully choose their words as we choose the best dates, I would not care if I died."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ: «لَوْلَا أَنْ أَضَعَ وَجْهِي لِلَّهِ، أَوْ يَخْرُجَ مِنِّي نَسَمَةٌ تُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ، أَوْ أَجْلِسَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ يَتَخَيَّرُونَ الْكَلَامَ كَمَا نَتَخَيَّرُ جَيِّدَ التَّمْرِ مَا بَالَيْتُ لَوْ مُتُّ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه، قَالَ: «لَوْلَا أَنْ أَضَعَ وَجْهِي لِلَّهِ، أَوْ يَخْرُجَ مِنِّي نَسَمَةٌ تُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ، أَوْ أَجْلِسَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ يَتَخَيَّرُونَ الْكَلَامَ كَمَا نَتَخَيَّرُ جَيِّدَ التَّمْرِ مَا بَالَيْتُ لَوْ مُتُّ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, that he said “That a devil should live next to me in my house and not harm me is more beloved to me than that a woman should live next to me.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَأَنْ يُجَاوِرَنِي فِي دَارِيَ شَيْطَانٌ لَا يَضُرُّنِي أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ ⦗ص: 214⦘ تُجَاوِرَنِيَ امْرَأَةٌ»

records.text_en: Then he reported to him from al-Hasan, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: “When God intends good for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their most forbearing and allocates their public revenues to their most generous. When God intends evil for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their worst and their revenues in the hands of their most miserly.”
records.text_ar: ثُمَّ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ خَيْرًا وَلَّى أَمَرَهُمْ حُلَمَاءَهُمْ، وَجَعَلْ فَيْئَهُمْ عِنْدَ سُمَحَائِهِمْ، وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ شَرًّا وَلَّى أَمْرَهُمْ شِرَارَهُمْ، وَجَعَلَ فَيْئَهُمْ عِنْدَ بُخَلَائِهِمْ»
records.raw_text_ar: ثُمَّ حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ خَيْرًا وَلَّى أَمَرَهُمْ حُلَمَاءَهُمْ، وَجَعَلْ فَيْئَهُمْ عِنْدَ سُمَحَائِهِمْ، وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ شَرًّا وَلَّى أَمْرَهُمْ شِرَارَهُمْ، وَجَعَلَ فَيْئَهُمْ عِنْدَ بُخَلَائِهِمْ»
records.raw_text_en: Then he reported to him from al-Hasan, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said When God intends good for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their most forbearing, and He puts their wealth in the possession of their most generous. When God intends evil for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their worst, and He puts their wealth in the possession of their most miserly.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from al-Hasan, who said: “The young people among my neighbors—if I answer them, they do not understand; and if they are left to themselves, they are left to serious error. Were it not for the duty God has laid upon scholars, I would answer only a few.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ «أُغَيْلِمَةُ جَارِي إِنْ أُجِيبُوا لَمْ يَفْهَمُوا، وَإِنْ وُكِّلُوا وُكِّلُوا إِلَى غَيٍّ شَدِيدٍ، لَوْلَا مَا أَخَذَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْعُلَمَاءِ مَا أَجَبْتُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ «أُغَيْلِمَةُ جَارِي إِنْ أُجِيبُوا لَمْ يَفْهَمُوا، وَإِنْ وُكِّلُوا وُكِّلُوا إِلَى غَيٍّ شَدِيدٍ، لَوْلَا مَا أَخَذَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْعُلَمَاءِ مَا أَجَبْتُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, from al-Hasan, who said "These young lads—if they are answered, they do not understand, and if they are left to themselves, they are left to severe misguidance. Were it not for what God has taken upon the scholars, I would hardly ever respond."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ «أُغَيْلِمَةُ جَارِي إِنْ أُجِيبُوا لَمْ يَفْهَمُوا، وَإِنْ وُكِّلُوا وُكِّلُوا إِلَى غَيٍّ شَدِيدٍ، لَوْلَا مَا أَخَذَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْعُلَمَاءِ مَا أَجَبْتُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»

records.text_en: Abu Hanifah said It has reached me that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: "The best of your youth are those who emulate your elders, and the worst of your elders are those who emulate your youth. The worst of your men are those who emulate your women, and the worst of your women are those who emulate your men."
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «خَيْرُ شَبَابِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشُيُوخِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ شُيُوخِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشَبَابِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ رِجَالِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِنِسَائِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ نِسَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِرِجَالِكُمْ»
records.raw_text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «خَيْرُ شَبَابِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشُيُوخِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ شُيُوخِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشَبَابِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ رِجَالِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِنِسَائِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ نِسَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِرِجَالِكُمْ»

records.isnad_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ:
records.matn_ar: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «خَيْرُ شَبَابِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشُيُوخِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ شُيُوخِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِشَبَابِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ رِجَالِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِنِسَائِكُمْ، وَشَرُّ نِسَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَتَشَبَّهُونَ بِرِجَالِكُمْ»
records.isnad_en: Abu Hanifah said
records.matn_en: It has reached me that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: "The best of your youth are those who emulate your elders, and the worst of your elders are those who emulate your youth. The worst of your men are those who emulate your women, and the worst of your women are those who emulate your men."
records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hanifah gives a balagh; no intermediary to the Prophet is specified.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that Abu Bakr, ؓ, noticed the Prophet, ﷺ, was in a lightened state. He sought his permission to visit the daughter of Kharijah, who was in the orchards of the Ansar. This was the rest before death, though he was unaware. The Prophet permitted him, then passed away that very night. Abu Bakr awoke the next morning to find people in commotion. He ordered a servant to listen and report back. The servant said, "I heard them saying, 'Muhammad, ﷺ, has died.'" Abu Bakr leaned against a wall, exclaiming, "May my back be severed!" When he reached the mosque, they thought he would not make it. The hypocrites began spreading doubt, saying, "If Muhammad were a prophet, he would not have died." Umar said , "I will strike with my sword anyone who says Muhammad has died." They fell silent. When Abu Bakr arrived and the Prophet, ﷺ, was laid out, he uncovered his face, kissed him, and said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. God would not make you taste death twice. You are too noble for that in God’s sight." Then Abu Bakr went out and said, "O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped the Lord of Muhammad, the Lord of Muhammad lives and does not die." Then he recited, *"Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful."* Umar said, "By God, it was as if we had never read this verse before." The people echoed Abu Bakr’s words and recitation. The Prophet died on Monday night, remained that night and the following day and Tuesday night, and was buried on Tuesday. Usamah ibn Zayd andAws ibn Khawli al-Ansari, ؓ, poured the water, while Ali and al-Fadl, ؓ, washed him. Abu Hanifah said, "It reached me that they prayed over him in groups without an imam."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه، " أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه، رَأَى مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خِفَّةً، فَاسْتَأْذَنَهُ إِلَى ابْنَةِ خَارِجَةَ، وَكَانَتْ فِي حَوَائِطِ الْأَنْصَارِ، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ رَاحَةَ الْمَوْتِ وَلَا يَشْعُرُ، فَأَذِنَ لَهُ، ثُمَّ تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، فَأَصْبَحَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه فَجَعَلَ يَرَى النَّاسَ يَتَرَامَسُونَ فَأَمَرَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ غُلَامًا يَتَسَمَّعُ ثُمَّ يُخْبِرُهُ، فَقَالَ: سَمِعْتُهُمْ يَقُولُونَ: مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَأَسْنَدَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ظَهْرَهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: وَاقْطَعَ ظَهْرَاهُ، قَالَ فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْمَسْجِدَ حَتَّى ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ لَا يَبْلُغُ، قَالَ: فَأَرْجَفَ الْمُنَافِقُونَ، فَقَالُوا: لَوْ كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيًّا لَمْ يَمُتْ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: لَا أَسْمَعُ أَحَدًا يَقُولُ: مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ، إِلَّا ضَرَبْتُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ، فَكَفُّوا لِذَلِكَ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه وَالنَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُسَجًّى كَشَفَ الثَّوْبَ وَجَعَلَ يَلْثِمُهُ، وَيَقُولُ ⦗ص: 215⦘ : بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي، مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُذِيقَكَ الْمَوْتَ مَرَّتَيْنِ، أَنْتَ أَكْرَمُ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ مَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ مُحَمَّدًا فَقَدْ مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَمَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ رَبَّ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِنَّ رَبَّ مُحَمَّدٍ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ، أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ وَمَنْ يَنْقَلِبْ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَنْ يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْئًا وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّاكِرِينَ} [آل عمران: 144] قَالَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه: وَاللَّهِ لَكَأَنَّا لَمْ نَقْرَأْهَا قَبْلَهَا قَطُّ، فَقَالَ النَّاسُ مِثْلَ مَقَالَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ وَقِرَاءَتِهِ، قَالَ: وَمَاتَ لَيْلَةَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ فَمَكَثَ لَيْلَتَئِذٍ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَيْلَةَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ وَدُفِنَ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ وَأَوْسُ بْنُ خَوْلِيٍّ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ رضي الله عنهم يَصُبَّانِ الْمَاءَ، وَعَلِيٌّ وَالْفَضْلُ رضي الله عنهما يُغَسِّلَانِهِ " وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا عَلَيْهِ أَفْوَاجًا بِغَيْرِ إِمَامٍ

عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه: وَاللَّهِ لَكَأَنَّا لَمْ نَقْرَأْهَا قَبْلَهَا قَطُّ، فَقَالَ النَّاسُ مِثْلَ مَقَالَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ وَقِرَاءَتِهِ، قَالَ: وَمَاتَ لَيْلَةَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ فَمَكَثَ لَيْلَتَئِذٍ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَيْلَةَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ وَدُفِنَ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ وَأَوْسُ بْنُ خَوْلِيٍّ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ رضي الله عنهم يَصُبَّانِ الْمَاءَ، وَعَلِيٌّ وَالْفَضْلُ رضي الله عنهما يُغَسِّلَانِهِ " وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا عَلَيْهِ أَفْوَاجًا بِغَيْرِ إِمَامٍ
records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that Abu Bakr, ؓ, noticed the Prophet, ﷺ, was in a lightened state. He sought his permission to visit the daughter of Kharijah, who was in the orchards of the Ansar. This was the rest before death, though he was unaware. The Prophet permitted him, then passed away that very night. Abu Bakr awoke the next morning to find people in commotion. He ordered a servant to listen and report back. The servant said, "I heard them saying, 'Muhammad, ﷺ, has died.'" Abu Bakr leaned against a wall, exclaiming, "May my back be severed!" When he reached the mosque, they thought he would not make it. The hypocrites began spreading doubt, saying, "If Muhammad were a prophet, he would not have died." Umar said , "I will strike with my sword anyone who says Muhammad has died." They fell silent. When Abu Bakr arrived and the Prophet, ﷺ, was laid out, he uncovered his face, kissed him, and said, "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. God would not make you taste death twice. You are too noble for that in God’s sight." Then Abu Bakr went out and said, "O people, whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped the Lord of Muhammad, the Lord of Muhammad lives and does not die." Then he recited, *"Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful."* Umar said, "By God, it was as if we had never read this verse before." The people echoed Abu Bakr’s words and recitation. The Prophet died on Monday night, remained that night and the following day and Tuesday night, and was buried on Tuesday. Usamah ibn Zayd andAws ibn Khawli al-Ansari, ؓ, poured the water, while Ali and al-Fadl, ؓ, washed him. Abu Hanifah said, "It reached me that they prayed over him in groups without an imam."
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضي الله عنه، "
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه، رَأَى مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خِفَّةً، فَاسْتَأْذَنَهُ إِلَى ابْنَةِ خَارِجَةَ، وَكَانَتْ فِي حَوَائِطِ الْأَنْصَارِ، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ رَاحَةَ الْمَوْتِ وَلَا يَشْعُرُ، فَأَذِنَ لَهُ، ثُمَّ تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، فَأَصْبَحَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه فَجَعَلَ يَرَى النَّاسَ يَتَرَامَسُونَ فَأَمَرَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ غُلَامًا يَتَسَمَّعُ ثُمَّ يُخْبِرُهُ، فَقَالَ: سَمِعْتُهُمْ يَقُولُونَ: مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَأَسْنَدَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ظَهْرَهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: وَاقْطَعَ ظَهْرَاهُ، قَالَ فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْمَسْجِدَ حَتَّى ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ لَا يَبْلُغُ، قَالَ: فَأَرْجَفَ الْمُنَافِقُونَ، فَقَالُوا: لَوْ كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيًّا لَمْ يَمُتْ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: لَا أَسْمَعُ أَحَدًا يَقُولُ: مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ، إِلَّا ضَرَبْتُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ، فَكَفُّوا لِذَلِكَ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ رضي الله عنه وَالنَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُسَجًّى كَشَفَ الثَّوْبَ وَجَعَلَ يَلْثِمُهُ، وَيَقُولُ : بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي، مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُذِيقَكَ الْمَوْتَ مَرَّتَيْنِ، أَنْتَ أَكْرَمُ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ مَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ مُحَمَّدًا فَقَدْ مَاتَ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَمَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ رَبَّ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِنَّ رَبَّ مُحَمَّدٍ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ، أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ وَمَنْ يَنْقَلِبْ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَنْ يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْئًا وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّاكِرِينَ} [آل عمران: 144] قَالَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه: وَاللَّهِ لَكَأَنَّا لَمْ نَقْرَأْهَا قَبْلَهَا قَطُّ، فَقَالَ النَّاسُ مِثْلَ مَقَالَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ وَقِرَاءَتِهِ، قَالَ: وَمَاتَ لَيْلَةَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ فَمَكَثَ لَيْلَتَئِذٍ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَيْلَةَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ وَدُفِنَ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ، قَالَ: وَكَانَ أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ وَأَوْسُ بْنُ خَوْلِيٍّ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ رضي الله عنهم يَصُبَّانِ الْمَاءَ، وَعَلِيٌّ وَالْفَضْلُ رضي الله عنهما يُغَسِّلَانِهِ " وَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا عَلَيْهِ أَفْوَاجًا بِغَيْرِ إِمَامٍ

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he said to Umar, ؓ, while he was shrouded: "There is no one whose record I would rather meet God Almighty with than this shrouded one."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Hind, from ‘Amir, that he was sitting by a pillar when a man behind him was backbiting him. ‘Amir turned to him and said May it be wholesome and easy to digest, not a lingering sickness… For the honor of our reputations, what has she made lawful?
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هِنْدَ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّهُ " كَانَ جَالِسًا إِلَى أُسْطُوَانَةٍ وَرَجُلٌ خَلْفَهُ يَقَعُ فِيهِ، فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهِ عَامِرٌ فَقَالَ [البحر الطويل] هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا غَيْرَ دَاءٍ مُخَامِرٍ … لِعَزَّةَ مِنْ أَعْرَاضِنَا مَا اسْتَحَلَّتِ "

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abd al-Karim, who attributed this report to the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: “Whoever plays chess is like one who performs ablution with the flesh of swine.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، يَرْفَعُ الْحَدِيثَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَنْ لَعِبَ بِالشِّطْرَنْجِ فَهُوَ كَالَّذِي يَتَوَضَّأُ بِلَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from someone who reported to him from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: “Beware of these two gaming knucklebones [dice], which are thrown forcefully.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Musa ibn Abi Kathir and Al-Haytham that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, passed by Uthman, ؓ, who was grieving shortly after the Prophet’s daughter married to him had died. Umar asked, “What grieves you?” Uthman said, “Should I not grieve, when the marriage tie between me and the Messenger of God has been severed?” Umar asked, “Would you like me to marry you to Hafsah?” Uthman said yes. Umar said, “Let me mention it to the Messenger of God.” Umar told him what had happened, and the Prophet said: “Shall I guide you to a marriage tie better for you than the one with Uthman, and guide Uthman to one better for him than the one with you?” Umar said, “Yes.” The Prophet said: “You marry me to Hafsah, and I will marry Uthman to my daughter.” The Messenger of God then did so.

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Musa ibn Abi Kathir and Al-Haytham that Umar ibn Al-Khattab passed by Uthman when the latter was grieving shortly after the death of the daughter of the Messenger of God, who was under his care. Umar said , "What grieves you?" Uthman replied, "Should I not grieve when the bond of marriage between me and the Messenger of God has been severed?" Umar said, "Would you like me to marry you to Hafsah?" Uthman said, "Yes." Umar said, "Let me mention this to the Messenger of God." Umar then mentioned the story to the Messenger of God, who said to Umar, "Shall I not guide you to a son-in-law better for you than Uthman, and guide Uthman to a son-in-law better for him than you?" Umar said, "Yes." The Prophet said, "You marry me to Hafsah, and I will marry Uthman to my daughter." The Messenger of God then did so.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Ali ibn al-Aqmar from al-Agharr from Ali, ؓ, from the Prophet, ﷺ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, passed by a group remembering God and said: “You are the people with whom I have been commanded to remain patiently. Whenever a group of people sit remembering God, the angels surround them with their wings, mercy envelops them, and God mentions them among those who are with Him.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that he said When you see the gardens of Paradise, graze therein. Indeed, they are not the gatherings of storytellers, but rather the gatherings of the people of jurisprudence.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah who said that it had reached him that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: “If I had appointed Uthman, he would have placed the family of Abu Muayt on the people’s shoulders. By God, if I had done so, he would have done it; and if he did, they would soon march against him and cut off his head.” They asked, “What about Ali?” Umar said, “He is a weak, unimpressive man.” They asked, “Talhah?” He said, “That man is conceited.” They asked, “Al-Zubayr?” He said, “He is not suited to it.” They asked, “Saʿd?” He said, “He is a horseman and archer.” They asked, “Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf?” He said, “He is very tight-fisted. This office suits only someone who gives without extravagance and withholds without being miserly.”

By God, if I did so, he would do it, and if he did, they would soon march against him until they cut off his head." They said, "Ali?" He replied, "A man of great stature." They said, "Talha?" records.text_en: Yusuf ibn Abi Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding killing that it occurs in three forms: Intentional killing is when you deliberately strike someone with a weapon, and in this case, retaliation (qisas) is required. Unintentional killing is when you intend to strike something but strike someone else with a weapon, and in this case, the blood money (diyah) is upon the clan (aqilah). Semi-intentional killing is when you deliberately strike someone without a weapon, and in this case, the blood money is increased and is upon the clan if it results in death. In cases of wounds, semi-intentional applies to anything where you deliberately strike someone with or without a weapon, but retaliation is not possible, so the blood money is increased.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “A slave’s blood-wit does not reach the amount of a free person’s, because you will never find a slave for whom there is not someone among the free who is better than him.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا يَبْلُغُ بِالْعَبْدِ دِيَةُ الْحُرِّ، وَذَلِكَ لَا تَجِدُ عَبْدًا أَبَدًا إِلَّا وَفِي الْأَحْرَارِ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The blood money of a free person does not apply to a slave, for you will never find a slave without there being among the free people someone better than him.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that a man shaved another man’s beard and it did not grow back, so he ruled that the full blood money (diyah) be paid for it.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, who said: “For quasi-intentional homicide, [the compensation is] thirty-three ḥiqqah camels (females entering their fourth year), thirty-three jadhaʿah camels (females entering their fifth year), and thirty-four thaniyyah camels (females entering their sixth year) through the bāzil stage; all are pregnant.”
records.text_ar: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الْخَطَإِ مِثْلَ قَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه، وَقَالَ " فِي شِبْهِ الْعَمْدِ: ثَلَاثَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ حِقَّةً، وَثَلَاثَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ جَذَعَةً، وَأَرْبَعَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ ثَنِيَّةً إِلَى بَازِلِ عَامِهَا كُلُّهَا خَلِفَةٌ "

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he said regarding unintentional killing the same as Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, said. And he said regarding semi-intentional killing: "Thirty-three mature she-camels, thirty-three fully-grown she-camels, and thirty-four she-camels that have reached the age of shedding their front teeth, all of them in their next pregnancy."

records.matn_en: who said: “For quasi-intentional homicide, [the compensation is] thirty-three ḥiqqah camels (females entering their fourth year), thirty-three jadhaʿah camels (females entering their fifth year), and thirty-four thaniyyah camels (females entering their sixth year) through the bāzil stage; all are pregnant.”
records.boundary_review_note: Ali’s statement contains a comparison with Ibn Masud’s opinion and then a separate ruling; both belong to the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas‘ud, ؓ, who said regarding the blood-wit for accidental homicide, divided into five groups: twenty jadhaʿah camels (females entering their fifth year), twenty ḥiqqah camels (females entering their fourth year), twenty bint labun camels (females entering their third year), twenty bint makhad camels (females entering their second year), and twenty ibn makhad camels (males entering their second year).
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ ⦗ص: 219⦘ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي " دِيَةِ الْخَطَإِ أَخْمَاسًا: عِشْرِينَ جَذَعَةً، وَعِشْرِينَ حِقَّةً، وَعِشْرِينَ بَنَاتِ لَبُونٍ، وَعِشْرِينَ بَنَاتِ مَخَاضٍ، وَعِشْرِينَ بَنِي مَخَاضٍ "

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Shurayh said regarding the fingers: "The fingers of the hand and the foot are equal; for each finger, a tenth."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ شُرَيْحًا، قَالَ فِي الْأَصَابِعِ: «أَصَابِعُ الْيَدِ وَالرِّجْلِ سَوَاءٌ فِي كُلِّ أُصْبُعٍ الْعُشْرُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim, who said regarding blood money: For a tooth, half of a tenth. Likewise for a wound exposing the bone. For a displaced bone, a tenth and a half of a tenth. For a penetrating wound, a third of the blood money. For a wound reaching the skull, a third of the blood money. If the intellect is lost, the full blood money is due. For the nose, the full blood money. For the nasal septum, the full blood money. For the penis, the full blood money. For the glans, the full blood money. For the testicles, the full blood money. For the tongue, the full blood money. For both eyes, the full blood money, and for one eye, half. Likewise for both hands and both feet, half the blood money for each. For both ears, the full blood money, and for one ear, half. For both eyebrows, the full blood money.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «السِّنِّ نِصْفُ الْعُشْرِ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْمُوضِحَةِ، وَفِي الْمُنَقِّلَةِ الْعُشْرُ وَنِصْفُ الْعُشْرِ، وَفِي ⦗ص: 220⦘ الْجَائِفَةِ ثُلُثُ الدِّيَةِ، وَفِي الْآمَّةِ ثُلُثُ الدِّيَةِ، فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ الْعَقْلُ فَفِيهَا الدِّيَةُ كَامِلَةٌ، وَفِي الْأَنْفِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الْمَارِنِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الذَّكَرِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الْحَشَفَةِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي اللِّسَانِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الْعَيْنَيْنِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي الْوَاحِدَةِ النِّصْفُ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْيَدَيْنِ وَالرِّجْلَيْنِ فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ، وَفِي الْأُذُنَيْنِ الدِّيَةُ، وَفِي إِحْدَاهُمَا النِّصْفُ، وَفِي الْحَاجِبَيْنِ الدِّيَةُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said regarding a man who cut off another man’s hand and then the victim took retaliation by cutting off the offender’s hand, but the offender died: the blood money for him is upon the clan of the one who took retaliation.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «رَجُلٍ قَطَعَ يَدَ رَجُلٍ فَاقْتَصَّ مِنْهُ فَمَاتَ الْمُقْتَصُّ مِنْهُ، أَنَّ دِيَتَهُ عَلَى عَاقِلَةِ الْمُقْتَصِّ لَهُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "The testimony of a slave under contract of manumission is not valid."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding a slave killed accidentally: “[The blood-wit] is borne by the offender’s ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group); any injury short of death is paid from the offender’s own property.”
records.text_ar: : قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «الْعَبْدِ يُقْتَلُ خَطَأً عَلَى الْعَاقِلَةِ وَمَا كَانَ دُونَ النَّفْسِ فَهُوَ فِي مَالِ الْجَانِي»
records.raw_text_ar: : قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي «الْعَبْدِ يُقْتَلُ خَطَأً عَلَى الْعَاقِلَةِ وَمَا كَانَ دُونَ النَّفْسِ فَهُوَ فِي مَالِ الْجَانِي»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding "the slave killed by mistake: it is upon the *‘aqilah*, and whatever is less than a life is upon the property of the perpetrator."

records.text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir who said: “The ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) does not bear compensation for a slave, intentional killing, a settlement, or an admission.”
records.text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ عَبْدًا وَلَا عَمْدًا وَلَا صُلْحًا وَلَا اعْتِرَافًا»
records.raw_text_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ، قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ عَبْدًا وَلَا عَمْدًا وَلَا صُلْحًا وَلَا اعْتِرَافًا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir who said The blood-money group does not pay for a slave, nor for intentional killing, nor for a settlement, nor for a confession.

records.isnad_ar: يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، عَنْ عَامِرٍ،

records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim’s statement on the liability of the blood-money group.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “The ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) does not bear compensation when a slave is killed accidentally.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ الْعَبْدَ إِذَا قُتِلَ خَطَأً»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ الْعَبْدَ إِذَا قُتِلَ خَطَأً»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The blood-money group does not pay for a slave if he is killed by mistake.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said: “The ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) bears liability only when the amount is five hundred dirhams or more.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فَصَاعِدًا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَا تَعْقِلُ الْعَاقِلَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فَصَاعِدًا»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said The blood-money paying group does not pay except for five hundred dirhams and above.

records.matn_en: who said: “The ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) bears liability only when the amount is five hundred dirhams or more.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah, from someone who reported to him, from 'Amir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, “He fixed the blood-wit at ten thousand dirhams for those who pay in silver, one thousand dinars for those who pay in gold, one hundred camels for those who pay in camels, two hundred head of cattle, two hundred suits of garments, or two thousand sheep; all of these rates applied to those enrolled in the dīwān (the state register).”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that a slain person was found in Yemen between Wadaʿah and Khaywan. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, wrote: “Measure the distance between them. The people of whichever village he was nearer to shall provide fifty men to swear: ‘We did not kill him, and we know no killer.’ They must then pay the blood-wit.”
records.text_ar: : قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ قَتِيلًا ⦗ص: 222⦘ وُجِدَ بِالْيَمَنِ بَيْنَ وَدَاعَةَ وَخَيْوَانَ، فَكَتَبَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه أَنْ «قِيسُوهُ، فَإِلَى أَيِّ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ كَانَ أَقْرَبَ أَقْسَمَ مِنْهُمْ خَمْسُونَ رَجُلًا مَا قَتَلْنَا، وَلَا عَلِمْنَا قَاتِلًا، ثُمَّ يَضْمَنُونَ الدِّيَةَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who ruled concerning a blind man who destroys the sound eye of a sighted person: “If he does so intentionally, he owes the blood-wit from his own property; if unintentionally, the ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) bears it.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “The full blood-wit is payable over three years; half is payable over two years, and one third—or any amount less than one third—over one year.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said concerning a man who emancipates half of his slave: “The slave must work to pay for the remaining half. If he commits an unintentional homicide, the ʿāqilah (agnatic kin group liable for accidental blood-wit) bears half the blood-wit on his behalf, and the slave must work to pay half his value.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “For any bodily part of a slave of which there are two, injury to both entails his full value, and injury to one entails half his value. For any bodily part of which there is only one, injury to it entails his full value. Compensation for his wounds is assessed in proportion to the compensation for a free person’s wounds relative to that person’s blood-wit.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ فِيهِ مِنْهُ اثْنَانِ، فَفِيهِمَا قِيمَتُهُ، وَفِي أَحَدِهِمَا نِصْفُ قِيمَتِهِ، وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فِيهِ مِنْهُ وَاحِدٌ، فَفِيهِ قِيمَتُهُ، وَجِرَاحَتُهُ مِنْ قِيمَتِهِ عَلَى قَدْرِ جِرَاحَةِ الْحُرِّ مِنْ دِيَتِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ فِيهِ مِنْهُ اثْنَانِ، فَفِيهِمَا قِيمَتُهُ، وَفِي أَحَدِهِمَا نِصْفُ قِيمَتِهِ، وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فِيهِ مِنْهُ وَاحِدٌ، فَفِيهِ قِيمَتُهُ، وَجِرَاحَتُهُ مِنْ قِيمَتِهِ عَلَى قَدْرِ جِرَاحَةِ الْحُرِّ مِنْ دِيَتِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said Everything of the slave in which there are two of it, its value is in both, and in one of them is half its value. And everything in which there is one of it, its value is in it, and his wounds are valued according to the proportion of a free person’s wounds from his blood money.
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ فِيهِ مِنْهُ اثْنَانِ، فَفِيهِمَا قِيمَتُهُ، وَفِي أَحَدِهِمَا نِصْفُ قِيمَتِهِ، وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فِيهِ مِنْهُ وَاحِدٌ، فَفِيهِ قِيمَتُهُ، وَجِرَاحَتُهُ مِنْ قِيمَتِهِ عَلَى قَدْرِ جِرَاحَةِ الْحُرِّ مِنْ دِيَتِهِ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “For any bodily part of a slave of which there are two, injury to both entails his full value, and injury to one entails half his value. For any bodily part of which there is only one, injury to it entails his full value. Compensation for his wounds is assessed in proportion to the compensation for a free person’s wounds relative to that person’s blood-wit.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “When an enslaved person commits an offense, his master must either surrender him or ransom him for the full amount of the offense.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim. Hammad said: “I visited Ibrahim while he was eating and ate with him. He called for nabīdh for me; when he saw me hesitate, he told me from ʿAlqamah that ʿAlqamah visited Ibn Masʿud while he was eating and ate with him. Then they were brought nabīdh that Sirin, Ibn Masʿud’s umm walad (enslaved woman who bore him a child), had fermented in a green earthenware jar. Ibn Masʿud and ʿAlqamah drank from it.”

records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ حَمَّادٌ: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَهُوَ يَأْكُلُ فَأَكَلْتُ مَعَهُ، فَدَعَا لِي بِنَبِيذٍ فَلَمَّا رَأَى إِبْطَائِي عَنْهُ، حَدَّثَنِي عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ أَنَّهُ «دَخَلَ عَلَى ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه وَهُوَ يَأْكُلُ، فَأَكَلَ مَعَهُ، ثُمَّ أُتُوا بِنَبِيذٍ تَنْبِذُهُ أُمُّ وَلَدِهِ سِيرِينَ فِي جَرٍّ أَخْضَرَ، فَشَرِبَ مِنْهُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ وَعَلْقَمَةُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said Hammad said: I entered upon Ibrahim while he was eating, so I ate with him. He called for a drink of nabidh for me, and when he saw my hesitation, he narrated to me from Alqamah that he entered upon Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, while he was eating, so he ate with him. Then they were brought nabidh prepared by his concubine Sirin in a green jar, and Ibn Mas'ud and Alqamah drank from it.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Muzahim ibn Zufar from al-Dahhak who said Abu Ubaydah showed me the green earthenware jar in which drink used to be prepared for Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

records.matn_ar: قَالَ «أَرَانِي أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ الْجَرَّ الْأَخْضَرَ الَّتِي كَانَ يُنْبَذُ فِيهَا لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that he used to stay with Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari in Wasit al-Qasab, and he would send someone to the market to buy him nabidh from the large jars.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Amir that he said There is no harm in nabidh prepared in a coated waterskin, both its inside and outside.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, ؓ, Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: “I had forbidden you three things: visiting graves—now visit them, for permission was granted to Muhammad to visit his mother’s grave, but do not say anything indecent; keeping sacrificial meat for more than three days—now keep it and take provisions, for I forbade it only so that your wealthy could make room for your poor; and drinking from gourds, pitch-coated vessels, and green jars. Now drink from any containers you wish, for containers make nothing lawful or unlawful. But do not drink anything intoxicating.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ رضي الله عنه، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ " كُنَّا نَهَيْنَاكُمْ عَنْ ثَلَاثٍ: عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، فَقَدْ أُذِنَ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ، وَلَا تَقُولُوا هُجْرًا، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ أَنْ تُمْسِكُوا لُحُومَ الْأَضَاحِي فَوْقَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ، فَأَمْسِكُوا وَتَزَوَّدُوا، فَإِنَّمَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ لِيَتَّسِعَ بِهِ غَنِيُّكُمْ عَلَى فَقِيرِكُمْ، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ أَنْ تَشْرَبُوا فِي الدُّبَّاءِ وَالْمُزَفَّتِ وَالْحَنْتَمِ، فَاشْرَبُوا فِيمَا بَدَا لَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّرُوفِ؛ فَإِنَّ الظُّرُوفَ لَا تُحِلُّ شَيْئًا وَلَا تُحَرِّمُهُ، وَلَا تَشْرَبُوا مُسْكِرًا "
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ رضي الله عنه، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ " كُنَّا نَهَيْنَاكُمْ عَنْ ثَلَاثٍ: عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، فَقَدْ أُذِنَ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ، وَلَا تَقُولُوا هُجْرًا، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ أَنْ تُمْسِكُوا لُحُومَ الْأَضَاحِي فَوْقَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ، فَأَمْسِكُوا وَتَزَوَّدُوا، فَإِنَّمَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ لِيَتَّسِعَ بِهِ غَنِيُّكُمْ عَلَى فَقِيرِكُمْ، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ أَنْ تَشْرَبُوا فِي الدُّبَّاءِ وَالْمُزَفَّتِ وَالْحَنْتَمِ، فَاشْرَبُوا فِيمَا بَدَا لَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّرُوفِ؛ فَإِنَّ الظُّرُوفَ لَا تُحِلُّ شَيْئًا وَلَا تُحَرِّمُهُ، وَلَا تَشْرَبُوا مُسْكِرًا "
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said We had forbidden you three things: visiting graves, but now visit them, for Muhammad, ﷺ, has been permitted to visit his mother’s grave. Do not say anything offensive. We had forbidden you from keeping the meat of sacrificial animals for more than three days, but now keep it and store it, for we only forbade you so that your wealthy could provide for your poor. We had forbidden you from drinking from gourds, varnished jars, and green jars, but now drink from whatever vessels you prefer, for vessels do not make anything lawful or unlawful. And do not drink anything intoxicating.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, caught a drunk man. He tried to find him an excuse, but the man insisted that he had lost his reason. ʿUmar said: “Detain him, and when he is sober, flog him.” He then took the remainder of his waterskin’s drink and tasted it. “Ugh! This has really affected men,” he said. He poured water into it to dilute it, then drank and gave his companions to drink. He said: “Do this to your drink when its devil overcomes you.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Abu Ishaq from Uqbah ibn Ziyad, who said Ibn Umar, ؓ, gave me a drink, and I could barely find my way home. The next day, I returned to him and mentioned that to him, so he said: "We only added to you a pressed date and raisins."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, wrote to ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, ؓ: “I was brought a drink from Syria that had been boiled over a fire until two-thirds evaporated and one-third remained. Its forbidden, intoxicating part and the madness-inducing effect were gone; its sweetness and lawful portion remained. It resembles ṭilāʾ (grape must boiled down). Tell those under your authority to use it freely in their drinks.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه كَتَبَ إِلَى عَمَّارِ بْنِ يَاسِرٍ رضي الله عنهما «إِنِّي أُتِيتُ بِشَرَابٍ مِنَ الشَّامِ قَدْ طُبِخَ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ ثُلُثَاهُ فِي النَّارِ، وَبَقِيَ ثُلُثُهُ، وَذَهَبَ حَرَامُهُ وَرِيحُ جُنُونِهِ، وَبَقِيَ حُلْوُهُ وَحَلَالُهُ، يُشْبِهُ طِلَاءَ الْإِبِلِ، فَمُرْ مَنْ قِبَلِكَ يَتَوَسَّعُوا بِهِ فِي أَشْرِبَتِهِمْ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, wrote to Ammar ibn Yasir, ؓ: "I have been brought a drink from Syria that was cooked until two-thirds of it evaporated in the fire, and one-third remained. Its unlawful part and the intoxicating effect have gone, while its sweetness and lawful part remain, resembling the drink of camels. So instruct those under your authority to use it liberally in their beverages."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Walid ibn Shuraih from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, that he used to drink *al-tila’* mixed half and half.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, who said: “Do not give your children wine to drink or feed it to them. God has not placed your cure in what He has forbidden you. The sin for giving it to them rests only on the one who gives it to them.”

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: “I heard Ibn ʿUmar, ؓ, when Abu Kathir asked him about selling wine. He said: ‘May God condemn the Jews! Fat was forbidden to them, so they refrained from eating it but permitted its sale and consumption of its price. God has forbidden wine; therefore, its sale is forbidden, and consuming its price is forbidden.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما وَسَأَلَهُ أَبُو كَثِيرٍ عَنْ بَيْعِ الْخَمْرِ، فَقَالَ «قَاتَلَ اللَّهُ ⦗ص: 228⦘ الْيَهُودَ، حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّحُومُ فَحَرَّمُوا أَكْلَهَا، وَاسْتَحَلُّوا بَيْعَهَا، وَأَكْلَ ثَمَنِهَا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ الْخَمْرَ، فَحَرَامٌ بَيْعُهَا وَحَرَامٌ أَكْلُ ثَمَنِهَا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Ibn Umar, ؓ, and Abu Kathir asked him about selling wine. He said May God fight the Jews. Fat was made unlawful for them, so they made its consumption unlawful but permitted its sale and consuming its price. Indeed, God has made wine unlawful, so its sale is unlawful, and consuming its price is unlawful.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Amir al-Thaqafi, Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu ʿAmir al-Thaqafi, that he used to give the Prophet, ﷺ, a waterskin of wine each year. records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَامِرٍ الثَّقَفِيِّ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُهْدِي لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كُلَّ عَامٍ رَاوِيَةً مِنْ خَمْرٍ، فَأَهْدَى لَهُ رَاوِيَةً فِي الْعَامِ الَّذِي حُرِّمَتْ فِيهِ الْخَمْرُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ حَرَّمَ الْخَمْرَ، فَلَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِي خَمْرِكَ» ، فَقَالَ: خُذْهَا فَبِعْهَا، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِثَمَنِهَا، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ الَّذِيَ حَرَّمَ شُرْبَهَا، حَرَّمَ بَيْعَهَا، وَأَكْلَ ثَمَنِهَا»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Amir al-Thaqafi, that he used to gift the Prophet, ﷺ, a skin of wine every year. So he gifted him a skin in the year wine was prohibited. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said "God has prohibited wine, so we have no need for your wine." He said: "Take it, sell it, and use its price." The Prophet, ﷺ, said to him: "He who prohibited drinking it has also prohibited its sale and consuming its price."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Ali ibn Abi Talib, ؓ, that he drank while standing.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, sent out an army and granted them victory. As they returned and neared Medina, ʿUmar went out with the people to welcome them. When they heard he was coming, they put on the silk and brocade they had brought. Seeing them, he grew angry and said: “Take off the garments of the people of the Fire.” They did so and apologized: “We wore them to show you the spoils God granted us.” ʿUmar’s anger subsided, and he then allowed a decorative strip [of silk] two, three, or four fingers wide.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه بَعَثَ جَيْشًا فَفُتِحَ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَأَقْبَلُوا فَلَمَّا دَنَوْا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ خَرَجَ عُمَرُ رضي الله عنه يَسْتَقْبِلُهُمْ بِالنَّاسِ، فَلَمَّا بَلَغَهُمْ خُرُوجُ عُمَرَ بِالنَّاسِ إِلَيْهِمْ، لَبِسُوا مَا مَعَهُمْ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ وَالدِّيبَاجِ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ غَضِبَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ «أَلْقُوا ثِيَابَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عَنْكُمْ» ، فَأَلْقَوْهَا وَاعْتَذَرُوا إِلَيْهِ، وَقَالُوا: لَبِسْنَاهَا لِنُرِيَكَ فَيْءَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي فَاءَ عَلَيْنَا، قَالَ فَسُرِّيَ عَنْ عُمَرَ، قَالَ: «ثُمَّ رَخَّصَ فِي الْعَلَمِ مِثْلَ الْإِصْبَعَيْنِ وَالثَّلَاثِ وَالْأَرْبَعِ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, sent an army, and they were granted victory. They returned, and when they neared Medina, Umar, ؓ, went out with the people to receive them. When the army learned that Umar had come out with the people to meet them, they put on the silk and brocade they had with them. When Umar saw them, he became angry and said "Remove the garments of the people of the Fire from yourselves." So they removed them and apologized to him, saying: "We wore them to show you the spoils God has bestowed upon us." Umar’s anger then subsided, and he said: "Then he permitted a stripe the size of two, three, or four fingers."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Sulayman Abu Abdillah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said Hudhayfah was absent for a time, then he returned to find his daughters and sons dressed in silk shirts. He removed them from the males but left them on the females.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، قَالَ «غَابَ حُذَيْفَةُ رضي الله عنه غِيبَةً، ثُمَّ قَدِمَ وَقَدْ كُسِيَ بَنَاتُهُ وَبَنُوهُ قُمُصَ حَرِيرٍ، فَنَزَعَهَا عَنِ الذُّكُورِ وَتَرَكَهَا عَلَى الْإِنَاثِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Farwah, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah, ؓ, Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Farwah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah, ؓ, who said: “We stayed with Hudhayfah in al-Madaʾin, at the home of a local landowner. He brought them food, and they ate. Hudhayfah then asked for a drink, which was brought in a silver vessel. He flung it back at him and said: ‘Last year I stayed with him. He brought us food, and when I asked for his drink, he brought it in a silver vessel. I told him that the Prophet, ﷺ, forbade us to drink from or eat from gold and silver vessels, and to wear silk and brocade. He said: “They are for the polytheists in this world and for you in the Hereafter.”’”
records.text_ar: 1016 - قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي فَرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ رضي الله عنه أَنَّهُ قَالَ نَزَلْنَا مَعَ حُذَيْفَةَ بِالْمَدَائِنِ عَلَى دِهْقَانٍ فَأَتَاهُمْ بِطَعَامِهِ، فَأَكَلُوا، ثُمَّ دَعَا حُذَيْفَةُ بِشَرَابٍ فَأُتِيَ بِهِ فِي إِنَاءِ فِضَّةٍ، فَرَمَى بِهِ وَجْهَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: إِنِّي نَزَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ الْعَامَ الْمَاضِي، فَأَتَانَا بِطَعَامِهِ، ثُمَّ دَعَوْتُ بِشَرَابِهِ فَأَتَانَا بِهِ فِي إِنَاءِ فِضَّةٍ، فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَانَا أَنْ نَشْرَبَ فِي آنِيَةِ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ، وَأَنْ نَأْكُلَ فِيهَا، وَأَنْ نَلْبَسَ الْحَرِيرَ وَالدِّيبَاجَ، وَقَالَ: «هِيَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَلَكُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ»

records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Abu Farwah, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah, ؓ, who said We stayed with Hudhayfah in al-Mada’in at a landowner’s place. He brought them his food, and they ate. Then Hudhayfah asked for a drink, and it was brought to him in a silver vessel. He threw it at his face and said, "Last year I stayed with him, and he brought us his food. Then I asked for his drink, and he brought it to us in a silver vessel. I informed him that the Prophet, ﷺ, forbade us from drinking in vessels of gold and silver, eating in them, and wearing silk and brocade. He said, 'These are for the polytheists in this world, and for you in the Hereafter.'" Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Mujahid, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah, ؓ, with the same narration.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from a man of the people of Egypt, who said One day the Messenger of God, ﷺ, came out holding silk in one hand and gold in the other, and he said: "These two are forbidden for the males of my community, but permissible for their females."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that he would marry off his daughters for a dowry of one thousand dinars, out of which he would adorn them with jewelry worth four hundred dinars, and he would adorn his daughters with gold.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّهُ «كَانَ يُزَوِّجُ بَنَاتَهُ عَلَى أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ يُحَلِّيهِنَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بِأَرْبَعِمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ، وَكَانَ يُحَلِّي بَنَاتَهُ الذَّهَبَ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, who said: “It has reached me that ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, ʿImran ibn Husayn, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Hurayrah, Anas ibn Malik, Husayn ibn ʿAli, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Shurayh used to wear khazz (a fine fabric, often silk-and-wool blend).”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ بَلَغَنِي عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ، وَعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ، وَعِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَوْفَى، وَأَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، وَأَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ وَحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، وَابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، وَشُرَيْحٍ رضي الله عنهم «أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَلْبَسُونَ الْخَزَّ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، قَالَ بَلَغَنِي عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ، وَعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ، وَعِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَوْفَى، وَأَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، وَأَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ وَحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، وَابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، وَشُرَيْحٍ رضي الله عنهم «أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَلْبَسُونَ الْخَزَّ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated to us from his father from Abu Hanifah, who said It reached me from Uthman ibn Affan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Imran ibn Husayn, Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Hurayrah, Anas ibn Malik, Husayn ibn Ali, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Shurayh, ؓ, that they used to wear silk brocade.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he used to wear clothes dyed with safflower.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad who said Ibrahim used to go out and lead us in prayer wearing a deep red wrap.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that the engraving on his ring was: "God is the Protector of Ibrahim and his Helper," made of iron.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muntashir, from his father, from Masruq, that the inscription on his ring was: “In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.”

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham, that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, ؓ, each wore a gold ring; one of the two rings had an image of two lionesses on its bezel.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، «أَنَّ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ عَوْفٍ، وَالْبَرَاءَ بْنَ عَازِبٍ رضي الله عنهم كَانَا يَلْبَسَانِ خَاتَمَيْنِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ فِي فَصِّ أَحَدِهِمَا صُورَةُ لَبْوَتَيْنِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: ثنا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنِ الْهَيْثَمِ، «أَنَّ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ عَوْفٍ، وَالْبَرَاءَ بْنَ عَازِبٍ رضي الله عنهم كَانَا يَلْبَسَانِ خَاتَمَيْنِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ فِي فَصِّ أَحَدِهِمَا صُورَةُ لَبْوَتَيْنِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from al-Haytham that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and al-Bara ibn Azib, ؓ, used to wear two gold rings, each with the engraving of two lionesses on one of their bezels.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Husayn from Mujahid from Ibn Umar, ؓ, that the engraving on his ring was: "Abdullah ibn Umar."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حُصَيْنٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما، أَنَّهُ " كَانَ نَقْشُ خَاتَمِهِ: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ "

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: “The purification of every hide is its tanning.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه: «ذَكَاةُ كُلِّ مَسْكٍ دِبَاغُهُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه: «ذَكَاةُ كُلِّ مَسْكٍ دِبَاغُهُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said "The slaughter of every musk is its tanning."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه: «ذَكَاةُ كُلِّ مَسْكٍ دِبَاغُهُ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: “The purification of every hide is its tanning.”

records.matn_ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رضي الله عنه: «ذَكَاةُ كُلِّ مَسْكٍ دِبَاغُهُ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim,
records.matn_en: who said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ؓ, said: “The purification of every hide is its tanning.”
records.boundary_review_note: Ibrahim transmits the statement attributed to Umar.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said Whatever you use to treat the hide that prevents it from decay is tanning for it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَا أَصْلَحْتَ بِهِ الْجِلْدَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يَمْنَعُهُ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ فَهُوَ لَهُ دِبَاغٌ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: “The tanning of every hide is its purification.”

records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «ذَكَاةُ كُلِّ جَلْدٍ دِبَاغُهُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said "The slaughter of every hide is its tanning."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father from Abu Hanifah from Uthman ibn Abdillah ibn Mawhab who said Umm Salamah, ؓ, brought out for us a small bundle of the hair of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, dyed with henna and katam.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: “I saw the head and beard of al-Husayn ibn ʿAli, ؓ, dyed with wasmah, and the dye had faded.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ «أَبْصَرْتُ رَأْسَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ رضي الله عنهما وَلِحْيَتَهُ مَخْضُوبَتَيْنِ بِالْوَسْمَةِ وَقَدْ نَصَلَا»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim who said He was asked about dyeing with *wasmah*, so he said, "It is a good herb."

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Yazid al-Rishk from Anas ibn Malik, ؓ, who said I saw Abu Bakr, and his beard seemed like the flame of *‘arfaj*, meaning it glistened.

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, and Abu Hanifah said: “I saw Musa ibn Talhah with his beard dyed with wasmah (a plant dye).

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Ḥujayyah, from Ibn Buraydah, from Abu al-Aswad, from Abu Dharr, ؓ, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said, "The best things with which you may change gray hair are henna and katam."

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, and Abu Hanifah said "I saw 'Amir with his beard dyed with henna, and I saw him wearing a red cloak."

records.matn_ar: رَأَيْتُ عَامِرًا مَخْضُوبُ اللِّحْيَةِ بِالْحِنَّاءِ، وَرَأَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ مِلْحَفَةً حَمْرَاءَ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, and Abu Hanifah said "
records.matn_en: I saw 'Amir with his beard dyed with henna, and I saw him wearing a red cloak."
records.boundary_review_note: This is Abu Hanifah’s first-person observation about Amir.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from al-Haytham from Abu Quhafah, ؓ, that he was brought to the Prophet, ﷺ, while his beard had grown long and spread out. The Prophet said , "If you would trim," and he gestured with his hand toward the sides of his beard.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim that he said There is no harm in a man trimming his beard, so long as he does not imitate the people of polytheism.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said regarding the moustache: “What is disapproved of it is only resembling the unbelievers; apart from that, there is no harm in it.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي الشَّارِبَيْنِ: «إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ مِنْهُ التَّشَبُّهُ بِأَهْلِ الْكُفْرِ، فَأَمَّا مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, ؓ, that he underwent cauterization, sought a charm (ruqyah) for a venomous bite or sting, and used to trim his beard.

records.matn_en: h, that he underwent cauterization, sought a charm (ruqyah) for a venomous bite or sting, and used to trim his beard.
records.boundary_review_note: The account attributes both practices to Ibn Umar.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Najih, from Abdullah ibn Umar, ؓ, that Asma bint Umays, ؓ, said to the Prophet, ﷺ: "Shall I not seek ruqyah for your nephew from the evil eye?" He said: "Yes, for if anything were to precede destiny, the evil eye would precede it."
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي نَجِيحٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رضي الله عنهما أَنَّ أَسْمَاءَ ابْنَةَ عُمَيْسٍ رضي الله عنها قَالَتْ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم: أَلَا أَسْتَرْقِي لِابْنِ أَخِيكَ مِنَ الْعَيْنِ؟ قَالَ: «بَلَى، فَلَوْ أَنَّ شَيْئًا سَبَقَ الْقَدَرَ لَسَبَقَتْهُ الْعَيْنُ»

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ؓ, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said God has not sent down any disease except that He has also sent down its cure, except for death and old age. So take to the milk of cows, for it is a mixture from every tree.
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ طَارِقِ بْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رضي الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «مَا وَضَعَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلَّا وَضَعَ لَهُ دَوَاءً، إِلَّا السَّامَ وَالْهَرَمَ، فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِأَلْبَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَإِنَّهَا تُخْلَطُ مِنْ كُلِّ الشَّجَرِ»

records.text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from ʿAʾishah, ؓ, that a woman asked her about plucking facial hair. She replied: “Remove the unwanted hair from your face.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها أَنَّهَا سَأَلَتْهَا امْرَأَةٌ عَنِ الْحَفِّ؟ فَقَالَتْ «أَمِيطِي الْأَذَى عَنْ وَجْهِكِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها أَنَّهَا سَأَلَتْهَا امْرَأَةٌ عَنِ الْحَفِّ؟ فَقَالَتْ «أَمِيطِي الْأَذَى عَنْ وَجْهِكِ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Aisha, ؓ, that a woman asked her about trimming the edges of the head. She said "Remove the harm from your face."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رضي الله عنها أَنَّهَا سَأَلَتْهَا امْرَأَةٌ عَنِ الْحَفِّ؟ فَقَالَتْ «أَمِيطِي الْأَذَى عَنْ وَجْهِكِ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from ʿAʾishah, ؓ, that a woman asked her about plucking facial hair. She replied: “Remove the unwanted hair from your face.”

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهَا سَأَلَتْهَا امْرَأَةٌ عَنِ الْحَفِّ؟ فَقَالَتْ «أَمِيطِي الْأَذَى عَنْ وَجْهِكِ»
records.isnad_en: Yusuf narrated from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Aisha, ؓ,
records.matn_en: r, that a woman asked her about plucking facial hair. She replied: “Remove the unwanted hair from your face.”
records.boundary_review_note: A woman asks Aisha about trimming; the woman is unnamed and remains part of the matn.

records.text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: “God has cursed the woman who attaches hair extensions and the woman who has them attached; the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed; the woman who files her teeth and the woman who has them filed; the woman who marks herself and the woman who has herself marked; the one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, its witnesses and its recorder; and the one who makes a woman lawful for her former husband [through an intervening marriage], and the man for whose sake this is done.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْوَاصِلَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِلَةَ، وَالْوَاشِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِمَةَ، وَالْوَاشِرَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِرَةَ، وَالْوَاصِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِمَةَ، وَآكِلَ الرِّبَا، وَمُطْعِمَهُ، وَشَاهِدَهُ، وَكَاتِبَهُ، وَالْمُحَلِّلَ، وَالْمُحَلَّلَ لَهُ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْوَاصِلَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِلَةَ، وَالْوَاشِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِمَةَ، وَالْوَاشِرَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِرَةَ، وَالْوَاصِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِمَةَ، وَآكِلَ الرِّبَا، وَمُطْعِمَهُ، وَشَاهِدَهُ، وَكَاتِبَهُ، وَالْمُحَلِّلَ، وَالْمُحَلَّلَ لَهُ»
records.raw_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father from Abu Hanifah from Hammad from Ibrahim from the Prophet, ﷺ, that he said "God has cursed the woman who adds hair extensions, the one who asks for them to be added, the woman who tattoos, the one who asks to be tattooed, the woman who plucks facial hair, the one who asks for it to be plucked, the woman who brands her face, the one who asks for it to be branded, the one who consumes usury, the one who feeds it, its witness, its scribe, the one who facilitates a temporary marriage, and the one for whom it is facilitated."
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ «لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْوَاصِلَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِلَةَ، وَالْوَاشِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِمَةَ، وَالْوَاشِرَةَ، وَالْمُوتَشِرَةَ، وَالْوَاصِمَةَ، وَالْمُوتَصِمَةَ، وَآكِلَ الرِّبَا، وَمُطْعِمَهُ، وَشَاهِدَهُ، وَكَاتِبَهُ، وَالْمُحَلِّلَ، وَالْمُحَلَّلَ لَهُ»
records.display_text_en: Yusuf reported from his father, from Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from the Prophet, ﷺ, who said: “God has cursed the woman who attaches hair extensions and the woman who has them attached; the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed; the woman who files her teeth and the woman who has them filed; the woman who marks herself and the woman who has herself marked; the one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, its witnesses and its recorder; and the one who makes a woman lawful for her former husband [through an intervening marriage], and the man for whose sake this is done.”
